The ordinance chronology DHCD compiled in September 1978, with the City Solicitor's 1977 title inquiry, gives the lot's whole history. Ordinance 567 (Oct. 22, 1956, Mayor D'Alesandro) let the City take 3207-3219 Barclay St for parking; Ordinance 502 (Nov. 25, 1960) sold the 32nd-and-Brentwood parcel, which the merchants leased and then bought (Waverly Merchants Parking Lot, Inc.). In 1972 Ordinances 382/383 and 528 closed and sold a 10-ft alley. In May 1974 Ordinances 1279/1280, 1306 and 1313 closed Brentwood Ave between Merryman's Lane and 32nd and sold its bed to Luck Dome, Inc. for a twelve-story hotel, office and apartment building with a garage and health club; Ordinance 1640 made Brentwood revert if nothing was built in two years. The merchants had sold the lot to Luck Dome (confirmatory deed Liber RHB 3002 f.371) and leased spaces back. Luck Dome mortgaged it to Fidelity Mortgage Investors, went bankrupt, and Fidelity took title by foreclosure on June 10, 1975 (Liber RHB 3239 f.672), with a large deficiency decree (Circuit Court No. 2, Equity 22510-C). Nothing was ever built. City Archives BRG48-43-10-22, pages 0055-0058, 0061-0062, 0109-0110, 0118-0120, 0163, 0174-0175.

A 99-year lease dated March 9, 1973 (recorded March 20, Liber RHB 3002 f.373) from Luck Dome, Inc. (Simantovs Capon, c/o A. D. Gomborov) to Waverpark, Inc., the merchants' new vehicle (officers Alvin Miller and Harry Orman): 100 parking spaces at $5,000 a year, 30 daily and 70 hourly, with tiered free time (four hours for beauty-parlor customers, three for theatre customers, two for everyone else) and signs reading "Reserved for guests of Waverly Merchants." Exhibit 1 describes 3201-3221 Barclay St (25,891 sq ft) plus 415 Merryman's Lane, Block 3881-A. Paragraph 11 bound the site to an office building, motel or hotel and barred competing shops; an October 1973 modification pushed Luck Dome's garage deadline to Dec. 31, 1975. The copy is stamped as a complainant's exhibit, so it came out of the 1975 lawsuits. City Archives BRG48-43-10-22, pages 0141-0151.

Assistant City Solicitor Kenneth E. Lee asked Lowell R. Bowen of Miles & Stockbridge for the lease, deed, mortgage and any court cases (April 28, 1977). Bowen's May 13 reply laid out the chain (merchants to Luck Dome to Fidelity foreclosure) and three pending cases: Title Guarantee v. Waverpark, Luck Dome and Fidelity (filed June 9, 1975, No. 45288A); Betts et al., Fidelity's trustees, v. Title Guarantee (D. Md. B-75-905, July 7, 1975); and Fidelity's own bankruptcy (S.D.N.Y. 75-B-154), with settlement expected by June 15, 1977. Bowen believed Waverpark would surrender its lease to the City for $5,000. Paul Gilbert meanwhile asked Land Development (April 18) to appraise the lot for metered City parking, measuring it at about 21,250 sq ft; a Sept. 16 memo put it at 41,500 sq ft plus a 2,370 sq ft alley, with only a deteriorating attendant's booth on it. City Archives BRG48-43-10-22, pages 0091, 0109-0110, 0116-0122, 0174-0175, 0206.

The Appraisal Committee valued Block 3881-A lots 16 and 23 at $30,000 and lots 1-12 at $100,000 (Jan. 30, 1978; appraiser William Miley). Commissioner M. J. Brodie ordered Real Estate Officer Jerome Goldfein to acquire the lot from Fidelity Mortgage Investors (Howard Watts; attorney Ken Singer) on Feb. 28, 1978: cap $130,000, about $135,000 in fee, Off-Street Parking account 9964-577-005, lots 17-18 (417-419 Merryman) unwanted but possibly forced in; Waverpark had agreed in writing to surrender its lease. Routing slips show the draft stalled three weeks until Bob Schaffner of the Off-Street Parking Commission talked to Gilbert. The City's option of March 23, 1978 was mailed to Lifetime Communities (Fidelity's successor) and never returned. Gilbert's June 5 memo said the whole project fit the $200,000 allocated in 1977 and listed the supporters: Greater Homewood, Oakenshawe, Abell, Waverly and Charles Village associations, and merchants George Bluso (Mr. Nifty), Bob Moore (Gorsuch House), Alan Orman (Harry's Liquors), Stanley Adler and Alvin Miller (Princess Shops). A Feb. 6 estimate priced the rehab at about $44,000-$55,000: resurfacing $16,000, 15 lights $13,000, 50 trees $15,000, a screening wall $45,000 or a hedge $2,250. City Archives BRG48-43-10-22, pages 0090, 0124-0126, 0134-0139, 0158, 0163, 0170.

With the option unsigned, the Off-Street Parking Commission first raised condemnation on June 19, 1978 (Schaffner's status report); Brodie wrote "Give me details!" Pat Massey's July 14 briefing: the City had been buying from Fidelity at $130,000 since fall 1977, Fidelity went into receivership and Lifetime Communities took possession and sat on the option; improvements were estimated at $70,000; Bernard Klein, who managed the lot outside the merchants' Waverpark lease, proposed a Sambo's fast-food restaurant on part of it and threatened a taxpayer's suit. Brodie: "A wonderful mess, but keep pushing!" Bill Hoffman drafted a condemnation ordinance dated Aug. 4, 1978 for everything bounded by Barclay, Merryman's Lane, Brentwood and E. 32nd, modeled on a 1977 Frankford park-site ordinance; it was introduced in Council by Aug. 10 with hearings in late September, Mary Pat Clarke strongly for it. Terry J. Phillips told Clarke (July 31) that small businesses stored trucks on the lot and Union Memorial employees parked there, yet it hardly filled. On Sept. 25 Massey met Schaffner with a list of open questions (what the City and the developer had paid, lots 16-18, the alley closing, repeal of the hotel ordinance, who owned Brentwood Avenue, whether Fidelity knew about condemnation), and on Oct. 20 Goldfein formally told Lifetime's attorney that a condemnation ordinance was proposed. City Archives BRG48-43-10-22, pages 0033, 0035-0036, 0049-0053, 0060, 0063-0070.

Mrs. Sallie Sanders of 1116 York road was probably fatally burned about 1 PM on July 7, 1904 when a gasoline stove exploded at her mother Mrs. Thomas Dowary's home, 103 Reese street, Waverly. Neighbor Henry Kistler of 203 Brady avenue rolled her in the mud to put out the flames. Dr. W. J. Pillsbury, 2801 Greenmount avenue, and Dr. H. F. Cooper, 324 East Twenty-fifth street, treated her at the house. Husband William Sanders said frequent fatal gasoline fires in Waverly had kept him from owning such a stove. Alarm from box 744 by M. Robert Kurtz; No. 7 truck stuck two hours in the mud. A second gasoline fire the same day at 425 West Twenty-third street (George Burch). The fire story behind the held death notice (768:372049501). Her husband said Waverly's frequent gasoline-stove fires had kept him from owning one. 2801 Greenmount was Dr. Pillsbury's office.

Editorial. The white Harlem Avenue Christian Church membership is deciding whether to sell its building at Harlem and Fremont avenues to colored Seventh Day Adventists; white churches and residents oppose a colored congregation owning the corner, with the final meeting next Monday. Meanwhile in the Waverly section, where colored people have long lived and built churches, white community associations are asking colored people, by word of mouth and in long letters to neighborhood leaders, to give up their homes and churches and move to the northwest section of Baltimore because more whites are moving to the suburbs. The paper's advice: behave the best we know how and let the neighbors move when they don't like us. George W. Biddle, Baltimore's oldest public school teacher, retired on pension after 52 years (37 in Baltimore City schools); honored Thursday at School 118's Community House and Friday by the Principals' Association with a gold watch. Born in South Baltimore 72 years ago, he taught first in Carroll County at age 20, then Kent County, then Baltimore County and Waverly, and entered the city system when Waverly was incorporated into Baltimore. He was the city's first colored principal, when School No. 9 on Carrollton Avenue was turned over to colored people, and has been principal of the Argyle Avenue school for 12 years. Nearly every city principal once served on his faculty; he calls Miss Fannie Barbour the best teacher in the city. The segregated school on this block (School No. 115 in Belco's history) had a teacher of note; the 1938 eulogy repeats it.

George B. Murphy Sr.'s remarks at the funeral of George W. Biddle, Baltimore's first colored school principal. Next year marks 50 years since the first colored high school class (nine women, two men) graduated; City Council had made graduates with an 85 average eligible to teach without exam, and a 12-room school was built at Riggs and Carrollton avenues for colored teachers. Seven of the first class qualified; Biddle, then teaching in the Waverly school, was brought into the city system by the 1888 Annexation Act, which also brought Miss Roberta Sheridan, Mrs. Mary J. Camper and Miss Nannie B. Groomes. Biddle became principal of the boys' department at No. 9 and Fannie Barbour of the girls'; school board president John T. Morris called the experiment a success. Adjacent story: Mrs. Violet Hill Whyte, Baltimore's only colored policewoman, completes her first year in the Northwestern district.

About 2 a.m. on Sunday May 16, 1858 an alarm of fire was raised for St. John's Episcopal church at the first toll-gate on the York road; the church was entirely destroyed except its stone walls, which were still good. Only the Independent fire company went all the way out and it protected the parsonage. A neighbor woke to the smoke and ran to save the sacramental vessels, but they had already been stolen and the door left open. The church was only two or three years old with a large congregation; damage about $2,500, insured for $1,700 with the Baltimore County Mutual Society. No fire had been lit since the previous Thursday, so arson was assumed. Damage about $2,500, insured for $1,700; only the Independent company came out and saved the parsonage.

Between 1 and 2 a.m. on May 16, 1858, St. John's Episcopal Church (Rev. George F. Adams, pastor), 'situated on the York turnpike, near the first toll-gate, about a mile beyond the city limits', burned to its walls. Built about ten years earlier in plain Gothic style of dark granite, it was insured for only $1,700; the church was believed robbed of valuables before being fired. Few fire companies went beyond Greenmount Cemetery; only the Independent Company reached the scene.

The Vestry of St. John's Church, Huntingdon, offers $200 for the arrest and conviction of anyone concerned in the burning of the church near the first turnpike gate on the York road on Sunday May 16 at about 2 a.m. Ad marked m19-4t (to run four times).

Planning's 1976 parking study is the fullest picture of the lot before the City took it. Facility #1041 at Barclay and 32nd, 132 spaces (112 adjusted), was meant to be free with a member merchant's stamp and 50 cents an hour otherwise, but was unattended, enforcement was irregular, and about 15 spaces were leased monthly at $15-$25. At the Friday Feb. 20, 1976 peak it held 55 cars (42%); turnover was 0.8 a day against 4.0-7.6 at the Greenmount meters; Figure 6 shows a block of roughly 40 all-day parkers filling it, and 45 of its 55 peak users were long-term. Drivers on Greenmount could not tell it existed, and from 33rd the only way in was one-way Merrymans Lane heading the wrong way. Recommendations: redesign for access and flow, then signing, cap long-term use at half the lot, add about five meters on Venable between Barclay and Greenmount, pave the Hardware Fair/Baltimore Dictating Machine lot and landscape Eddie's. 'New parking supply as such is not warranted.' Three years later the City condemned the lot to build one anyway. City Archives BRG48-43-10-21, pages 0023-0030, 0037, 0040-0041.

The paper trail of the first attempt to take the block by law. Chief Solicitor William Hoffman sent Mayor Schaefer and Council President Orlinsky the draft on Aug. 4, 1978: its purpose was 'to guarantee issuer that the Waverly Parking Lot will continue to be used as a parking lot,' because an outstanding lease would let the lessor turn it commercial. Introduced Aug. 8 as City Council Bill 1887 (Orlinsky, by request of the Department of Law): acquire by purchase or condemnation, for off-street parking, every interest in the lots bounded by Barclay St, Merryman Lane, Brentwood Ave and E 32nd St, the Off-Street Parking Commission to negotiate and the City Solicitor to condemn under Title XII if no price is agreed. Robert T. Schaffner of the Commission told the Council on Sept. 25 that the bill was introduced at the request of DHCD's Commercial Revitalization office 'to preserve the use of said property for public parking use.' Inside DHCD the report went two ways: R. N. Caasi's Sept. 22 draft, which wrongly said the site 'is not within the boundaries of this Department's community development areas' but urged approval, was struck through, and Pat Massey's rewrite signed by Brodie on Oct. 20 approved the acquisition in principle but recommended the Council withdraw 1887 in favor of the Waverly urban renewal ordinance, due mid-November, which would carry the same power. Two Bureau of Plans & Surveys plats of Block 3881-A came with the file, one marking 'Sites #3 + 3A (3A = lots 1 & 13)', the other outlining the whole triangle and noting the 10-ft alley closed by Ordinance 162 of July 5, 1972. The opposition to the City taking the lot, in its own words. Bernard Klein (Buckingham Arms Apartments, 3706 N. Charles), who operated the lot, gathered a petition of residents, merchants, Union Memorial Hospital nurses and area employees against Bill 1887: meters would be costly, the lot was available now with free validated parking for customers, employees parked cheaply, and the City would lose the parking-license revenue; 'Dan' (Mendelson) forwarded it to Massey with the note that its 572 signatures included 'some of questionable legitimacy.' A yellow handbill called a special meeting for Tuesday, May 8, 1979, 7:30 PM at Waverly Presbyterian, 34th and Old York Road, 'to object to City acquiring parking lot to install meters.' At the CC 2278 hearing that night many speakers made those arguments. DHCD's counter-evidence was a handwritten staff survey: 140-170 spaces, $11 a month, 50 cents the first hour for non-customers, at least half the cars repeaters and many of them Union Memorial employees, three garages (Perry's Auto, Brentwood Auto) storing repair cars, unlicensed cars and trucks, haphazard parking with no lines, a booth staffed 9-5 with lapses, full only on Orioles opening day and Colt games, 'I've never had to turn a shopper away'; conclusion, good for the hospital, secondary for shoppers, 'a physical blight to the neighborhood. Not to mention a speculative property for B. Klein and friends.' City Archives BRG48-43-10-21, pages 0054, 0071-0072, 0089-0091.

The March 22, 1976 steering committee asked the City to check the ownership and title of the 'ugly' merchants' lot. A 2003 mortgage on 3040 Greenmount describes the lot by pointing back to a deed from Mary S. Ruppersberger and others to George E. Zepp, dated October 15, 1937 and recorded in Liber SCL 5767, folio 252 (the 2003 typist spelled it 'Zapp'). George E. Zepp is the son who ran Geo. E. Zepp & Co., films, beside his father Simon's photo supply business, which had been at this address since about 1913. So this is the family business buying its own building after roughly 24 years there. The Ruppersbergers held 3036-3038 next door until 1975, so they probably owned this whole stretch of the west side. The lot is 56 feet 1 inch on Greenmount and 155 feet 3 inches deep, starting 112 feet 1 inch north of Vineyard Lane (formerly Gilmore Lane), with a half share of the ten-foot alley behind. Its north line is land that Thomas J. Wilson and other trustees leased to B.M. Cook (Liber BHA 67, folio 100). The 1937 deed itself has not been pulled; it is the next document to order.

Deed of trust dated September 11, 2003 and recorded December 2, 2003 (Liber FMC 4681, folios 90-97). Monica Ann Brown borrowed $147,382.75 from Wachovia Bank, due October 10, 2023. The trustee was Elizabeth Zajic of First American Title. It recites how she took title: a deed dated July 27, 1998 and recorded December 17, 1998 in Liber FMC 7977, folio 302. That is the deed the state's sales data lists as the seller's deed on the March 2013 sale. Page 7 carries the full legal description, which reaches back to the 1937 Ruppersberger-to-Zepp deed.

Certificate of release dated August 8, 2013 and recorded September 4, 2013 (Liber FMC 15590, folios 334-335). Wells Fargo, as successor by merger to Wachovia, released Monica Ann Brown's 2003 deed of trust. It was signed by Serena Wilson Moore, vice president, and notarized by Amy Deskins in Roanoke, Virginia. The release came in the same months the property changed hands twice: out of Brown's name in March 2013 for $110,320, then to 3040 Greenmount LLC for $190,000.

Certificate of satisfaction dated August 15, 2014 and recorded October 1, 2014 (Liber FMC 16590, folios 157-158). Presidential Bank (Sharon McGinley, vice president) released the purchase-money deed of trust that 3040 Greenmount LLC gave on August 29, 2013 (Liber 15581, folio 34), and the assignment of leases and rents (Liber 15581, folio 79). The assignment of rents shows the LLC bought it as a rental building. The payoff came the day after the LLC refinanced with Blueridge Bank.

Certificate of satisfaction dated June 17, 2024 and recorded June 18, 2024 (Liber 26978, folio 287). Sandy Spring Bank, as successor to Blueridge Bank (William Byrd), released the deed of trust 3040 Greenmount LLC gave on August 14, 2014 (Liber 16475, folio 31) and its assignment of leases (Liber 16475, folio 74). The property is described as 3040 and 3044 Greenmount, Block 3856: one lot with two street numbers, the old Zepp Photo building. Four months later the LLC sold to O & O Realty Inc. for $700,000, so this was clearing the title for that sale.

The 1976 deed recites that Helen M. Bordley conveyed the lot to George E. Zepp and his wife Matilda G. Zepp by a deed dated June 23, 1944 (Liber M.L.P. 6612, folio 428). George had bought it alone from the Ruppersbergers in 1937, so this was most likely a pass-through deed to put the couple on title jointly. A deed like that also means the survivor gets the building without probate. Bordley is an old Waverly name: Wm. C. Bordley held a York Road lot in the 1876 Hopkins atlas, and several Bordleys are buried at St. John's. Whether Helen belonged to that family is not established. The 1944 deed itself has not been pulled.

The 1976 deed states that George E. Zepp died on or about August 2, 1949 (the day is handwritten), which left full title with his widow Matilda G. Zepp. Matilda held 3040-3044 Greenmount for the next 27 years, while the family's business grew into the Zepp Photo Centers chain.

Deed dated April 19, 1976 and recorded April 21, 1976 (Liber R.H.B. 3339, folios 45-46; Title Guarantee Company application H-89636). Matilda G. Zepp sold to Morris Bloom, Leo Bloom and Herman Bloom, partners trading as Bloom Realty. The buildings are described as 3040, 3042 and 3044 Greenmount. This ends 39 years of Zepp ownership. The Blooms made it their base: the city's Waverly owner roster of about 1977 gives Bloom Realty's address as 3042 Greenmount, and Bloom Realty also owned 2920 Greenmount. A city survey photo of about 1977 still shows the Zepp Photo Centers sign, so the camera store probably stayed on as a tenant.

Purchase-money mortgage dated April 19, 1976 and recorded April 21, 1976 (Liber R.H.B. 3339, folios 47-50). The Blooms owed Matilda G. Zepp $30,000, the unpaid balance of the price, at 7 percent. They paid $2,000 every six months from April 15, 1976, with the balance due October 15, 1983. So the widow financed part of her own sale. A margin note on the mortgage points to its release in Liber 128, folio 61.

Short release signed by Matilda G. Zepp on October 13, 1983 and recorded October 26, 1983 (Liber S.E.B. 128, folio 61). It releases the 1976 mortgage from Morris Bloom and partners. The Blooms paid off on schedule, since the balance was due October 15, 1983. Matilda was still alive in October 1983.

The 1998 deed recites a deed dated September 11, 1992 from Howard Alan Bloom to Peter S. and Grace S. Lee (Liber 3366, folio 367). The Lees borrowed from Westview Federal Savings and Loan (Liber 3366, folio 370) and gave Bloom a second, seller-financed deed of trust for the rest (Liber 3366, folio 385). The Blooms held the building 16 years. How it passed from the Bloom Realty partnership to Howard Alan Bloom alone is not yet known. The 1992 deed itself has not been pulled. One of the release papers dates the Westview mortgage to 1993, but the other records all say September 11, 1992.

Certificate of satisfaction dated April 20, 1998 and recorded May 14, 1998 (Liber PMB 7324, folios 290-291). Howard Allan Bloom confirms the Lees' 1992 deed of trust to him (Liber 3366, folio 385) is paid in full. It was returned to Grace S. Lee at 1705 Bywoods Lane, Stevenson. The payoff cleared the way for the Lees' sale to Monica Ann Brown three months later.

Release dated August 3, 1998 (Liber PMB 7597, folios 450-451). Westview Federal Savings and Loan Association (Lisa M. McGuire, vice president) releases the Lees' mortgage of Liber 3366, folio 370, paid in full from the July 1998 sale. The release dates that mortgage September 11, 1993, while the Lees' other papers say 1992.

Deed dated July 27, 1998 and recorded December 17, 1998 (Liber FMC 7977, folios 302-307), prepared by Marci J. Smedley of Yerman & Smedley. The Lees sold to Monica Ann Brown for $148,000. The buildings are 3040, 3042 and 3044 Greenmount. The sellers swore the property was a multi-family dwelling, so tenants had no right of first refusal. That means the upstairs were apartments by 1998.

Deed of trust and absolute assignment of rents dated July 27, 1998 (Liber FMC 7977, folios 308-317). Monica Ann Brown, then of 66-09 Almeda Avenue, Far Rockaway, New York, borrowed $105,000 from First Union National Bank. Title insurance was from Security Title Guarantee Corporation of Baltimore. The rent assignment and her New York address show she bought it as an income property to own from out of town.

Second purchase-money mortgage dated July 27, 1998 and recorded December 17, 1998 (Liber FMC 7977, folios 318-322). Brown owed Peter and Grace Lee, then of 5217 York Road, $30,000 at 10 percent, paid at $637.42 a month from August 1998, with the balance due July 2003. The price was therefore $105,000 from the bank, $30,000 from the sellers and about $13,000 cash. Her $147,383 Wachovia loan came two months after this balloon fell due, and First Union had merged into Wachovia in 2001. That loan was probably the refinance that paid off both.

Limited power of attorney signed April 27, 2006 in St. Lucie County, Florida (Liber FMC 7723, folios 207-209; scanned by the Archives only in May 2026). Monica Brown of 1652 SE Mariner Lane, Port Saint Lucie, named Angie Brown of 3044 Greenmount Avenue her agent to transfer, pledge or mortgage the property. So by 2006 the owner lived in Florida and a relative, or at least someone sharing her surname, lived in the building and handled it.

The 3040-3044 lot runs from 112 feet 1 inch to 168 feet 2 inches north of Vineyard Lane. Its north line is the edge of the Thomas J. Wilson trustees' old lease to B.M. Cook. 3046 Greenmount begins at exactly 168 feet 2 inches, so it sits on that Wilson-Cook leasehold (1984 ground lease, Liber SEB 387, folio 462). Irvin A. Forrest bought 3036-3038 to the south from the Ruppersberger and Magers trustees in 1975 (Liber 3265, folio 573). He bought 3046 to the north from Metropolis Building Association on August 23, 1977 (Liber JFC 3529, folio 425). So from 1977 the Blooms' building at 3040-3044 had the same owner on both sides. The Ruppersbergers had sold the middle lot to the Zepps in 1937 and kept 3036-3038 until 1975. In December 1984 Forrest put 3046 on a new 99-year ground lease at $120 a year and sold the leasehold to Stanford H. Cohan, Albert B. Cowing and partners for $37,500.

Release dated May 16, 1984 and recorded in August 1984 (Liber SEB 273, folio 518). Patapsco Federal Savings and Loan Association (Daniel T. Mulheran, president) released five mortgages Irvin A. Forrest had given it: October 20, 1971 on 704 and 706 Montpelier Street, taken with his partner Charles R. Hyson (RHB 2842/533); July 31, 1975 on 3036 and 3038 Greenmount and 3043 Mathews Street (RHB 3265/576); November 19, 1975 on 3045 and 3050 Mathews (RHB 3293/192); November 15, 1976 on 3049 Frisby Street (RHB 3414/887); and October 24, 1977 on 3200 Avon Avenue (RHB 3553/565). The Greenmount mortgage sits three folios after Forrest's purchase deed from the Ruppersberger and Magers trustees (RHB 3265/573), so it was the purchase loan. The list shows Forrest assembling Waverly houses one or two at a time from 1971 to 1977, each on its own Patapsco loan. With the loans paid off he began selling the buildings and keeping the ground: 3046 in December 1984, 3036-3038 in March 1985.

Recited in the 1990 assignment (SEB 2508/532) and the 1991 mortgage (SEB 2749/468): by a lease dated March 11, 1985 (Liber SEB 465, folio 473) Irvin A. Forrest 'demised and leased' the lot to Darrell K. Carter, Lee Carter and Daniel Allen as tenants in common, renewable forever, at $240 a year payable March 11 and September 11. This is the Baltimore way of selling: the buyers got the buildings, Forrest kept the ground and an income. He had done the same with 3046 three months earlier ($120 a year, December 1984). The buyers borrowed from Golden Prague Building, Loan and Savings Association (mortgage at SEB 465/476, three folios on; released 1993). The lease itself, and so the price, has not been pulled.

Assignment of leasehold dated June 12, 1990 and recorded June 14, 1990 (Liber SEB 2508, folios 532-534), prepared by Rogers, Moore & Rogers, 6 South Calvert Street. Lee Carter and Daniel Allen assigned their interest to Darrell K. Carter for nothing; the grantors certify they are 'conveying over to their brother for no consideration.' Lee signed on May 29 and Daniel on June 11. The description is the old one: a lot on the west side of 'York Turnpike Road (now Greenmount Avenue)' beginning 57 feet north of 'a lane known as Gilmore Lane (now Vineyard Lane)', 56 feet 6 inches on the street and about 155 feet deep, 'saving and excepting' a parcel Gusta Ruppersberger and his wife sold to John Schuman by deed of January 13, 1873 (Baltimore County Liber EHA 79, folio 37). See 3034 for where that parcel probably is. The same day Lee Roy Carter assigned Darrell 5212 St. Charles Avenue (SEB 2508/535).

Second partial purchase-money mortgage dated January 29, 1991 and recorded February 6, 1991 (Liber SEB 2749, folios 467-473). Darrell K. Carter, then of 726 Reservoir Street, borrowed $48,000 from Regal Savings Bank, F.S.B. of Owings Mills at 14.5 percent, $759.78 a month, due February 1, 2001. It paid for part of 938 North Calvert Street, which he bought the same day from Aaron Wolfson trading as Beowulf Realty, and sat behind a mortgage to Virginia Zeller (SEB 57/764). Four leaseholds secured it: 938 N. Calvert ($150 ground rent), 3036-3038 Greenmount ($240), 2442 Callow Avenue (from Howard W. Cohen, 1989; $120) and 5212 St. Charles Avenue (from Lee Roy Carter, 1990; $65). By 1991 Darrell was a small landlord using the equity in one house to buy the next. Prepared by Dackman, Heyman & Dackman (Gordon B. Heyman); Stewart D. Sachs swore to the disbursement for Regal.

Deed dated and recorded May 20, 1993 (Liber SEB 3688, folios 480-481). Darrell K. Carter assigned the leasehold to Brown, Jones, and Pettiford, Inc. for $42,000, subject to the $240 ground rent; the state transfer tax was $210. The clerk's return note on the back reads 'Brown Jones & Pettiford, 3042 Greenmount, Balt Md 21218'. 3040-3044 had belonged to Peter and Grace Lee since September 1992, so the buyer was their tenant next door. Carter's two mortgages came off the same week. Within about 17 months the lot was the Lees' too: Peter S. Lee Realty held it by 1996, and the state's sales data shows a $25,500 sale on October 23, 1994, well under this price.

Short release signed May 24, 1993 by Joseph M. Platek, president of Golden Prague Federal Savings and Loan Association ('formerly Golden Prague Building Loan and Savings Association of Baltimore City'), recorded August 24, 1993 (Liber SEB 3829, folio 309). It releases Darrell K. Carter's mortgage at SEB 465/476, three folios after Forrest's 1985 lease to the Carters (465/473), so it was the purchase loan. The form itself doesn't name the property. It was mailed to Isaac Klein, as was Regal Savings' release that week, so he probably handled the May 1993 sale.

Partial release dated May 28, 1993 and recorded June 11, 1993 (Liber SEB 3722, folios 189-190). Regal Savings Bank, F.S.B. (Faith M. Insley, assistant vice president) released 3036 and 3038 Greenmount from the $48,000 mortgage of January 1991 (SEB 2749/467) and kept its lien on Carter's other houses. Returned to Isaac Klein. Eight days after the sale to Brown, Jones and Pettiford.

Assignment of leases and rents dated July 12, 1996 and recorded July 16, 1996 (Liber SEB 5700, folios 312-318), from the Security Title Guarantee Corporation of Baltimore. Peter S. Lee Realty, Inc. (Peter S. Lee, president) gave Westview Federal Savings and Loan Association a $53,000 deed of trust (trustees Maryjo Pundt and Regina R. Cohen, recorded just before this) and assigned it all rents from '3036-38 Greenmount Avenue', promising to report expected vacancies. So the building was let. Westview Federal was also the Lees' lender on 3040-3044 next door (1992). From late 1994 to July 1998 the Lees held every storefront from 3036 to 3044. How the company bought is not pulled: the state's sales data has a $25,500 sale on October 23, 1994, and names the company's deed as SEB 4534/419 when it sold in 2013.

Recited in every later deed: by an assignment dated April 17, 2013 (Liber FMC 15154, folio 58), Peter S. Lee and Grace Lee, 'Surviving Shareholders and Trustees of Peter S. Lee Realty, Inc.', assigned the leasehold to S & B Developers 2, LLC. That wording means the company had been dissolved or had lost its charter, so its last owners conveyed as trustees. The state's sales data gives $118,000 on April 22, 2013. S & B (Steven Verstandig, authorized person) later split the lot: 3036 sold in 2021, 3038 in 2022. The 2013 deed itself has not been pulled.

Release of indemnity deed of trust dated May 14, 2019 (Liber MB 21139, folios 99-144). Paul W. and Amy S. Nochumowitz had pledged their Baltimore ground rents to Lexington National Bail Services (Ronald A. Frank, president) as collateral for bail bonds, by an indemnity deed of trust dated December 26, 2008 (Liber 11263, folio 329). Its 44-page Exhibit A lists roughly 1,600 ground rents by address, deed and annual rent. Deed dated January 13, 1873 and recorded January 15, 1873 (Baltimore County Liber E.H.A. No. 79, folios 37-38). Gustar Ruppersberger and Mary C. Wilms and others, Trustees," by deed dated January 8, 1873, recorded immediately before this one (729:mdlr-eha79-35-wilms-1873) -- Ruppersberger flipped it five days after taking title, for $2,700 against the $1,700 he had just paid for the whole lot. This confirms, with the primary source rather than only a later recital, the hypothesis this row previously carried as "probable": the frontage (57 to 85 feet 3 inches north of Gilmor/Vineyard Lane) matches the parcel the 1990-91 deeds for 3036-3038 except out of their description, and lines up with 3034 next door. Signed Gustar Ruppensberger and Mary C. Ruppensberger (both by seal); witnessed by Frank Lewis; acknowledged January 13, 1873 before Frank Lewis, J.P., Baltimore County; recorded per Edw. H. Ady, Clerk. That fits the Schumans staying on this lot for generations: George A. Schuman's soft-drink stand here in 1920 and George Shuman's restaurant in 1937.

When Brown, Jones and Pettiford, Inc. bought 3036-3038 next door for $42,000 on May 20, 1993 (SEB 3688/480), the clerk's note for returning the deed reads 'Brown Jones & Pettiford, 3042 Greenmount, Balt Md 21218'. Peter and Grace Lee had owned 3040-3044 since September 1992, so the company was their tenant. By about October 1994 the Lees' company owned 3036-3038 as well, and until July 1998 they held every storefront from 3036 to 3044. Monica Ann Brown, who bought 3040-3044 from the Lees in 1998, then lived in Far Rockaway, New York; whether she is connected to the company is untested (its Maryland charter record would name its officers).

Recited in the 1977 deed (RHB 3529/425): by a lease dated October 10, 1910 (Liber SCL 2613, folio 232) James M. Biggs and his wife leased the lot to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County for 99 years at $72 a year, paid April 1 and October 1. The National Register survey dates the building to about 1910 and the Association had its office here by 1920, so this lease is probably when the savings society put up its own front on Greenmount. The lease itself has not been pulled.

The 1977 deed saves and excepts 'that portion of said lot of ground which by deed dated September 14, 1931 ... in Liber SCL No. 5252 folio 353 was granted and surrendered' by the Waverly Building Association to The Lakeshire Company. 'Surrendered' suggests the Association handed back part of its leasehold, probably at the rear, since the 1977 lot runs only about 65 feet back from Greenmount. Which part, and who The Lakeshire Company was, is open; SCL 5252/353 is the next document to pull.

Recited in the 1977 deed: by a deed dated January 22, 1947 (Liber MLP 7079, folio 61) Amelia E. Joesting, unmarried, conveyed the lot to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County. The Association already held the 1910 leasehold, so buying the ground ended its $72 rent and gave it the whole title. Joesting presumably held the Biggs ground rent by then. The deed has not been pulled.

Deed dated August 23, 1977 and recorded October 5, 1977 (Liber RHB 3529, folios 425-427). Metropolis Building Association (William B. Sawers, Jr., president) conveyed 3046 Greenmount to Irvin A. Forrest in fee simple for a stated $5. The taxes put the price near $14,000: state transfer tax $70 at half a percent, recordation $61.60 at $2.20 per $500. The deed explains the seller: The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County became Waverly Savings and Loan Association, which merged into Metropolis Building Association (merger agreement of March 17, 1975, recorded in Harford County, HDC 968/449). So the Waverly thrift's own building of about 67 years was sold two years after the name disappeared. The lot is 16 feet 2 inches on Greenmount, beginning 168 feet 2 inches north of Vineyard Lane (formerly Gilmor's Lane) and running back 64.88 feet along the brick wall of the building to the north. The deed and Forrest's mortgage were both notarized by Anna M. Ozazewski, who witnessed Patapsco Federal's releases in 1984, so the closing was probably held at Patapsco.

Forrest borrowed $9,800 from Patapsco Federal Savings and Loan Association at 10 percent, $129.52 a month; Francis J. Schuster, vice president, swore to the disbursement, and T. Bayard Williams, Jr. drew it. It is a sixth Patapsco loan on a Forrest property, beside the five (1971-77) listed in the 1984 release on 3038. A clerk's note in the margin records its release on December 20, 1984 (SEB 388/104).

Lease dated December 1, 1984 and recorded December 20, 1984 (Liber SEB 387, folios 462-465). Irvin A. Forrest leased the lot to Cherlan Realty Corporation (Jonathan A. Azrael, president) for 99 years, renewable forever for a $1 fine, at $120 a year paid half-yearly from December 1, 1984. Forrest signed on November 21, 1984 before a Florida notary, so he had moved south by then. Cherlan was the lawyers' company (the papers came from Azrael, Gann and Franz, 401 Washington Avenue, Towson) and held the lease for a minute: its assignment to the real buyers was recorded right after. This is how a Baltimore owner turned a building into a ground rent: lease it to a straw, have the straw sell the leasehold, keep the rent. Forrest did the same to 3036-3038 three months later.

Cowing, and Daniel E. and Mildred Cohan owed Irvin A. Forrest $22,500 at 13 percent, $335.96 a month from January 1985, with the balance due December 31, 1994, and warranted it was a business loan. Deed dated October 27, 1909 and recorded October 29, 1909 (Liber SCL 2537, folios 193-194), for a nominal $1. Matilda W. Sanger, a widow of New Jersey, conveyed to The Waverly Amusement Company two lots on the east side of 'the York Turnpike Road (now called Greenmount Avenue)' south of Gorsuch Avenue. The first lot begins 102 feet 7 inches south of Gorsuch, runs 78 feet 6 1/2 inches along the turnpike and through to the west side of the Old York Road; every later deed of 3211 starts from this description. The second is a 23-foot lot 201 feet south of Gorsuch. Sanger had put neighbouring lots on ground leases between 1889 and 1895 (to John T. Hickman, John N. C. Deal, William J. Fink and Charles W. Kramer), and those reversions came with the sale. The company gave her a $3,000 purchase-money mortgage the same week. This is the founding purchase of the Waverly Theatre, which opened that year.

Mortgage dated October 29, 1909 and recorded the same afternoon (Liber SCL 2537, folios 194-198). The Waverly Amusement Company, incorporated in Maryland in 1909, owed Matilda W. Sanger $3,000 of the price, secured on the two lots she had just sold it and on the reversions in the ground-leased lots next door. The company's president signed it; one page reads his name as George A. Cole and another as George A. Cook, so the spelling is uncertain. John I. Lowe(?) attested as secretary, Thomas G. Hull notarized, and Harry E. Karr was named to sell on default.

Deed of September 20, 1923 (Liber SCL 4082, folio 156). The Crystal Amusement Company (Benjamin Cluster, president) conveyed 3207 and 3209 Greenmount to Leah Schloss, a widow, who took on $12,000 of the $26,000 Mortgage Guarantee Company loan that also covered the theatre at 3211 (SCL 3731/199, 1921). The company reserved a 5-foot strip along the north side of the lot, from about 87 feet back to Old York Road, 'for a means of ingress and egress in and to the moving picture parlor adjoining on the north'. So the theatre's owners split off the storefronts to the south and kept a side passage to the hall. 3207-3209 is now part of the 3203-3209 frontage.

The lots could not yet be released from the Mortgage Guarantee Company loan, which also covered 3211 Greenmount, named as the property adjoining on the north.

(Manpreet Singh, president) owed Williams Realty, LLC $260,000, due by October 7, 2022; trustee David L. Thurston. The lot is 15 feet 6 inches on Greenmount and runs back to Merryman's Lane.

Waiver of priority dated December 16, 1980 and recorded December 18, 1980 (Liber WA 3991, folios 857-860). Robert Spielmann & Associates and Robert Spielmann subordinated their June 1980 mortgage on 3222 Greenmount to a new $6,400 third deed of trust from Ira and Lucille Adler to Richard E. Kramer and Howard E. Mirsky, trustees for Stevenson Associates. The Adlers were stacking small private liens on the building within five years of buying it.

Release signed July 30, 1981 by Richard E. Kramer, trustee, and recorded September 15, 1981 (Liber CWM Jr. 4097, folio 775). It releases Ira and Lucille Adler's deed of trust of December 1980 on 3222 Greenmount, very likely the $6,400 Stevenson Associates loan, repaid in about seven months.

Mortgage dated April 15, 1982 and recorded April 19, 1982 (Liber CWM Jr. 4176, folios 95-98). Ira and Lucille Adler, then of 4 Irving Place, Pikesville, borrowed $10,000 from Morton Feldman, Joel Charkatz and Robert Spielmann of 303 East Fayette Street, at 20 percent interest only, $166.66 a month, with the whole due April 15, 1983. It sat behind the City's $67,000 housing-department loan of 1980. The lenders' lawyer was Louis J. Glick. One clause says $11,000, a slip in the drafting. Released in parts in 1983 and fully in January 1986 (SEB 111/399, 756/518).

Mortgage dated April 22, 1982 and recorded May 28, 1982 (Liber CWM Jr. 4189, folios 741-742). Ira and Lucille Adler pledged 3220 Greenmount to The Equitable Trust Company for a $3,903.05 installment loan, a week after the $10,000 private second mortgage. Released September 1983 (SEB 111/398).

Partial release signed in September 1982 (the notary dated it the impossible 'September 31') and recorded September 22, 1983 (Liber SEB 111, folio 399). Joel Charkatz released his $5,000 share of the April 1982 mortgage from Ira and Lucille Adler; the shares were Feldman $10,000, Charkatz $5,000 and Spielmann about $3,210. It describes 3220 as 21 feet 8 inches on the west side of the York Turnpike, 165 feet north of Merryman's Lane, 100 feet deep to a 3-foot alley.

Release signed September 19, 1983 and recorded September 22, 1983 (Liber SEB 111, folio 398). The Equitable Trust Company (F. Frank Macy, Jr., vice president) released Ira and Lucille Adler's April 1982 mortgage (CWM Jr. 4189/741) as paid. The clerk wrote 3220 Greenmount and block 3882 in the margin.

Deed of trust dated November 15, 1983 and recorded November 22, 1983 (Liber SEB 142, folios 132-137). Ira and Lucille Adler (Lucille signing for Ira under a power of attorney) gave Sequoia Savings and Loan Association of 507 Reisterstown Road a $105,000 deed of trust on 3220 and 3222 Greenmount, due December 1, 1988, with Jerome S. and Sanford R. Cardin as trustees. It was declared a commercial loan. A private loan from Robert Spielmann was paid off the next day. Released in 1987 (SEB 1523/331).

Deed of trust dated August 6, 1984 and recorded August 28, 1984 (Liber SEB 288, folios 202-208). Ira and Lucille Adler borrowed $35,000 more from Sequoia Savings and Loan on 3220 and 3222 Greenmount, due September 1, 1999 and callable after three years; trustees Sanford R. Cardin and Gary W. Bass. It was cross-defaulted with the $105,000 Sequoia loan of 1983 and the City's $67,000 loan of 1980, so by 1984 the two storefronts carried about $207,000 of recorded debt. Title by Nationwide Title Company.

Mortgage dated March 22, 1985 and recorded March 27, 1985 (Liber SEB 472, folios 551-554). Ira and Lucille Adler pledged 3220 and 3222 Greenmount to Thomas Acampora and Samuel W. Goldberg for $31,000, repaid in 52 weekly payments of $685.58 at 15 percent add-on interest, alongside a loan to refinance Suburban Management Company, Inc. Paid off by December 1986 (SEB 1163/250).

Release acknowledged January 2, 1986 and recorded January 8, 1986 (Liber SEB 756, folios 518-519). Morton Feldman, Joel Charkatz and Robert Spielmann released Ira and Lucille Adler's April 1982 mortgage on 3220 Greenmount (CWM Jr. 4176/95). It was returned to Jeanne M. Ripley, the Adlers' lawyer on later deals. The next day the Adlers pledged 3220 and 3222 to guarantee the Baker Block loan (SEB 759/500), so this cleared the way.

Release dated December 20, 1986 and recorded February 3, 1987 (Liber SEB 1163, folios 250-251). Thomas Acampora and Samuel W. Goldberg released Ira and Lucille Adler's March 1985 mortgage on 3220 and 3222 Greenmount (SEB 472/551). Notarized by Jeanne M. Ripley; prepared by David S. Goldberg. It came as the Adlers sold 3220 to Jin Wook Kang.

Short release signed February 2, 1987 by F. Ripley Bowman, managing officer of Sequoia Savings & Loan, and recorded November 23, 1987 (Liber SEB 1523, folio 331). It releases the Adlers' $105,000 deed of trust of 1983 (SEB 142/132; trustee Jerome S. Cardin) on 3220 and 3222 Greenmount.

Mortgage dated September 13, 1989 and recorded September 25, 1989 (Liber SEB 2234, folios 88-89). Ira and Lucille Adler pledged 3222 Greenmount to Albert G. Aaron of 416 North Charles Street for $50,000 payable on demand; a typed rider adds default on any federal lien against them. Aaron was also president of Monumental Management, which extended a $220,000 line of credit to 3222 Greenmount Ave., Inc. the next year. Aaron released this mortgage himself in May 1992.

Certificate of satisfaction signed October 5, 1999 and recorded February 11, 2000 (Liber FMC 103, folios 7-8). Centrabank Inc., now Bank of America (Ronald D. Spake), certified that Greenmount Avenue Limited Partnership's January 1986 deed of trust on 3226-3240 Greenmount, Block 3882 (SEB 759/477), was paid. That was the loan the Adlers guaranteed with 3220 and 3222 (SEB 759/500). Returned to Jeanne M. Ripley of Bel Air.

Certificate of satisfaction signed October 5, 1999 and recorded February 11, 2000 (Liber FMC 103, folios 5-6). Centrabank, now Bank of America, released Greenmount Avenue Limited Partnership's May 1999 deed of trust on 3226-3240 Greenmount. The partnership had refinanced in September 1999 with a $1,755,000 Morgan Guaranty loan.

Assignment dated December 27, 2000, effective January 25, 2000, and recorded February 16, 2001 (Liber FMC 1094, folios 382-385). Morgan Guaranty Trust Company of New York assigned Greenmount Avenue Limited Partnership's 1999 deed of trust on 3228-3232 Greenmount, a $1,755,000 loan (trustee Stuart A. Kruger), to Norwest Bank Minnesota as trustee for J.P. Morgan Commercial Mortgage Finance Corp. Mortgage Pass-Through Certificates, Series 2000-C9 (loan 1043). So the Baker Block's loan became part of a Wall Street commercial mortgage bond.

Assignment dated December 27, 2000 and recorded February 16, 2001 (Liber FMC 1094, folios 378-381). Morgan Guaranty assigned the partnership's 1999 assignment of leases and rents on 3228-3232 Greenmount (Book 8844, page 314) to the same J.P. Morgan 2000-C9 trustee, Norwest Bank Minnesota.

Certificate of satisfaction signed May 16, 2017 and recorded June 12, 2017 (Liber MB 19225, folios 50-54). JAPAK, LLC (Sung K. Pak, managing member), signing in Westmoreland County, Virginia, certified that Samuel S. and Mie Young Ha had repaid the $650,000 deed of trust of May 2016 on 3226 Greenmount, the 0.47-acre lot at 33rd Street (tax ID 12-20-3882-012). JAPAK had sold the Has the block for about $3 million and carried part of the price itself.

Purchase-money mortgage dated January 21, 1976 and recorded January 22, 1976 at 9:01 a.m. (Liber RHB 3311, folios 875-878), a minute after the deed from Stanley and Thelma Plaine (3311/873). Ira and Lucille Adler, then of Stonehedge Court, Pikesville, borrowed $14,000 from Universal Savings and Loan Association of 17 Old Court Road at 12 percent, $311.43 a month for five years. The deed's taxes ($92.40 recordation, $105 transfer) put the price near $21,000, so they paid about $7,000 down. The mortgage says the loan was for business, so 3222 was bought as a commercial property from the start. Released October 19, 1978 (RHB 3676/528) when Universal refinanced them.

Second deed of trust dated April 3, 1978 and recorded April 5, 1978 (Liber RHB 3595, folios 622-625). Richard E. Kramer and David S. Goldberg of 600 Reisterstown Road, Pikesville, were lenders, trustees and notary at once. $20,000 repaid in 12 monthly payments of $1,916.67, a flat 15 percent add-on, about 26 percent a year in true terms. Three days earlier the same two men had lent the Adlers another $20,000 on 3220 (RHB 3595/626). Released October 31, 1979 (WA 3832/485).

Mortgage dated October 16, 1978 and recorded October 17, 1978 (Liber RHB 3674, folios 828-831). Ira and Lucille Adler borrowed $30,000 from Universal Savings and Loan at 12 percent, $430.42 a month for ten years, again declared a business loan. It paid off the $14,000 purchase loan of 1976, released three days later. Universal sold the loan to Merritt Savings and Loan in March 1979 (WA 3739/893); it was released in February 1984 (SEB 184/13).

Release signed October 18, 1978 and recorded October 19, 1978 (Liber RHB 3676, folio 528). Universal Savings and Loan released the $14,000 mortgage of January 1976 (RHB 3311/875), paid from its own $30,000 refinance two days earlier. The page names no property; the 1976 mortgage's margin ties it to 3222.

Assignment dated March 15, 1979 and recorded March 30, 1979 (Liber WA 3739, folio 893). Universal Savings and Loan Association assigned the Adlers' October 1978 mortgage (RHB 3674/828) to Merritt Savings & Loan, which released it in 1984.

Short release signed and recorded October 31, 1979 (Liber WA 3832, folio 485). Richard E. Kramer and David S. Goldberg, trustees, released the Adlers' April 1978 deed of trust (RHB 3595/622). Mailed to Ira Adler at 306 Old Crossing Drive. The next folio releases their companion loan on 3220.

Second mortgage dated May 27, 1980 and recorded June 6, 1980 (Liber WA 3916, folios 432-435). Ira and Lucille Adler, then giving 'Stevenson Crossing' as their address, borrowed $8,000 from Robert Spielmann of 303 East Fayette Street at 20 percent, $577.77 a month for 18 months; the payments work out to a flat add-on. Attorney Louis J. Glick. Its prior-lien clause still names the 1976 mortgage, which had been released. Released February 17, 1984 (SEB 184/15).

Third mortgage acknowledged October 31, 1980 and recorded November 14, 1980 (Liber WA 3977, folios 137-140). Robert Spielmann and Associates lent Ira and Lucille Adler $42,000 at 20 percent; the payment amount, start date and maturity are all left blank on the form. With the $30,000 Universal loan and Spielmann's $8,000, recorded debt on a building bought four years earlier for about $21,000 was near $80,000. Released February 17, 1984 (SEB 184/14).

Deed of trust dated December 11, 1980 and recorded December 18, 1980 (Liber WA 3991, folios 853-856). Stevenson Associates of 3701 Old Court Road lent $6,400 at a 14 percent add-on, six payments of $1,141.32 ending June 1981; trustees Richard E. Kramer and Howard E. Mirsky. It was the fourth lien on 3222 that year, and here the Adlers gave 3222 Greenmount as their own address. Spielmann subordinated to it the same day (WA 3991/857); released 1981 (CWM Jr. 4097/775).

Release recorded February 17, 1984 (Liber SEB 184, folio 13). Merritt Savings & Loan released the Adlers' mortgage originally given to Universal Savings (RHB 3674/828). The next two folios release both Spielmann mortgages (184/14, 184/15), so all three came off in one refinance, the $105,000 Sequoia loan of November 1983.

Short release signed about November 16, 1983 and recorded February 17, 1984 (Liber SEB 184, folio 14). Robert Spielman Associates released the Adlers' mortgage at WA 3977/137, paid at the Sequoia refinance of November 15, 1983.

Short release signed November 16, 1983 and recorded February 17, 1984 (Liber SEB 184, folio 15). Robert Spielmann released the Adlers' mortgage at WA 3916/432. Its title-file number, NT-11005, is the one on the Sequoia deed of trust of November 15, 1983 (SEB 142/132). Mailed to Nationwide Title Company, 3723 Old Court Road.

Mortgage dated July 30, 1985 but recorded only on June 19, 1987 (Liber SEB 1334, folios 205-207). Ira and Lucille Adler pledged 3222, 3220 and a lot at 4 Irving Place, Baltimore County (bought from Johns Hopkins in 1979), to Albert G. Aaron for $50,000, 24 monthly payments of $2,496.21, about 18 percent. Its stated purpose was 'to help refinance 3222 Greenmount Avenue, Inc.'s debt and to stabilize the corporations capital position', the first appearance of the Adlers' company named for the building. Aaron later ran Monumental Management, lender on the company's $220,000 line in 1990.

Deed of trust dated January 28, 1987 and recorded February 3, 1987 (Liber SEB 1163, folios 245-249). Ira and Lucille Adler borrowed $88,000 from Capital Savings Bank F.S.B. of 421 North Charles Street, at 11 percent and $1,000.21 a month over 15 years (per the note, SEB 2472/200); trustees Rita M. Miller and Thomas F. Costantini. A single-family form was used for a declared commercial loan. It took out the 1984 Sequoia loan, paid on February 2, 1987, as the Adlers sold 3220 to the Kangs. Paid off February 27, 1990.

Release signed July 9, 1987 by F. Ripley Bowman, managing officer, and recorded August 11, 1987 (Liber SEB 1400, folios 556-557). Sequoia Savings and Loan released a deed of trust from Ira and Lucille Adler that it cites as SEB 1163/245. That citation is Capital Savings' $88,000 deed of trust of January 1987, which stayed open until 1990, not a Sequoia loan. Sequoia's own loans were SEB 142/132 and 288/202, already satisfied by paid notes. A title examiner could misread this as releasing the Capital Savings lien.

Paid note with certificate of satisfaction, recorded May 10, 1990 (Liber SEB 2472, folios 200-201). The $88,000 Capital Savings Bank note of January 1987 (11 percent, $1,000.21 a month, due 2002) was stamped paid February 27, 1990. Five months later 3222 Greenmount Avenue, Inc. took a $220,000 credit line from Monumental Management backed by 3222, 3413 and 3415 (SEB 2542/327).

Indemnity deed of trust dated June 5, 1992 and recorded July 9, 1992 (Liber SEB 3282, folios 254-260). Ira and Lucille Adler pledged 3222 Greenmount and, on the east side, 3413 and 3415 Greenmount, to Jay H. Golding of Houston as security for their guaranty of his $300,000 line of credit to 3222 Greenmount Avenue, Inc. Jeanne M. Ripley of Bel Air was trustee, witness, notary and preparer. Albert Aaron's 1989 mortgage on 3222 had been released a month before (SEB 3359/460) to clear the way.

Deed of trust dated December 15, 1994 and recorded January 26, 1995 (Liber SEB 4695, folios 473-481). Ira and Lucille Adler borrowed $40,000 from Mildred C. Slaughter of 904C Woodson Road, due January 1, 1998, as a declared commercial loan; trustee Millard S. Rubenstein. The intake sheet gives the parcel as Block 3882, Lot 010 (tax ID 12-20-3882-010), which confirms the '3882' written on all the Adler papers is the block.

Subordination agreement acknowledged December 1994 to January 27, 1995 and recorded February 9, 1995 (Liber SEB 4720, folios 1-7). Jay Golding, in Houston, was paid $10,000 to put his $300,000 indemnity lien on 3222 (SEB 3282/254) behind Mildred C. Slaughter's $40,000 deed of trust; his lien on 3413 and 3415 kept first place. Slaughter's lien was capped at $40,000 and due by January 1, 1997. Valley Pine Mortgage, Inc. (Stewart Sachs) signed in Slaughter's place, so it probably arranged the loan.

Assignment of leases dated December 15, 1994, acknowledged January 27, 1995 and recorded February 9, 1995 (Liber SEB 4720, folios 8-12). Ira and Lucille Adler assigned all leases and rents at 3222 Greenmount to Mildred C. Slaughter as collateral for the $40,000 loan, warranting the leases valid and not in default. So the building had rent-paying tenants in 1995, though none are named.

Mortgage dated April 19, 1977 and recorded June 22, 1977 (Liber RHB 3488, folios 433-437). Ira and Lucille Adler, then of 21 Stonehenge Circle, Pikesville, borrowed $18,000 from Midtown Savings and Loan Association at 10 percent, $580.81 a month, due May 1980. It is the earliest recital of their purchase from Martin Beerman, personal representative of the estate of Kate Felser, dated April 11, 1977 (RHB 3461/716). Released October 1978 (RHB 3672/535).

Second deed of trust dated March 31, 1978 and recorded April 5, 1978 (Liber RHB 3595, folios 626-629). Richard E. Kramer and David S. Goldberg, Pikesville lawyers, lent $20,000 as lenders, trustees and notary, repaid in 12 payments of $1,916.67 (a flat 15 percent add-on); Kramer took his own oath of consideration. Its recitals point back to an earlier deed at MLP 8618/330 (November 2, 1951), the next link toward how the Felsers held 3220. The same lenders took a twin loan on 3222 three days later. Released October 31, 1979 (WA 3832/486).

Short release signed and recorded October 31, 1979 (Liber WA 3832, folio 486). Richard E. Kramer, trustee, released the Adlers' deed of trust recorded at RHB 3595/626. Mailed to Ira Adler, 306 Old Crossing Drive.

Partial release dated January 8, 1980 and recorded January 18, 1980 (Liber WA 3865, folio 496). Jeffrey A. Levitt, Karol Levitt, Samuel J. Aaron and Rebecca Aaron released 3220 Greenmount from the Adlers' mortgage of December 15, 1978 (WA 3719/79), 'retaining the liens on all other properties'. It sits 17 folios before the City's $67,000 housing-department loan on 3220 (WA 3865/513), so clearing it was a condition of the City loan. The lenders' names match Jeffrey A. Levitt of Old Court Savings and Loan and his wife Karol, but the page does not identify them further. WA 3719/79 should list the other properties.

Third mortgage dated April 15, 1983 and recorded April 18, 1983 (Liber SEB 40, folios 39-42). Ira and Lucille Adler (Lucille signing for Ira) borrowed $6,000 from Robert Spielmann and Charles Sandler at 20 percent, interest only at $100 a month, due April 1985. They covenanted to use the money only for 'withholding taxes due the United States', a business's payroll tax debt. It sat behind the City's $67,000 loan. Released January 1986 (SEB 756/514).

Release signed December 19, 1985 and recorded January 8, 1986 (Liber SEB 756, folios 516-517). Robert Spielmann and Associates released the Adlers' 1980 assignment of rents (CWM Jr. 4075/686), which it describes as covering 3220 and 3222. That assignment had pledged the Better Looks lease on 3220. It was part of the January 1986 package that cleared both lots for the Baker Block guaranty.

Subordination agreement dated January 8, 1986 and recorded April 8, 1986 (Liber SEB 840, folios 457-459). Thomas Acampora and Samuel W. Goldberg put their $31,000 mortgage on 3220 and 3222 (SEB 472/551) behind a $550,000 CentraBank deed of trust the Adlers were about to give. The next day the Adlers signed the indemnity deed of trust backing their guaranty of CentraBank's $550,000 loan to Greenmount Avenue Limited Partnership for the Baker Block (SEB 759/500), so that is the lien meant.

Deed of release dated November 21, 1986 and recorded February 3, 1987 (Liber SEB 1163, folios 252-256). Trustees Barry C. Sheehan and Helen M. Schwarz released the indemnity deed of trust of January 9, 1986 (SEB 759/500) on 3220 and 3222, reciting that the beneficiary had canceled the guaranty it secured. It cleared 3220 for the sale to Jin Wook Kang. Both acknowledgments are dated November 13, eight days before the date written in the release.

Paid note with certificate of satisfaction, sworn February 27, 1987 and recorded March 5, 1987 (Liber SEB 1197, folios 464-465). The $35,000 Sequoia Savings note of August 1984 (15.5 percent, $501.90 a month, callable after three years), secured on '3220 & 3222 Greenmount Avenue' by SEB 288/202, was stamped paid February 2, 1987 out of the Capital Savings refinance.

Paid note with certificate of satisfaction, sworn July 13, 1987 and recorded July 14, 1987 (Liber SEB 1368, folios 295-296). The $105,000 Sequoia Savings note of November 1983, 14 percent at $1,263 a month with a balloon in December 1988, signed by Lucille Adler for herself and as Ira's attorney-in-fact, was stamped paid February 2, 1987. The trustees were Jerome S. and Sanford R. Cardin; the name matches the Baltimore lawyer who co-owned Old Court Savings and Loan, but the page doesn't identify him.

Deed dated November 11, 1993 and recorded July 22, 1994 (Liber SEB 4378, folios 423-426). Eun Hee Kang conveyed 3220 Greenmount to Jin Wook Kang and herself as tenants by the entireties for love and affection, reversing his 1990 deed to her (SEB 2570/562). Both deeds certify the building owner-occupied.

Deed dated March 29, 1922 and recorded April 7, 1922 (Liber SCL 3844, folios 65-67), for $5. Peter and Sophia Oletsky and Benjamin and Fannie Cluster (he also signed in Hebrew) conveyed six lots to The Crystal Amusement Company: the 1909 theatre lot at 3211, the lots to its south that became 3207 and 3209, and three lots on Gay Street near Mott Street. The recitals show how they got the theatre: an assignment from The Waverly Amusement Company in 1914 (SCL 2946/504), one from Benjamin Rosenheim in 1919 (SCL 3341/77), and 1921 deeds from George R. Gaither and others, trustees, and from Henry R. Granger (SCL 3731/193, /195). It was subject to a $35,000 Mortgage Guarantee Company mortgage of 1921 with $32,000 unpaid. Every later deed of 3211 cites this deed as the source of title.

Deed and agreement dated July 14, 1927 (Liber SCL 4803, folios 101-104). Leah Schloss, widow, owner of 3207 and 3209 Greenmount, and The Crystal Amusement Company (P. Oletsky, president), owner of 3211, settled two rights between the buildings. It recites that 3211 and its rear to Old York Road were 'used ... as a moving Picture Theatre', with the auditorium on the rear portion behind 3207-3209, and that the theatre had been venting 'permissively' through the northeast corner of 3209. Crystal got the right to keep that ventilator 'so long as' 3211 stayed a movie theatre. Schloss, about to build 'a building that is to be higher than the structures at present existing', got a permanent party-wall right, which dates a rebuild of 3207-3209 to about 1927-28. The Rosenheim estate executors and other mortgagees consented; four mortgages on 3211 are listed. Two of their liber numbers do not fit their dates as typed. It cites Schloss's 1923 deed as SCL 4083/155; the deed itself is recorded at SCL 4082/155-156, so the agreement's copyist was one volume off.

Deed and agreement dated July 14, 1927 (Liber SCL 4803, folios 101-104). Leah Schloss, who had bought 3207 and 3209 from The Crystal Amusement Company in 1923, was about to put up a taller building there. In return for letting the movie theatre at 3211 keep a ventilator on the northeast corner of 3209 for as long as it stayed a theatre, she got a permanent right to build into the party wall. It describes her lot as 34 feet 4 inches on Greenmount beginning 128 feet 11 1/4 inches south of Gorsuch Avenue, 90 feet 7 inches deep, and says the theatre's auditorium ran behind it. So the present 3207-3209 building dates from about 1927-28.

Deed dated January 29, 1988 and recorded February 1, 1988 (Liber SEB 1595, folios 218-221). The Grand Company, by Frank H. Durkee III, president, conveyed 3211 Greenmount, block 4076, to Greenmount Avenue Partnership for $300,000; the transfer and documentary taxes ($1,500 and $1,650) confirm the price. It also brings in two 1955 instruments no later deed repeats: a deed from Beulah Bruehl to The Grand Company (Liber 10007/357) and a revocable license between the company and Crown 5 and 10c to $1.00 Stores, Inc. (10007/361), a dime-store chain and probably a neighbour. The Grand Company had held the theatre since 1929.

Deed of trust dated January 29, 1988 and recorded February 1, 1988 (Liber SEB 1595, folios 222-227). Greenmount Avenue Partnership, by Israel Freedman, general partner, signing in Broward County, Florida, gave Maryland National Bank a $300,000 deed of trust on 3211 Greenmount, the full price; trustees Joseph A. Hilseberg and Stephen F. Beckenholdt. Notices went to 'Ted Greenberg' at 2237 East Monument Street. Israel Freedman, Earl Freedman and Beth Marlene Greenberg guaranteed it personally. The loan was modified in 1988, 1993 and 1994 and not released until January 2025.

Indemnity deed of trust dated August 14, 2003 and recorded August 18, 2003 (Liber FMC 4177, folios 262-284). Greenmount Avenue Partnership, LLP (Israel Freedman, partner), of 1800 Woodlawn Drive, pledged 3211 Greenmount to PRLAP, Inc., trustee for Bank of America, to secure its guaranty of a $1,000,000 term loan to Theodore Greenberg, Beth Greenberg and ESCO, Ltd., plus any swap contracts. The partnership was 'not primarily liable': the building backed a family business loan. Released December 2014 (FMC 16759/161).

Certificate of satisfaction dated December 2, 2014 and recorded December 9, 2014 (Liber FMC 16759, folios 161-163). Bank of America (Lee Ann Ouellette) released the 2003 indemnity deed of trust (FMC 4177/262) as paid, so the Greenbergs' $1 million loan was repaid by then.

Release dated December 2, 2014 and recorded December 9, 2014 (Liber FMC 16759, folios 164-166). Bank of America released the 2003 assignment of the building's leases and rents (FMC 4177/285), recorded the same morning as the deed-of-trust release.

Release dated January 28, 2025 and recorded January 31, 2025 (Liber XAC 27619, folios 221-222). Bank of America, successor to Maryland National Bank, released the partnership's 1994 assignment of lessor's interest in leases (SEB 4089/39) on the $300,000 loan. The rest of this PDF (folios 223-246) is an unrelated 2024 house sale at 3216 Yosemite Avenue that happens to follow in the book.

Certificate of satisfaction dated January 28, 2025 and recorded January 31, 2025 (Liber XAC 27619, folios 247-248). Bank of America, successor to Maryland National Bank, released the $300,000 deed of trust of January 29, 1988 (SEB 1595/222) as paid, and recited its history: the 1993 extension (SEB 3854/167) and the December 1993 increase to $243,200 (SEB 4089/36).

Deed dated February 3, 2025 and recorded March 3, 2025 (Liber XAC 27711, folios 158-163). Greenmount Avenue, LLC, successor to Greenmount Avenue Partnership, by Greg M. Greenberg, manager, conveyed 3211 Greenmount (tax ID 09-03-4076-006) to Maverick 3203 Greenmount LLC of 12612 Waterspout Court, Owings Mills, for $132,500, an arm's-length sale. Taxes: city recordation $1,325, city transfer $1,987.50, state transfer $662.50. The price is 44 percent of what the family paid in 1988. The buyer is the owner of 3203-3209 since 2015, so one owner now holds the theatre and the storefronts the theatre's owners split off in 1923. The state intake sheet classes the building as residential, not commercial.

Certificate of satisfaction dated January 14, 2020 and recorded January 17, 2020 (Liber MB 21788, folios 449-450). Bay Vanguard Bank, successor to St. Casimirs Savings Bank, released the indemnity deed of trust of October 7, 2009 (Liber 12115/396) by which Williams Realty, LLC pledged 3208 Greenmount for a loan to Robert D. Williams personally. It was given the day Williams Realty bought 3208 from Kitty's Bar (12115/391). Paid off a year before the 2021 sale to PP Singh.

Purchase-money deed of trust dated December 10, 2021 and recorded May 26, 2022 (Liber MB 24654, folios 362-374). QT Hau, LLC (Thy Vo, manager, and Quyen Vinh Hau) gave Open Bank of Los Angeles a $2,975,000 variable-rate deed of trust on the Baker Block (tax ID 12-20-3882-012), trustee Amerikor Title & Escrow of Rockville. The intake sheet gives the price as $2,900,000 from Samuel S. and Mie Young Ha, so the loan was 103 percent of the price. The borrowers also include Lux Nail Spa & Hair Salon LLC and Hau Realty LLC. Open Bank foreclosed in 2025 and released the loan in March 2026.

Assignment of rents dated December 10, 2021 and recorded May 26, 2022 (Liber MB 24654, folios 375-381), securing Open Bank loan 52210250 for $2,975,000. Signed by Thy Vo and Quyen Vinh Hau. The form puts the property in 'Baltimore County' and names California law, with venue in Los Angeles.

Commercial deed of trust dated March 9, 2026 and recorded May 18, 2026 (Liber XAC 29047, folios 399-414). NSR OF MD LLC of 14404 Big Bear Court, Silver Spring (members Joseph and Vasumathi L. Rollakanty) gave Union Service Corporation, trustee for Atlantic Union Bank of Reston, Virginia, a $1,641,500 deed of trust on parcel 3882-012, 3226-3238 Greenmount. So NSR bought the block after Open Bank's 2025 foreclosure; its own deed is not in this PDF but was probably recorded in the same batch. The legal description is word for word the 2021 one.

Certificate of satisfaction signed October 5, 1999 and recorded February 11, 2000 (Liber FMC 103, folios 9-10), the third CentraBank release in that batch. Deed dated May 18, 1993 and recorded June 30, 1993 at 10:39 a.m. (Liber SEB 3755, folios 235-239). Gerald M.
