Each house 15 by 48 ft; the cost is given as $6,000 here, $9,000 in the notes of Apr. 6-7 and $5,000 in the issued-permit list of Apr. 21: three estimates for one project. The plans were drawn by J. F. Gerwig.

The Sunday Sun's building-permits column of Apr. 21, 1912, p. 28 ('Jaco' and 'dwellin' are cut at the column edge and supplied). It is the issued-permit record of the project: location 'northwest corner York road and Gilmore lane', the toll-house lot at the northwest corner of the lane; 15 by 47 ft each (the notes of Apr. 6-10 say 48); tin roofs; hot-air heat; cost $5,000; architect J. F. Gerwig; 'owner, builder', so Aull built his own houses. Building could begin in late April 1912. Polk 1913, canvassed in autumn 1912, has no household on the row; Polk 1914, canvassed in autumn 1913, has the first.

The Sun's real-estate transfers of Dec. 17, 1912, p. 12: 'Jacob H. Aull and wife have sold to F. X. Hooper four lots on the west side of Greenmount avenue, near Gilmore lane, for $4,500 in fee. One lot measures 15 by 82 feet, and the other three 14 by 82 feet each.' The item gives no house numbers; the four lots have the shape of the row (15 + 14 + 14 + 14 = 57 ft, each 82 ft deep), 3026 and the three 14-ft bays 3028, 3030 and 3032. The deed behind it (S.C.L. 2787/376, Dec. 16, 1912) settles what was sold: Aull had leased the four new houses for 99 years to Alice M. Chapman on Dec. 6, 1912 at $72 and $66 a year (S.C.L. 2787/374), and Hooper bought the fee subject to that lease, 'particularly the aforesaid rents or reversions'. So '$4,500 in fee' is the price of the four ground rents, $270 a year capitalized at 6 per cent, not of four houses. The houses stayed under the lease, which is how Aull could still advertise 3026 and 3028 in July 1913 and sell houses of the row subject to ground rent in 1917 and 1918 (3026 to Spellman in Feb. 1917; lots to Shields and to Sanner, the families of 3032 and 3028, in Nov. 1918). The buyer, 'Frank X. Hooper of the County of Baltimore' in the deed, is probably the F. X. Hooper of the F. X. Hooper Company, the Glen Arm maker of corrugated-box machinery: the Sun of Feb. 3, 1914 (p. 12) records F. X. Hooper and wife conveying 2 acres at Glenarm, with the 'plant and good will of plant', to the F. X. Hooper Company for $150,000, and a Sun ad of Apr. 12, 1913 has him selling a small hotel at Lewes, Delaware. His testamentary trustee sold the 3028 rent in 1945 (M.L.P. 6799/549). The item spells the lane 'Gilmore' and calls the road 'Greenmount avenue'; the April 1912 notices said 'York road' and 'Gilmor'.

The Newspapers.com run of 135 pages of 1920-21 printing '3028 Greenmount' was sampled on four pages, the first, two in the middle and the last, and all four are sale listings for the house. (1) Sun, Sunday Aug. 1, 1920, p. 32 (this image), and Evening Sun Aug. 2, p. 16: a two-line classified, 'FOR SALE--3028 GREENMOUNT AVE.; a modern home, 6 rooms, bath, electric lights, gas, steam heat, front and back porches', with no agent or price. (2) Evening Sun, Sept. 16, 1920, p. 25 and Nov. 30, 1920, p. 22: the address in a multi-property list of Realty Mart, 100 N. Eutaw St. (3) Sun, Jan. 24, 1921, p. 13: in the 'Deal with Davis will help to finance' list, '3028 GREENMOUNT AVE. Porch front, 6 rooms and bath; modern'. So the house was offered through three channels for almost six months; the digits read 3028 on all four page images, and the listings do not name the owner. Polk 1918 has John G. Godwin at 3028 and Polk 1922 Charles E. Morris, motorman, so the house changed occupants between.

A classified in the Sun's furniture and household columns, Sunday, May 24, 1942, p. 42: 'FRIGIDAIRE. 6.6 cu. ft. Beds, dining-rm. suite. Can be seen Sun. & Mon. 3030 Greenmount ave.' The seller is not named. Martha V. Berterman of 3030 Greenmount died May 8, 1942, and her funeral was held at the William Cook Mansion on May 11; the sale may be the clearing of her household, but the ad does not say so.

The Sun's 'Situations Wanted--Female' column of July 16, 1941, p. 21, with the same line in the Evening Sun that day (p. 25): 'SEAMSTRESS desires mending & sewing work in homes. 3030 Greenmount ave.' The advertiser gives no name or telephone; she offered to work in other people's homes and gave 3030 as her address.

The Sun of Nov. 27, 1920, p. 18: Mrs. Sarah A. Bonsall (nee Huff), 'one of the first woman postmasters', died Nov. 26 at her home, 3120 Greenmount Avenue, one block north of the toll-house lot. She was appointed postmaster of the Waverly post office to succeed her husband, Townsend S. Bonsall, 'who died about 40 years ago' (he kept the first tollgate in Woods' directories of 1871-1875 and died in 1877), and 'remained postmaster for 14 years', so to about 1891; she was the incumbent challenged for the post in April 1890. Survivors: a daughter, Miss Florence V. B. Bonsall, and a brother, Joseph Huff. The Evening Sun's death notice the same day (p. 11) gives the funeral from her home on Sunday at 3.30 p.m. and private interment in St. John's Cemetery, Waverly; the Baltimore City Register of Wills has her estate (174965, filed Feb. 10, 1921), and the St. John's interment roll lists her as Sarah Ann Huff Bonsall, 1849-1920. The item does not mention the toll house. Two accounts place the post office differently. Anna Cole (1933) says it was at the tollgate under T. S. Bonsal and that his widow moved it to rooms in the Hamilton Hotel after his death. Charles T. Leight's Sun Magazine memoir of 1949 says Mrs. T. S. Bonsal ran the toll gate after her husband died and that 'the toll-gate building also contained the post office', with her as postmistress. Both put the post office in the toll house in Townsend's time; they differ on whether it stayed there under her.

The Sun of July 15, 1937, p. 18: 'SCHOFIELD.--On July 12, 1937, TILGHMAN, beloved husband of Emma G. Shehan Schofield.' Funeral from the E. A. Wiedefeld funeral home, Twenty-second street and Greenmount avenue; requiem Mass at St. Ann's; interment in Baltimore Cemetery. The notice prints no age, no 'Jr.' and no parents. The Baltimore City Register of Wills indexes the estate as 'SCHOFIELD JR, TILGHMAN', died 07/12/1937, filed 05/12/1948 (OLD49278), and Find a Grave memorial 207098543 (born 1867, died July 12, 1937, spouse Emma G. Sheehan Schofield) makes him the son of the toll keeper Tilghman Schofield (1834-1901). The directories show a Tilghman Schofield jr. as clerk at the Waverly toll gate from 1883 to 1892. Father and son were both buried in Baltimore Cemetery by the Wiedefeld firm (the father's funeral in 1901 was in the charge of Henry C. Wiedefeld). The Evening Sun ran the notice July 12-14 and the Sun on July 14.

The Sun of May 27, 1901, p. 7: 'The funeral of Mr. Tilghman Schofield, who was for 17 years keeper of the toll-gate on the York road at Waverly, took place yesterday [Sunday, May 26] from his home, 405 Montebello avenue.' The Rev. W. G. Herbert of the Caroline Street Methodist Episcopal Church officiated with the Rev. G. W. Feelemyer of the Waverly Church; a delegation came from Wilson Post, G.A.R., of which he was a member, and four men from Waverly Lodge, Knights of Honor, of which he was a charter member. The pallbearers were John Kahl, Charles Carroll, Charles Schofield, William H. Parker, H. Carroll and John Keller. Interment was in the Baltimore Cemetery; Henry C. Wiedefeld had charge. The death notice of May 25, 1901 (p. 4) gives the death: 'On Friday, May 24, at his late residence, No. 405 Montebello avenue, Waverly, TILGHMAN, in the 66th year of his age, beloved husband of Caroline Schofield.' He was a Union army man (the Sun of Oct. 15, 1892 says he was 'crippled in action'; Find a Grave gives Battery A, 1st Maryland Light Artillery). Seventeen years is consistent with the directories, which list him at the gate from 1878 to 1892.

The Baltimore County column of the Sun, Oct. 15, 1892, p. 10 ('The Assault on Toll-Gate Keeper Schofield'; the right edge of each line is cut in the copy). Schofield was beaten about the face with the butt end of a whip on Friday, Oct. 7, and was out again on Oct. 14. James Thompson, 'who lives in upper Baltimore county', was arrested on the charge; the hearing set for Oct. 12 was postponed to the following Wednesday because Schofield could not appear, and Thompson gave $1,000 bail. The men had had words about toll money; Schofield was knocked down, passers-by separated them, and a man named Hart (his title is cut) carried him into the toll-gate house and attended him: his nose was broken and he was cut over the right eye. The Sun adds that he received many complaints about the road, then being regraded, but was 'a general favorite with those who travel the York turnpike', deducted toll for the bad parts of the road, denied using the word thief, and had served in the Federal army and been crippled in action. The same day's front-page county digest says he is out of doors again. The column does not name the gate; it is the Waverly gate, which the directories give Schofield from 1878 to 1892, and the toll-gate house is probably the house the Sun described when it was pulled down in 1907. The details fit the elder Tilghman Schofield (born 1834-35), not his son.

Find a Grave memorial 179411650 (created 2017): born June 1834, Maryland; died May 1901, aged 66; buried in Baltimore Cemetery. The biography reads 'for 17 years, was the toll keeper at the York Rd tollgate in Waverly; home address: 405 Montebello Ave', and gives his service as a private in Battery A, 1st Regiment, Maryland Light Artillery, discharged Sept. 19, 1864 for disability after a fall from a horse; it cites the Sun of May 27, 1901. Child: Tilghman Schofield (1867-1937), memorial 207098543 (spouse Emma G. Sheehan Schofield, 1863-1942). The memorial is user-submitted and much of it is drawn from the Sun item; its own additions are the birth month and the muster record, which has not been checked against the rolls. Its birth year, 1834, sits a year off the Sun's 'in the 66th year' (born 1835-36).

The Sun of Nov. 3, 1967, p. 13, with his photograph. Dr. Nicholas Interrante died on Wednesday, Nov. 1, at the Veterans Hospital in Hampton, Va., after a long illness, aged 90 by the paper's count. 'Since his retirement as a physician' he had spent 30 years training canaries to sing given melodies and to harmonize, using Wagner, Mendelssohn and Strauss and the arias of Verdi and Puccini; the text says he began the hobby in 1937, a subhead says 1947, and the Sun's 1957 feature says 1936. His interest in music began in World War I, when he was music director at Walter Reed Hospital in Washington, playing the mandolin and staging programs for the troops. The death notice the same day (p. 35) gives him as 'DOCTOR NICHOLAS, of 506 McCabe avenue, beloved husband of the late Ida Interrante', with services at Henry W. Jenkins & Sons, 4905 York road, on Nov. 6 and interment in Moreland Memorial Park Cemetery. Ida Interrante had died at their home, 506 McCabe Avenue, on June 15, 1950 (Evening Sun notice, June 15, 1950, p. 49). His estate is Baltimore City Register of Wills OLD93339 (filed Nov. 22, 1967). His one documented tie to 3030 is the Sun's notice of July 11, 1943, which names him 'of 3030 Greenmount Avenue' at his marriage to Mrs. Ida H. Caples; neither 1967 item mentions Greenmount Avenue, and the Sun's 1957 feature calls him a retired chiropodist.

A Sunday feature with his photograph ('Singing Teacher' / 'Dr. Nicholas Interrante Turns Out Birds Able to Whistle the Classics'), about half of it read. Over twenty years he had trained hundreds of canaries to follow complex melodies, harmonize and improvise; 'Dr. Interrante is a retired chiropodist, a widower. The birds are his principal hobby.' In World War I he entertained the patients at Walter Reed Hospital with the mandolin and staged musical programs, and he wrote a march that was published; 'He became interested in birds in 1936.' The 1967 obituary calls him a physician. The part of the feature read does not say where he practised; his only documented tie to 3030 Greenmount is the 1943 marriage notice.

Find a Grave memorial 204633086 (created 2019): born May 15, 1884, Menfi, Province of Agrigento, Sicily; died Nov. 1, 1967 (aged 83), Hampton, Virginia; buried in Moreland Memorial Park, Parkville, Baltimore County. Spouse: Ida Heyser Interrante, 1879-1950, married 1943, the 'Mrs. Ida H. Caples' of the Sun's 1943 marriage notice; she died June 15, 1950. The death, place, burial and wife agree with the Sun; only the birth year conflicts: the Sun's obituary of Nov. 3, 1967 gives his age as 90 (born about 1877), the memorial 83 (born 1884). The memorial lists record sets (a Veterans Administration master index, a 1942 draft registration, Virginia death records, New York abstracts of World War I service and New York naturalization records) that have not been read; the 1942 registration or the naturalization record would settle the year. The memorial is user-submitted.

A help-wanted line in the Sun of Nov. 29, 1995, p. 35 (the same day also on pp. 33, 111 and 187) and Dec. 3, 1995, p. 105: 'BEAUTICIANS & Manicurist. Walk-in salon, 3030 Greenmount Ave.' The ad names neither the salon nor its owner. In 1995 the health center owned 3028-3032; it bought 3011-3013 for offices in April 1995 and sought bids for an elevator that October.

Maryland SDAT Business Express, Department ID D00311068, read in September 2026. The search returns six listings of five names: PEOPLE'S FREE MEDICAL CLINIC, INC.; THE PEOPLE'S COMMUNITY HEALTH CLINIC, INC.; THE PEOPLE'S COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTER, INC. (listed twice); MEDHEALTH OF MARYLAND, INC.; and the current name, THE PEOPLE'S COMMUNITY HEALTH CENTERS, INC., status forfeited, not in good standing. General information: a non-stock corporation formed in Maryland on Apr. 16, 1970, with principal office and resident agent at Suite 800, 1 East Pratt Street. Filing history, newest first: forfeiture by department action Oct. 11, 2019; articles of amendment changing the name Apr. 12, 2017, Dec. 29, 2014 and Sept. 10, 2014; articles of amendment and a resolution Mar. 10, 2014; articles of transfer and a certificate of conveyance Mar. 14, 2012; two articles of transfer and two certificates of conveyance June 3, 2011; articles of transfer June 30, 2006 (film B00978/1267) and resolutions Mar. 15 and Jan. 9, 2006; amendments with a name change June 22, 1982 (F2546/3352) and July 30, 1980 (F2482/992); articles of incorporation Apr. 16, 1970 (F802/438, 8 pages). The filings themselves have not been opened, so the counterparties of the 2006, 2011 and 2012 transfers and which amendment created which name are not known. The clinic opened at 3028 on May 4, 1970; the Sun of Nov. 8, 1981 says it was renamed in 1980.

The Evening Sun of June 5, 1913, p. 11: 'WANTED--Exp. Photographer for amateur developing and printing. 3044 Greenmount ave.', with the insertion code J5-6t (six insertions from June 5; the Sun ran it June 6-8). The ad is unsigned, but its wording is identical to the help-wanted ad that printed '3030 Greenmount av.' in Sept. 1912, and Zepp Photo Supply Co. advertised for darkroom help at 3030 under its own name in May 1912. The block had been renumbered by the autumn of 1912 (Polk 1913 prints 'Zepp Photo Supply Co (Simon J Zepp) 3044 Greenmt av'), so the old 3030 is today's 3044.

A Sunday classified under 'Fishing Shores' in the Sun of Mar. 12, 1911, p. 4: 'FOR LEASE--On Magothy River, Anne Arundel county, 300 FT. OF BEAUTIFUL SHORE FRONT. High Bluff. Will lease in 50 ft front lots at 40c. foot. Address ZEPP PHOTO SUPPLY CO., 3030 Greenmount avenue.' It is the earliest '3030 Greenmount' page on Newspapers.com and names the firm at the number the building carried before the renumbering of 1912, when 3030 became 3044. The same firm prints 3044 from 1913 and, as Zepp Photo Centers, 3040 Greenmount Avenue in 1961-62.

A list of newly registered automobiles in the Evening Sun of Apr. 11, 1912, p. 9 (numbers 4970-4982, with owner, address, make and horsepower) includes 'J. Zepp, 3030 Greenmount avenue, Stanley 10', a 10-horsepower Stanley steamer. 3030 was the Zepp photo-supply building's number before the renumbering of 1912 (now 3044). Which Zepp 'J.' is has not been resolved; Polk 1913 prints Simon J. Zepp, photographer, at 3044 with his house at 3042.

The Sun of May 29, 1912, p. 3 (and May 30 and 31, p. 3; the Evening Sun May 29-30, p. 11): 'WANTED--YOUNG MAN to do Developing, Trimming and Mounting; amateur pictures. Apply ZEPP PHOTO SUPPLY CO., 3030 Greenmount ave.' The insertion code m29-6t means six insertions from May 29; the pages seen run May 29 to 31. It names the firm at the building's pre-1913 number, now 3044.

A Muntz TV display ad in the Sun of Aug. 21, 1955, p. 85, repeated in the Evening Sun of Aug. 23, 1955 (p. 24) and in the Baltimore Afro-American of Oct. 1 and 15, 1955, ends with the bar '3000 GREENMOUNT AVE. * OPEN EVERY NITE 'TIL 9 * FREE PARKING'; the Afro version reads 'See Muntz in your home tonite! Call VE. 7-1200' for factory authorized Muntz TV service, and prints the third digit of the address blotted. Muntz's earlier Baltimore store, in the Sun of May 16, 1953, was at the corner of North Avenue and Howard Street, with the same telephone. By Nov. 1958 Muntz Television Sales Corp. was advertising from 3334 Greenmount Ave.

Read on the scan (R.O. 1949, pp. 239-240). Augustus D. Clemens Junior and Mary Clemens his wife, of Baltimore County, convey to Charles M. Rahe of Baltimore City, in fee simple, for $500, a lot 'in the Village of Waverly', beginning on the easternmost side of the York Turnpike Road 175 feet 7 inches south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot and 252 feet 2 inches south of the north side of Bateman's Alley, running south 15 feet to the northwest corner of the lot Clemens sold William L. Fink (deed of April 12, 1898, R.O. 1729/241), east 48 feet 3 inches to Old York Road, north 15 feet 2 inches, and west 53 feet to the beginning. Recital: 'a portion of the ground conveyed by [Shepard?] T. Keller (widower) to said Augustus D. Clemens Junior by Deed in fee simple dated December 20th 1897' (R.O. 1710/105, which Jeff pulled on Oct. 12, 2026: folios 104 to 108 hold other deeds recorded Dec. 20, 1897, see 720:negative-ro-1710-105-keller-clemens-1897; the grantor's first name is handwritten and uncertain). Acknowledged March 20, 1902 before Chas. J. Fox, notary, Baltimore County; received for record March 27, 1902 at 3:50 P.M. (Robert Ogle, clerk). The same metes and an unbroken chain of recitals run through the deeds of 1926, 1934, 1944, 1961, 1982 and 2016, so 'the lot conveyed to Charles M. Rahe' named in the 3017 descriptions is 3015. Der Deutsche Correspondent's transfer columns printed the sale on March 29, 1902 (p. 5, '$550') and April 1, 1902 (p. 5, '$500'). Correction/pointer, Oct. 13, 2026: the grantor of the Dec. 20, 1897 deed is Shepard G. Miller, widower (read in R.O. 1729/241, 1728/284, 1728/286), not 'Keller', and the deed is at R.O. 1710/153 (see 720:negative-ro-1710-105-keller-clemens-1897). Update Oct. 13, 2026: the parent deed (the 'Keller' above) is read: Shepard G. Miller, unmarried, to Augustus D. Clemens Jr., Dec. 20, 1897, $5,300, R.O. 1710/153 (720:mdlr-ro1710-153-miller-clemens-1897); Miller took it from William H. Bayless, trustee, Sept. 2, 1896 (R.O. 1637/49).

Read on the scan (S.C.L. 4613, pp. 367-368). By a decree of the Circuit Court of Baltimore City of April 28, 1926, in Thomas Mackenzie, Trustee, et al. v. Thomas Mackenzie, Executor, the trustee under Charles M. Rahe's will was directed to sell the fee-simple property; on or about June 2, 1926 he sold it to Harry S. Schapiro for $5,125, and the sale was ratified. The deed, dated and recorded Aug. 3, 1926 (2:02 P.M.; Louise C. Wimmer, notary), repeats the 1902 metes (175 feet 7 inches south of the two-mile stone, 15 feet, the Fink lot, 53 feet) and recites the 1902 deed from Clemens Jr. (R.O. 1949/239). So the Rahe family owned the 3015 lot from 1902 until the trust was wound up after the widow's death (Dec. 28, 1925) and the Reilly v. MacKenzie appeal (June 29, 1926): 24 years.

Read on the scan (S.C.L. 5481, pp. 414-415). By an order of Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City of Feb. 6, 1933, in Hortense Schapiro, administratrix, et al. v. Harry S. Schapiro et al. (Docket 37A, folio 44A), Edward L. Ward was appointed receiver; on Aug. 16, 1934 he reported the sale of the property to Fletcher L. Vinson for $3,600, and the sale was ratified. The deed is dated Sept. 18, 1934 and was acknowledged the same day before Stanley K. Harman, J.P.; its recording date was not captured. Same 15-foot metes; recital: 'BEING the same lot of ground described in a deed from Thomas MacKenzie Trustee to the said Harry S Schapiro dated August 3 1926 ... Liber SCL No 4613 folio 367'. The Sun's transfer column of Sept. 20, 1934 (p. 23) prints the sale: 'YORK RD., e.s.-Edward L. Ward, rec., to Fletcher L. Vinson ... 3,600'. This is when a Vinson first owned 3015; the price had fallen from $5,125 in 1926.

(1) Read on the scan (S.C.L. 5497, pp. 145-146): Fletcher L. Vinson and Margaret C. Vinson his wife convey 3015 to Lillie E. Norris for $5 by a deed dated Dec. 18, 1934, with the same 15-foot metes and the recital 'BEING the same lot of ground described in a Deed from Edward L Ward Receiver to the said Fletcher L Vinson dated September 18 1934 ... Liber SCL No 5481 folio 414'. (2) Norris leases the lot back to Fletcher L. Vinson 'for the renewable term of ninety nine years subject to the annual ground rent of $120.00' (lease of Dec. 18, 1934, S.C.L. 5497/146); the lease is known from its recital in the 1944 deed M.L.P. 6619/478 and from the Sun's transfer column, not from its own page. (3) Norris sells the reversion and the rent to R. Benson Phelps, known only from the Sun's transfer column of Thursday, Dec. 20, 1934 (p. 23): 'Fletcher L. Vinson and wife to Lillie Norris ... 5 / Lillian Norris to Fletcher L. Vinson (lease) / Lillie Norris to R. Benson Phelps ... 5'; the liber of that deed has not been found. This is the usual Baltimore way of creating a ground rent: the owner probably raised money on the ground and kept the building. Fletcher's wife in this deed is Margaret C. Vinson; by 1943 it is Kathryn R. Vinson. Correction/pointer, Oct. 13, 2026: all four instruments of Dec. 18, 1934 are now read: the lease (S.C.L. 5497/146, 721:mdlr-scl5497-146-norris-vinson-lease-1934), Norris's deed of the rent and reversion to R. Benson Phelps (S.C.L. 5497/147 to 148, 721:mdlr-scl5497-147-norris-phelps-rent-1934, recorded 2:47 P.M.) and Vinson's $1,000 mortgage to Phelps (S.C.L. 5497/148 to 149, 721:mdlr-scl5497-148-vinson-phelps-mortgage-1934).

Read on the scans (M.L.P. 6619, pp. 477-479). (1) July 8, 1944: R. Benson Phelps and Mabel A. Phelps his wife convey to Fletcher L. Vinson in fee, for $5, with $2.20 U.S. and $2.00 Maryland stamps (about $2,000, the $120 rent capitalized at 6 percent); acknowledged before Louis H. Schillinger. (2) July 11, 1944: Fletcher L. Vinson and Kathryn R. Vinson his wife convey to Ella Thorington, for $5; the recital calls the lot 'now known as 3015 Greenmount Avenue' and recites the 1934 lease from Lillie E. Norris at $120 a year and the Phelps deed, 'under which the leasehold estate and the fee were merged and the said annual rent forever extinguished'. (3) July 11, 1944: Ella Thorington, unmarried, reconveys to Fletcher L. and Kathryn R. Vinson as tenants by the entireties (M.L.P. 6619/479, the deed the 1961 deed cites). Mildred R. De Rusha was witness and notary; all three were recorded July 12, 1944 (M. Luther Pittman, clerk). The same-day round trip through Thorington was a conveyancing step to create the joint tenancy, not a sale.

Read on the scan (S.C.L. 2500, pp. 73-74). Augustus D. Clemens Jr. of Baltimore City, for $5, assigns to Randolph B. Mason the 3017 lot (east side of the York Turnpike Road 156 feet 5 inches south of the two-mile stone, at the southwest corner of the lot Clemens leased to Jacob H. Aull, R.O. 1728/284; south 19 feet 2 inches 'to the lot conveyed to Charles M Rahe'; east along Rahe's lot 53 feet to Old York Road; north 20 feet 4 inches; west 58 feet 1 inch), 'for all the residue of the term of years ... with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the annual rent of fifty four dollars payable in half yearly instalments on the first of every April and October', and subject to a mortgage to the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County with a balance due of $390. Recital: 'Being the same lot described in a deed from Lennox B Clemens trustee to said Augustus D Clemens Jr dated 17 December 1908' (S.C.L. 2497/333), a trustee's deed. Acknowledged May 15, 1909 before Lennox B. Clemens, notary; recorded May 18, 1909. A. D. Clemens Jr. died six months later. Correction/pointer, Oct. 13, 2026: S.C.L. 2497/332 to 337 were pulled and hold no Lennox B. Clemens deed (721:negative-scl-2497-333-lennox-clemens-1908); the lease that created the $54 rent is Oct. 1, 1903, Clemens Jr. and wife to Joseph J. Willis, R.O. 2037/211 (recited in M.L.P. 8666/310). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the 3017 lease is read (721:mdlr-ro2037-211-clemens-willis-lease-3017-1903): Clemens Jr. to Joseph J. Willis, Oct. 1, 1903, 99 years renewable at $54, title from Shepherd G. Miller (R.O. 1710/153). Four days later Clemens sold the $54 rent to Mary K. Fink for $1,733 with a second lot (721:mdlr-ro2037-213-clemens-fink-3017-rent-1903); Fink sold it to Leopold Lehmann in 1907 (R.O. 2369/13), and his widow to the Sinclairs in 1946 (721:mdlr-mlp7060-156-lehmann-sinclair-3017-rent-1946).

Read on the scans. Randolph B. Mason assigns the 3017 leasehold to Michael G. Kilchenstein for $5 ($2 U.S. stamps, about $2,000) on April 28, 1921, reciting S.C.L. 2500/73 (S.C.L. 3785/519, recorded Oct. 5, 1921). The same day Kilchenstein mortgages it to the York Road Building Association of Baltimore City for an advance of $2,080 on 16 shares, 'being part purchase money' (S.C.L. 3785/520), and assigns it to the association by a deed of April 28, 1921, witnessed by Catherine Gossman, which was not recorded until Sept. 15, 1942, together with a confirmatory deed of May 11, 1942 (M.L.P. 6366/79 and 6366/80), both reciting the Mason deed and the $54 rent. Kilchenstein, who gave a purchase-money mortgage, was a financed buyer or the association's nominee rather than a bare straw; in 1930 he deeded a lot by Waverly Hall to Lennox B. Clemens (S.C.L. 5163/46). So the association named in the 1923 directory and in the Sunday meeting lists of 1925-26 held 3017 from 1921, under an assignment not recorded until 1942.

Read on the scan (M.L.P. 6413, pp. 491-492). J. Calvin Carney and Harry E. Parkhurst, receivers for the York Road Building Association of Baltimore City under Circuit Court No. 2 of Baltimore City in William A. Kreisel v. The York Road Building Association of Baltimore City (Docket 50A, folio 542), authorized by an order of Oct. 13, 1942 'to sell the leasehold property known as No 3017 Greenmount Avenue', sold it to Fletcher L. Vinson and Kathryn R. Vinson his wife for $5,700; the deed is dated Jan. 6, 1943 (Mary Davie, notary) and was recorded Jan. 12, 1943. 'FOR TITLE see deed from Michael G Kilchenstein to the York Road Building Association ... Liber MLP No 6366 folio 79 also Confirmatory Deed ... Liber MLP No 6366 folio 80 subject to the payment of the annual ground rent of fifty four dollars'. The same day the Vinsons mortgaged it to the Premier Building Association for $2,500 on 20 shares (M.L.P. 6413/492). With 3015 already theirs, the Vinsons now held both buildings. The leasehold of 3017 ran from Clemens Jr. (to 1909) to Randolph B. Mason (1909-21), the York Road Building Association (1921-43) and the Vinsons (from 1943); they bought the fee from Harry R. Sinclair and wife in 1951 (M.L.P. 8666/310, recited in the 1961 deed, not read). Who held the fee before Sinclair is not known. Fisher's Manual of Valuable and Worthless Securities (1946) indexes the association under 'Md. 1944'. Correction/pointer, Oct. 13, 2026: who held the 3017 reversion before the Sinclairs is read in M.L.P. 8666/310 (721:mdlr-mlp8666-310-sinclair-vinson-3017-1951): Leopold Lehman, then his widow Mary C. Lehmann (will W.J.P. 16/78; her son Ernest George died c. Jan. 13, 1924), who sold the Sinclairs on Dec. 21, 1946 (M.L.P. 7060/156); the Sinclairs sold the Vinsons the reversion on Dec. 20, 1951, merging the lease and extinguishing the $54 rent.

Read on the scan (J.F.C. 1112, pp. 129-131). July 26, 1961: Kathryn R. Milholland, unmarried, of St. Petersburg, Florida, conveys to Bryant C. Vinson and Margaret E. Vinson his wife, as tenants by the entireties, two lots: first, the 19-foot-2-inch lot, improvements known as 3017 Greenmount Avenue, held under the receivers' deed of Jan. 6, 1943 (M.L.P. 6413/491) from J. Calvin Carney et al. to Fletcher L. and Kathryn R. Vinson and under a deed of Dec. 20, 1951 (M.L.P. 8666/310) from Harry R. Sinclair and wife to the same; second, the 15-foot lot known as 3015, held under the deed of July 11, 1944 from Ella Thorington, unmarried (M.L.P. 6619/479). The recital adds that Fletcher L. Vinson died on or about Feb. 2, 1955, and that his widow, Kathryn R. Vinson, had remarried and been divorced (a 1959 Florida decree is recited). Consideration $5; U.S. documentary stamps of $30, $10, $3 and $1 ($44, about $40,000 at 55 cents per $500) and six $22 Maryland recordation stamps. The conveyance kept both lots in the family, from the founder's widow to his surviving brother, and it shows who Kathryn R. Milholland was.

The deed of Aug. 25, 1982 (CWM Jr. 4224/362, read on the page image) recites that 'MARGARET E. VINSON departed this life on or about July 17, 1968', so that title to 3015 and 3017, which she and her husband Bryant C. Vinson had taken as tenants by the entireties in 1961 (J.F.C. 1112/129), vested in him as survivor. No estate is indexed under her name in Baltimore City. The Sun's death notices of July 18, 1968 (p. 36) have not been read.

Eight volumes (1903, 1904, 1905, 1906, 1907, 1908, 1909, 1912; 1910 and 1911 are not available) print 'Rahe Louis W, shoes, 1007 York rd'; the 1909 entry continues 'h 105 Tinges la', with no '1/2' after 1007 (page image read). Der Deutsche Correspondent's list of Democratic candidates of Sept. 25, 1909 also prints 'Louis W. Rahe, Nr. 1007 York-Road'. The 1915 Sanborn plate puts 1007 on the brick office at 3015 and 1007 1/2 on the frame store at 3017, and the land records show that Charles M. Rahe bought the 15-foot lot that is 3015 in March 1902, the year before Louis W. is first listed at 1007. So the shop of these years was in the 3015 brick building: the directory lines are certain, the building is an inference from the plate and the deed. In 1907 and 1908 Rahe was also agent for a flour line at the same address ('Lewis W Rahe, agt, flour, 1007 York rd', Crescent Milling Co.).

Polk 1913 and 1914 print 'Rahe Louis W, shoes, 1009 York rd, h 105 Tinges la' (1913 page image read). The 1914 volume also prints 'Rahe Louis W, real estate, 3017 Greenmt av, h 105 Tinges la' and lists him at 3017 among real-estate agents; the 1915 volume prints 'Louis W, boots and shoes, 3017 Greenmt av, h 505 e 28th'. The Maryland Manual notary lists print 'Rahe, Louis W., 1007 York Road' for 1913-14 and '3017 Greenmount Ave.' for 1914-15 and 1915-16. 1009 York rd was a shoemakers' stand in these years: Polk lists Samuel Piazzo there in 1909, the shoemaker Louis Stoler in 1912, and the Waverly Electric Shoe Repairing Co. as well as Rahe in 1913; Stoler moved to his own shop at 3208 Greenmount in 1913. Which building 1009 was, 3017 or 3019, is not settled (Polk has the York Road Building Association at 1009 York rd in 1909 and at 3019 from 1912). The probable reading is that the shop left the 3015 brick in 1913, when the O'Mailey Mfg. Co. was already using it, and settled in the larger two-story frame store at 3017.

Polk 1915: 'Louis W, boots and shoes, 3017 Greenmt av, h 505 e 28th'; 1917: 'Rahe Louis W, shoes, 3017 Greenmt av, h 505 e 28th n' (1918, 1920 and 1921 the same, the street garbled in 1918); 1922: 'Rahe Louis W (Caroline), shoemaker, 3017 Greenmt av'. In 1923 Polk prints him as a shoemaker at 3021 Greenmount, the next frame pair to the north, and lists the York Road Bldg Assn at 3017. Polk 1915 also lists 'Wm H Rahe, shoemaker, b 505 e 28th n'. Caroline Schuman Rahe (1875-1957) is buried with him at St. John's. The National Register inventory gives the 3021 shop to the Conosenti family's shoe repair by 1928.

The Baltimore County Union (Towsontown) of Jan. 18, 1908, p. 3: 'Mrs. Sophia Bach, one of the oldest residents of Waverly and a native of Saxony', organist of St. John's Church, Waverly, 'and also for many years a teacher in the school attached to the parish'; 'Mrs. Bach is survived by two daughters, Mrs. R. D. Wing and Mrs. C. Rahe, and six grandchildren.' The St. John's churchyard has Sophia C. C. Gabler Bach, 1820-1908, and Mary E. Bach Rahe, 1846-1925, and Polk 1888 and 1908 put Sophia C. Bach at 1229 York rd (now 3427 Greenmount). Reading 'Mrs. C. Rahe' as Charles M. Rahe's widow, Mary E. (Bach) Rahe of 2 Fair Oak av, is an inference from the names.

The Sun of Sept. 16, 1904: 'Bequests of Chas. M. Rahe / Leaves Fair Oak Avenue Dwelling To Widow For Life'. The will, admitted to probate the day before (Sept. 15), gives the widow, Mrs. Mary E. Rahe, the dwelling 2 Fair Oak avenue, Waverly, with its furniture, free of taxes and repairs, for life; the residue is held in trust, the widow to receive $50 a month and the house expenses and the balance to be divided equally among the eight children, named here: Miss Sophia W. Rahe, Lewis [Louis] W. Rahe, Mrs. Eva E. Tilling, John G., Mary G., Eleanor E., Herman W. and Charles M. Rahe Jr.; John G.'s share is held in trust until he is 40; $100 marriage portions; Thomas Mackenzie is executor without bond; the will was executed Dec. 3, 1903, and the testator died Sept. 12. The Court of Appeals quotes the same will in Reilly v. MacKenzie, 151 Md. 216 (1926), and the Circuit Court's opinion below (Mackenzie v. Mackenzie, 4 Balt. C. Rep. 450, Feb. 16, 1926) gives the death date: 'The testator died on September 12th, 1904, leaving a wife, Mary E. Rahe and eight children surviving him.' This is the trust whose trustee sold the 3015 lot in 1926 (S.C.L. 4613/367); the dwelling it left the widow is the house at 600 E 31st, and Herman W. Rahe is the lessor of that lot in 1931. The page number was not captured.

The Sun's 'Permits To Build' list of Friday, Feb. 21, 1908, p. 8: '[?] G. Ridgely-One-story frame building, at 1007 York road; to cost $230.' (the first initial is cut off at the column edge). It is a city permit, so the Waverly 1007 York road. 1007 was the Rahe shoe shop, the 3015 brick. A $230 one-story frame building is the size of a shed or a rear addition (the 1928 plate shows a rear annex at 3015); it does not match the two-story frame store at 3017 (1007 1/2) as drawn in 1915. What was built is not shown.

The Sun of Sunday, Nov. 28, 1909, p. 8, 'Ground Rents, Mortgages' column: '[FOR S]ALE-Two new FIVE-YEAR RENTS, $37.50 ... L. W. RAHE, 1007 York road. n28-tf', a card run until forbidden, seen through Dec. 1. The election had been held on Nov. 2. It shows the shoemaker and delegate already dealing in ground rents from the 3015 shop, four years before the directories call him a real-estate agent.

An 11-day run in the Sun and Evening Sun from May 17 to 27, 1911 (Sun image 372816246; Evening Sun 365458384), repeated in July (Sun, July 23, 1911, p. 4, image 373380116; Evening Sun, July 24, 1911, image 365481890): '9-ROOM MODERN COTTAGE-Gas and electric lights, front and side porch; lot 75x150; for $22.50 per month, or will sell for $1,900; $300 cash, balance on mortgage; ground rent $75; corner Poplar and Foster ave., Govans; take Towson car; two squares east of Lake Station. L. W. RAHE, 1007 York road. Phone, Mad. 4272.'

The Sun's marriage licences of Jan. 18, 1912, p. 8: 'STOLER-GABAU.-Louis Stoler, 24, 1007 York road; Lena Gabau, 20.' Polk 1912 lists 'Stoler Louis, shoemkr, 1009 York rd, h 1208 e Fayette' (and Louis Stoler, 1009 York rd, in its list of shoemakers); Polk 1909 has him at 1306 Harford av, and Polk 1913 and 1915 at his own shop, 3208 Greenmount. So the licensee is probably the shoemaker Louis Stoler, who had a shoe stand at 1009 York rd in 1912 (the licence prints 1007, the Rahe shop's number) before opening at 3208. He died in 1943; his wife, Lena Stoler, a merchant at 3208 Greenmount, declared for citizenship in 1926.

Polk 1913 (page image read, leaf 1444): "O'Mailey Mnfg Co (John A O'Mailey), flavoring extracts, 3015 Greenmt av" and "O'Mailey John A (O'Mailey Mnfg Co), h 426 e 21st n". The firm is not in Polk 1912, which lists John A. O'Mailey only at 2103 E. Madison St., nor in 1914 or 1915. Its newspaper advertisements give 3015 Greenmount from Sept. 22, 1912 (salesmen for extracts) to January 1913 (shoe polish). So the tenancy ran from about September 1912 into 1913, in the 3015 brick after the Rahe shoe shop moved next door, and it is the earliest use found of the number 3015, while Polk still printed the old York road numbers. The O'Mailey family had been leather dealers ('O'Mailey John & Co', 221 S. Sharp St., Polk 1908). No charter or trademark was found for the firm.

A help-wanted line in the Sun of Sept. 22, 1912, p. 3: 'WANTED-SALESMEN to call on Grocery and Saloon trade; extracts; 25% commission. O'MAILEY MFG. CO., 3015 Greenmount ave.' The same address appears in both Baltimore papers on Jan. 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16, 1913. This is the earliest print found of the number 3015. The wording comes from the newspaper's search index; the page has not been read in full.

The Sun of Tuesday, Jan. 14, 1913, p. 11 (run 'j14-6t', six days): 'WANTED-SALESMAN to carry as a side line 5c. Self-Shining Shoe Polish; liberal commission. O'MAILEY, 3015 Greenmount ave.' With the September 1912 extracts advertisement, the O'Mailey Mfg. Co. made or sold both flavoring extracts and shoe polish from the former Rahe shoe shop; the O'Mailey family had been leather dealers (Polk 1908).

The Sun of March 11, 1914, p. 10 (run 'm10-6t'): '4 A-1 GROUND RENTS, $45.50 EACH, on 2-story brick dwellings, 1739 and 43 Belt ave., 16[3]2 and 34 Jackson ave., South Balto.; 6% less title fee. L. W. Rahe, 3017 Greenmount ave.' It is the earliest print found of the new number for the Rahe business (Polk still printed 1009 York rd in 1913 and 1914), and it shows the business dealing in ground rents as much as shoes. Also the Evening Sun of April 20, 1918, p. 12: '9-ROOM COTTAGE, all conveniences, $1,600; g. r., $50, 428 CALVIN AVE. Apply L. W. RAHE, 3017 Greenmount ave.'

Polk 1914: 'Fowler Lawrence, conductor, 3017 Greenmt av' (page image checked); Polk 1915: 'Fowler C Lawrence, sexton, 3017 Greenmt av', with Adelaide M. Fowler, teacher, at the same address. A sexton is a church officer; St. John's Episcopal Church stands about 200 feet south and the Waverly M.E. church across the road, but neither church's sexton is named in the sources searched.

Polk 1917: 'Rainy Day Perm Savings and Loan Assn, 3015 Greenmt av' (alphabetical and classified lists); 1918: 'Rainy Day Perm Bldg and Loan Assn, 3015 Greenmt av'; 1920: both forms. By 1921 the association is at 501 E. 20th St. (Polk 1921 to 1923). Nothing is listed at 3015 in Polk between the O'Mailey firm (1913) and the Rainy Day. The building is the 15-foot brick 'Office' of the 1915 Sanborn plate; the lenders follow the Rahe shoe shop's move next door.
Polk 1917 and 1918: 'Pisani Annie Mrs, h 3017 Greenmt av' (the 1918 OCR garbles the name as 'Basano'); 1920 and 1921: 'Pisani Anna C, stenogr, 3017 Greenmt av' and 'Annie Mrs'.

Manufacturers Record, vol. 79, no. 21 (May 26, 1921), new financial corporations: 'Md., Baltimore.-Civic Building & Loan Assn., 3015 Greenmount Ave., capital $1,300,000 incptd. by Rodney J. Brooks, John J. Kernan, Edward B. Smith.' The figure is the authorised capital. Polk 1922 and 1923 list the Civic at 3015. The text was read in the archive's OCR.

Manufacturers Record, vol. 79, no. 8 (Feb. 24, 1921): 'Md., Baltimore.-Waverly-Guilford Building & Loan Assn., 2 Greenmount Ave., capital $20,000, incptd. with Harry B. Onion, Arthur B. Thompson, Gordon Gambrill.' The printed address is '2 Greenmount Ave.', probably truncated in print or in the OCR; Polk 1922 and 1923 put the Waverly-Guilford Bldg Assn at 3015 Greenmount. It is named for the two neighborhoods it served.

The Baltimore County Union, the Towson News, of Nov. 13, 1909, p. 2: Augustus D. Clemens Jr. died on Wednesday (Nov. 10); he 'was a director of the York Road Building Association and of the Waverly Building Association, and a member of the Maryland Historical Society, the St. Andrew's Society, the Royal Arcanum, the Heptasophs and Concordia Lodge of Masons'; a son of the late Augustus D. Clemens; educated in the public schools and the old Newton Academy; 'He helped in developing many of the northern suburbs, including Waverly, Oxford ...'. He was born Jan. 17, 1845, lived at 'Evesham' in Govanstown, and is buried at St. John's. The tie to this parcel is in the land records: Clemens Jr. sold the 3015 lot to Charles M. Rahe in 1902 and assigned the 3017 leasehold in May 1909, and the York Road Building Association bought 3017 in 1921.

The Sunday Sun's 1925 and 1926 runs are a paid directory of building and loan associations with their meeting nights; one line reads 'York Road Building and Loan Assn. / 3017 Greenmount Ave. / Wednesday' (Sun, April 19, 1925, p. 32; the same list weekly from April 19 to June 28, 1925 and from Jan. 31 to April 18, 1926). The association, named the York Road Building Association of Baltimore City in its deeds, met in the 3017 frame store it had bought in 1921 and would lose to receivers in 1942-43. A Sun advertisement of June 3, 1928 places a 'York Rd. Building & Loan Assn.' at 3117 Greenmount, so the association may have moved its meetings by then.

Death notice, Sun of Saturday, April 23, 1932, p. 16 (also Evening Sun, April 22, p. 51, and April 23, p. 13): 'RAHE.-On April 21, 1932, LOUIS W., beloved husband of Caroline S. Rahe (nee Schuman). Funeral from his home, 505 East Twenty-eighth street, on Saturday afternoon. Services at St. John's P. E. Church, Greenmount avenue and Thirtieth street, at 4 o'clock. Interment in church cemetery.' It gives the death date, his wife's maiden name and burial in the St. John's churchyard, a few doors south of 3015.

A Bureau of Buildings legal notice dated April 20, 1927, run three times from April 26 (this printing the Sun of April 28, 1927, p. 27): M. Schapiro has applied under the Building Code 'to use premises 3015 Greenmount Avenue for dog and cat hospital'. The title to 3015 was then in the name of Harry S. Schapiro (deed of Aug. 3, 1926); the tie to the Schapiro Realty of the 1928 rental advertisement is an inference. It is the earliest printed tie between 3015 and an animal hospital, and it falls in the year Kummer (1941) gives for Dr. Fletcher Vinson's arrival, but the applicant is Schapiro, so the notice proves the permitted use, not the operator.

The Sun of Tuesday, May 3, 1927, p. 21, under the headline 'Cat And Dog Hospital Approved By Osborne / Greenmount Avenue Project Sanctioned - Four Other Permits Granted': a permit for a dog and cat hospital at 3015 Greenmount avenue was approved the day before (May 2) by Charles H. Osborne, head of the Bureau of Buildings, who said he approved the application, filed by M. Schapiro, because the building was in a first commercial zone.

A classified advertisement run daily in the Sun and Evening Sun from Feb. 1 to 9, 1928 (17 pages; this printing the Evening Sun of Feb. 1, p. 30): 'STORES, NEW-RENTS, $90 AND $120. 3015 Greenmount Ave.-124 E. Wylie Ave. Schapiro Realty, 923 W. North ave.' The advertisement offers two properties and does not say which rent goes with which. Schapiro Realty is a Schapiro firm; the title to 3015 was in Harry S. Schapiro's name. 'New' fits a rebuilding or new front of the 3015 brick in 1927 (the 1928 Sanborn labels 3015 a store), and the advertisement shows that early in 1928 the space was not a working animal hospital.

Help-wanted lines put a barber shop at 3015 in the months after the Schapiro rental advertisement: 'BARBER, MUST BE STEADY. 3015 GREENMOUNT AVE.' (Sun, Sunday, Sept. 9, 1928, p. 44) and 'BARBER WANTED. APPLY 3015 GREENMOUNT AVE.' (Sun, Wednesday, April 10, 1929, p. 27, image 373484536). No barber's name is printed. The National Register inventory's reading of the 1928 directory as a dry goods store at 3015 remains untraced.

The practice's number, Belmont 5374 (first printed in the opening notice of March 1931), recurs in the classifieds without an address: 'DOCTOR'S Instrument Case lost. Black, initials F. L. V. Reward. Call Belmont 5374.' (Sun, Jan. 14, 1935, p. 12), which ties the number to Dr. Fletcher L. Vinson; 'HIGHLY Pedigreed English Setter Puppies, $50. Belmont 5374 or Towson 76-J.' (Sun, April 18, 1935, p. 22); a lost blue belton English setter named 'Rummey', strayed 'from my home on Woodholme ave.', with the owner, I. N. Grinsfelder, or 'Dr. F. L. Vincent, Belmont 5374' to be notified (Sun, Feb. 20, 1938, p. 25); and 'PEKINGESE (2), males, 6 mos. Pedigreed. Belmont 5374.' (Sun, Dec. 8, 1940, p. 49). The setter puppies are possibly of Dr. Vinson's Rockboro line.

The Evening Sun of Wednesday, Feb. 2, 1955, p. 38: Dr. Fletcher L. Vinson, 57, 'widely known veterinarian and dog-show judge', died that morning at Union Memorial Hospital after a heart attack ten days earlier. 'Born in Alabama in 1897, Dr. Vinson was graduated from Alabama Polytechnic Institute in 1918, and came to Baltimore in 1931, establishing an animal hospital.' He was a member of the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners, president of the English Setters Association of America and of the Baltimore County Kennel Club, and a member of the American Animal Hospital Association and the AVMA; he lived at Glen Arm, where he raised prize cattle. Survivors: his wife, Mrs. Katherine Robertson Vinson, a daughter, a sister, Ethel Vinson, and 'a brother, Dr. Curtis B. Vinson', who is Dr. Bryant Curtis Vinson with the names reversed. The Sun's longer obituary of Feb. 3, 1955 (p. 17) says his services to pets had 'endeared him to thousands of Baltimoreans for almost 24 years' (that is, from 1931), that 'His hospital in the 3000 block of Greenmount avenue was widely known as a treatment center for small animals, especially cats and dogs', that he helped organize the Baltimore Kennel Club, and that the funeral would be on Saturday, Feb. 5, at Trinity Protestant Episcopal Church in the Long Green Valley, with burial in its churchyard. Find a Grave (memorial 54520050) gives Fletcher Leroy Vinson, Aug. 4, 1897 to Feb. 2, 1955, buried at Trinity Episcopal Church Cemetery, Glen Arm, and links a wife, Margaret Cotton Vinson (1895-1971), probably the Margaret C. Vinson of the 1934 deed. The 1931 date fits the hospital's opening (at 3013, March 1931), not his arrival: the AVMA journal of October 1929 lists him at 426 W. North Ave., Baltimore. The AVMA journal of April 1955 misdates his death to Feb. 3.

Engineering News-Record, vol. 158, no. 10 (March 7, 1957), bid results: 'Sullivan Constr. Co., 3015 Greenmount Ave., Baltimore 18, Md. LB $77,696 (7 bidders) Contr. 541 S, Catonsville Intercepting Sewer, First District, TOWSON, MD. ... Bids Feb. 15.' A second OCR copy reads $77,698. Nothing else was found on the firm or on why it used the animal hospital's address.

Maryland SDAT entity records, read through the marylanddb.com mirror and OpenCorporates: Vinson's Animal Hospital, Inc., D00576041, articles F2177/289, May 21, 1975, forfeited Oct. 8, 2004; Vinson's Kennels, Inc., D02038248, articles F2763/1863, Nov. 26, 1985, forfeited Oct. 8, 2004; Vinson's Animal Hospital At Towson, Inc., D03778206, articles F3565/2436, Nov. 30, 1993, active. The kennels corporation was chartered twelve weeks before it received the three lots from the hospital corporation (deed of Feb. 14, 1986, SEB 851/315), and both older corporations were forfeited four days after the foreclosure deed of Oct. 4, 2004 was recorded. The hospital corporation was chartered in 1975, the year Dr. Bryant C. Vinson retired; no earlier charter for the practice was found.

The Evening Sun of Friday, June 18, 1982, p. 47: services for Dr. Bryant C. Vinson, 'who operated a veterinary hospital in Waverly for more than 20 years before his retirement in 1975', at the Lassahn funeral establishment, 7401 Belair road. He was 72 and died on Wednesday (June 16) of cancer at his home in the 3300 block of Beverly road. 'He joined two older brothers in practicing at the hospital in the 3000 block Greenmount avenue in 1930 after graduating from the Auburn University veterinary school.' He was president of the Baltimore County Kennel Club for many years, a life member of the American and Maryland State veterinary associations, a native of Loachapoka, Ala., a Mason (Highland Lodge, Scottish Rite, Boumi Temple), and a supporter of animal research at Cornell and at the Auburn veterinary school. Survivors included a sister and a nephew, Dr. Edmund H. James Jr. of Towson, the hospital's long-time associate. Kummer (1941) says the family had two sons and a daughter, so 'two older brothers' is probably an error of the obituary. The obituary also names a surviving wife, although the 1982 deed recites that his co-owner of 1961, Margaret E. Vinson, died on or about July 17, 1968; whether he remarried is not shown. The Register of Wills of Baltimore City indexes his estate as No. 123691, filed July 8, 1982, date of death June 16, 1982. Find a Grave (memorial 270514793) gives Bryant Curtis Vinson, Aug. 9, 1909 to June 16, 1982, buried at Dulaney Valley Memorial Gardens, Timonium. His retirement year, 1975, is the year Vinson's Animal Hospital, Inc. was chartered.

The Johns Hopkins News-Letter of June 2, 1995 (vol. 99, no. 26), repeated Sept. 8, 1995 (vol. 100, no. 1), walks the avenue block by block: '3000 block, odd ... Vinson's Animal Hospital. Just in case your pet gets sick'. The guide names the block, not the number; 3015 is the hospital's address in every other source of the period, and the Vinson's Kennels corporation held the building until 2004. A corporation named Vinson's Animal Hospital At Towson, Inc. had been chartered in 1993.

The Baltimore Sun of Saturday, Jan. 9, 2021, p. 3, Jacques Kelly's column 'Life anew is coming for Waverly's tarnished town hall', on the 1870 Waverly Hall at Greenmount and 31st: 'Not far down the street, the former Vinson animal hospital building has been painted in a playful mural that, among other things, pays homage to the No. 8 streetcar and Goetze caramel cremes.' It dates the mural to January 2021 or earlier and names two of its motifs.

The east side of Greenmount Avenue from 3009 to 3229 is on sheet 718 of the 1915 Sanborn atlas, Baltimore Vol. 7 (the index line reads 'Greenmount Ave 3009-3229 *718'; sheet 717 is the west side). The plate prints the old York road number beside the new one on each lot: 1005/3013, a one-story frame store; 1007/3015, a brick building with 8-inch walls, one story, labelled 'Office', with a one-story frame strip at the front and a one-story brick rear annex running back to Old York Road; 1007 1/2 / 3017, a two-story frame store about 50 feet deep; then the two-story frame 'Office' pair at 3019 and 3021. The story figure on 3015 is smudged by an overprint and reads 1 (possibly 1 1/2). Old York Road crosses the rear of both lots on the diagonal. The half number suggests that 3017 was numbered after the brick building at 1007.

Known from the recital in every later description of the 3015 lot (1902, 1982, 2001, 2004, 2016): the 3015 lot begins 175 feet 7 inches south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot and runs 15 feet south 'to the northwest corner of a lot of ground conveyed by Augustus D. Clemens, Jr., and wife, to William L. Fink, by Deed dated April 12, 1898', recorded in Liber R.O. No. 1729, folio 241. The 3013 lot's own description (R.H.B. 3116/428, 1974; F.M.C. 9050, p. 275, 2007) begins exactly there, 190 feet 7 inches south of the same stone, and runs 14 feet south. So the Fink lot is 3013, the lot the 1915 Sanborn plate numbers 1005 York road. The 3015 lot was 'a portion of the ground' Clemens Jr. had bought from a Keller, widower, on Dec. 20, 1897 (R.O. 1710/105, recited in the 1902 deed); the Fink lot very probably came out of the same purchase. The buyer was very probably the William L. Fink whom Polk lists in Waverly from 1889 to 1892: 'fancy gds, 1039 York rd, h 845 do' (1889), then 'dry gds, 1047 York rd, h 845 do' (1890-92). Woods and Polk carry a William L. Fink as a shoemaker and shoe dealer downtown from 1865 to 1888 (East Lombard, East Baltimore and North Eutaw streets), probably the same man. Bertha Fink kept a dry goods store on the lot, at 1005 York road, from 1901 to 1904, with her home at the same 845 York road, so she belonged to his household. A William L. Fink died July 8, 1946 (Baltimore City estate OLD45631); whether he is the grantee is not known. The deed itself has not been read. Correction/pointer, Oct. 13, 2026: the deed is read (720:mdlr-ro1729-241-clemens-fink-1898, R.O. 1729/241): it is dated April 18, 1898 and recorded April 20 (not April 12); the price is $500, fee simple; and the parent ground came from Shepard G. Miller, widower, by a deed of Dec. 20, 1897 at R.O. 1710/153, not from 'a Keller' at 1710/105.

Polk 1888: 'Rahe Chas M, shoes, 1001 York rd' (home 'h 2 Fair'); 1889: 'C M, 1001 York rd'; 1890: 'Rahe Chas M, shoes, 1001 York rd, h 2 Fair', with Lewis W. Rahe, clerk, at 1001 York rd; 1891: Paul Rahe, clerk, at 1001 York rd; 1892: 'Rahe Louis W, shoemkr, 2 Fair Oak av'; 1901: 'Rahe Louis W, shoemkr, 1001 York rd' (the volumes of 1893 to 1900 are not available). 1001 York rd is placed at 3011 through the Sinclair tin shop, listed at 1001 York rd in 1907-13 and at 3011 Greenmount in 1915-23; the 1915 Sanborn plate prints 1001 and 1003 on the two-story brick plumbing and tin shop without a Greenmount number, so the equation comes from the directories, not the plate. By Polk 1903 the Rahe shop is at 1007 York rd, the 3015 brick, on a lot Charles M. Rahe bought in March 1902. Woods directories of 1871 to 1886 list Charles Rahe, shoemaker, at Waverly from 1871 and Louis W. from 1881, without house numbers.

The Baltimore County Union (Towsontown) of March 15, 1879, p. 4, carries the card of 'CHARLES H. RAHE, manufacturer of all boots and shoes, E. Waverly, In the forks of the Old York Road and the Pike. Boots and shoes made to order at short notice. Satisfaction guaranteed. Also a full assortment of ready-made goods ... Repairing done in the best manner.' The run code ('Jan.18,'78.-ly') dates its first insertion to January 1878; the 'ESTABLISHED 1865' printed below it belongs to the next advertiser. The OCR prints the middle initial H.; the Woods and Polk directories give Chas M. Rahe. The card gives no street number: 'the forks' is the whole wedge between the Pike (Greenmount Avenue) and Old York Road, which holds 3011 to 3021, so it does not place the 1879 shop on a particular lot.

The Vinson practice's first dated print is an opening notice in the pets column of the Evening Sun of Wednesday, March 25, 1931 (p. 37): 'ANNOUNCING the opening of a new Modern Small Animal Hospital. DR. B. C. VINSON, 3013 Greenmount ave. Belmont 5374.' A one-line card, 'VINSON'S SMALL ANIMAL HOSPITAL, 3013 GREENMOUNT AVE. BELMONT 5374.', then ran daily in both papers to about May 21, 1931, and again from Nov. 5 to 12, 1931; every print examined reads 3013 (Evening Sun, April 17, 1931, p. 69; Sun, April 17, 1931, p. 23; Sun, April 25, 1931, p. 21, the clearest). 3013 is the lot next south of 3015. The practice was still at 3013 in August 1934, when the Twelfth International Veterinary Congress listed 'Vinson, F. L., 3013 Greenmount Avenue, Baltimore'; it is at 3015 from September 1935, a year after Dr. Fletcher L. Vinson bought that lot (Sept. 18, 1934).

A camera dealer list in the Sun of Sept. 21, 1965, p. 8, prints 'Service Photo Supply / 3011 Greenmount Avenue / Baltimore, Md.', below Zepp Photo Centers at the Towson Shopping Center. The last print of the firm at 3017 found is the Evening Sun of March 9, 1965, p. 20 ('SERVICE PHOTO SUPPLY CO., INC. 3017 Greenmount Ave.'). The move from 3017 to 3011 therefore probably falls between March and September 1965, which fits the change of telephone (HO. 7-2595 in 1962; BE 5-6200 in the 1966 yearbook advertisements) and the charter of Camera Corner, Inc. at 3011 in November 1964; the earliest 3011 print has not been dated.

OpenCorporates' copy of the Maryland record: Service Photo Supply, Inc., D00194456, articles of incorporation May 24, 1967; change of resident agent address Feb. 9, 1972; forfeited by proclamation Oct. 7, 1981; articles of revival April 17, 1986; articles of amendment June 20, 1991; status revived, with its registered agent at 3011 Greenmount Avenue and its principal office now at 3838 Falls Road. The shop was printed as Service Photo Supply Co. at 3017 Greenmount from 1955 to March 1965 and at 3011 by September 1965, probably moving between those dates; its telephone changed with it, from HO. 7-2595 (1962) to BE 5-6200 (1966). Printed 3011 listings follow: the Paillard (Sinar) dealer list of 1966; Loyola's Evergreen annual of 1966 and 1967; The Quaker of 1969 to 1971; Bawlamer (1976); The Greyhound (1990). The Better Business Bureau gives the business a 1965 start. Camera Corner, Inc. (D00070524), chartered Nov. 27, 1964, also at 3011, was forfeited in 1987.

Recited in the description of the 3017 lot (1909, 1961, 1982, 2016): the lot begins 'at the southwest corner of a lot leased by Augustus D. Clemens, Jr., to Jacob H. Aull recorded in Liber R.O. No. 1728 folio 284'. The lease is undated in every copy; folio 284 of Liber 1728 falls one book before the Fink deed of April 12, 1898 (R.O. 1729/241), so it was recorded about the spring of 1898. Jacob H. Aull (died Oct. 12, 1921) was the Waverly builder and real-estate man. The leased lot is 3019, where Polk lists the York Road Building Association from 1912 to 1922. The lease itself has not been read. Correction/pointer, Oct. 13, 2026: the lease is read (722:mdlr-ro1728-284-clemens-aull-lease-1898, R.O. 1728/284): April 14, 1898, 99 years at $60 a year, 33 feet on the turnpike from 123 ft 5 in south of the two-mile stone; the reversion and rent were sold to Henry D. Konig for $1,000 the same day (R.O. 1728/286, 722:mdlr-ro1728-286-clemens-konig-rent-1898).

The photo-supply shop occupied the 3017 frame store for about ten years. A camera dealers' list in the Sun of May 15, 1955, p. 193, prints 'Service Photo.......3017 Greenmount' beside 'Zepp Photo Supply..3042 Greenmount'; a classified card in the Sun of Thursday, April 5, 1962, p. 48 reads 'CAMERAS-Service photo Supply Co., 3017 Greenmount. HO. 7-2595.' (the 7 is clean at full size); and a dealer list in the Evening Sun of March 9, 1965, p. 20 prints 'SERVICE PHOTO SUPPLY CO., INC. 3017 Greenmount Ave.', the last 3017 print found. By September 1965 the firm was at 3011 Greenmount, a few doors south, where it was incorporated in 1967.

Lease dated Dec. 6, 1912, acknowledged that day before a Baltimore County notary and recorded Dec. 16, 1912 (Stephen C. Little, clerk), read on the page image of the handwritten record copy: Jacob H. Aull and Mary A. J. Aull, his wife, of Baltimore County, to Alice M. Chapman of Baltimore City, 'all those four lots of ground' on the west side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly the York Turnpike Road) at Vineyard Lane (formerly Gilmor Lane). The first lot is the corner, 15 ft on the avenue and 82 ft deep to a 4-ft alley (3026); the second, third and fourth are 14 x 82 ft lots beginning 15, 29 and 43 ft north of the lane (3028, 3030, 3032), the fourth running to the northernmost outline of the lot the Baltimore and Yorktown Turnpike Road company deeded to Aull on March 6, 1912 (S.C.L. 2727/29). Each lot is bounded through the partition wall between 'the house erected on the lot now being described' and its neighbour, so the four houses stood by Dec. 6, 1912. Term 99 years from Dec. 1, 1912, renewable forever on a $1 fine; rent $72 a year on the corner lot and $66 on each of the other three, half-yearly on June 1 and Dec. 1. Ten days later, on the day this lease was recorded, Aull sold the four rents to Frank X. Hooper (S.C.L. 2787/376), whose deed says the lease was 'recorded prior to the execution hereof'. The lease does not say that Chapman was a nominee, but the pattern, a lease to an individual followed by the sale of the rents while Aull himself advertised and sold the houses from 1913, is the usual one for a Baltimore builder creating ground rents. The date: the lease's own date line and Aull's deed to Hooper say Dec. 6, as does a 1975 recital (R.H.B. 3207/655); the 1945 deed of the 3028 rent recites the lease as 'December 12th 1912' (M.L.P. 6799/549). Lot one, 3026, is the separate parcel next door. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].

Deed dated, acknowledged and recorded Dec. 16, 1912 (Stephen C. Little, clerk), read on the page image of the handwritten record copy: Jacob H. Aull and Mary A. J. Aull, of Baltimore County, 'in consideration of the sum of forty five hundred dollars', to 'Frank X. Hooper of the County of Baltimore', in fee simple, 'all those four lots tracts and parcels of ground' (3026, 3028, 3030 and 3032, described as in the lease), 'being also the same land which by lease dated the 6th day of December and recorded prior to the execution hereof was demised and leased' to Alice M. Chapman for 99 years renewable forever at $72 a year on the first lot and $66 on each of the others, to hold 'the above granted property and particularly the aforesaid rents or reversions'. So Hooper bought the four ground rents, $270 a year in all, subject to the 99-year term, and not the houses. $4,500 is exactly $270 capitalized at 6 per cent (16 2/3 years' purchase). This is the transfer the Sun printed on Dec. 17, 1912 as four lots sold to F. X. Hooper 'for $4,500 in fee'. The houses stayed under the lease, which is why 'AULL, 210 East Lexington st.' could advertise 3026 and 3028 for sale in July 1913 and Aull could sell houses of the row subject to ground rent in 1917 and 1918. Hooper, called Francis X. Hooper in his will of Sept. 14, 1916 (recorded with the Register of Wills for Baltimore County), had died by 1945, when Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore, his surviving trustee, sold the 3028 rent to the Freitags (M.L.P. 6799/549). In 1964 'Mercantile-Safe Deposit and Trust Company, Trustee' sold the 3032 rent to David Siegel (recited in R.H.B. 3207/655), very probably the same trust under the bank's later name. A buyer of Baltimore County fits the F. X. Hooper of Glen Arm proposed from the Sun's transfer columns. Deed dated Dec. 27, 1944, read on the page image (grantee-index stamp Feb. 15, 1945): Daisy E. Masbach of Baltimore City to William F. Freitag Sr. and Belle H. Freitag, his wife, for $5 and other considerations, the lot 15 ft north of Vineyard Lane, 14 ft front through the partition walls and 82 ft deep to a 4-ft alley, 'the improvements thereon being known as No 3028 Greenmount Avenue', for the residue of the renewable term, subject to the annual rent of $66 payable June 1 and Dec. 1. Stamps: '$4.40 USS' and '$4.00 MDS'. At the federal rate of 55 cents per $500, $4.40 is eight units, a price over $3,500 and up to $4,000; the $4.00 of Maryland stamps fits $4,000. Recital: Masbach had the lot from Charles Morris (middle initial unclear on the scan, probably E.) and Lilly M. Morris, his wife, by deed of Jan. 13, 1925 (S.C.L. 4324/204, not read); Polk 1922 and 1923 list Chas. E. Morris, motorman, at 3028. J. Holliday Riepe, Inc. had reported the sale of the 'apartment dwelling' at 3028 to William Freitag in the Sun of Dec. 10, 1944. The land records print the buyer as William F. Freitag Sr. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Masbach's 1925 purchase is read (726:mdlr-scl4324-204-morris-masbach-3028-1925): from Charles E. and Lilly M. Morris, who had it from Lawrence W. Sanner and wife in 1921 (S.C.L. 3770/255).

Deed dated Sept. 18, 1945, recorded Sept. 24, 1945 (M. Luther Pittman, clerk), read on the page image: Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore, 'surviving trustee under the last Will and Testament of Francis X Hooper deceased sometimes called Frank X Hooper dated September 14 1916' (recorded with the Register of Wills for Baltimore County), under the will's power of sale, to William F. Freitag Sr. and Belle H. Freitag, his wife, for $1,100, the 3028 lot (15 ft north of Vineyard Lane, 14 x 82 ft). $1,100 is exactly the $66 rent capitalized at 6 per cent; the margin carries '$1.65 USS' (three units of $500 at 55 cents, which fits $1,100) and '$1.10 MDS'. Recitals: the lot is 'secondly described' in the 99-year lease from Jacob H. Aull and wife to Alice M. Chapman at $66 a year (S.C.L. 2787/374) and in Aull's deed of Dec. 16, 1912 to Hooper, 'who is in said deed called Frank X Hooper' (S.C.L. 2787/376); the grantees already held the leasehold from Daisy E. Masbach (M.L.P. 6688/415, Dec. 27, 1944). The deed is made 'to the end and intent that the leasehold and reversionary interests in said lot may be merged and the aforesaid rent may be forever extinguished', so from here 3028 was held in fee, as the 1975 deed says. This deed dates the Chapman lease 'December 12th 1912'; the lease itself, Aull's 1912 deed to Hooper and a 1975 recital all say Dec. 6.

Deed dated Aug. 1, 1947, read on the page image of the typed record copy: William F. Freitag Sr. and Belle H. Freitag, his wife, to Freitag's Inc, 3028 Greenmount Avenue in fee simple, for $5. Margin '$6.05 USS CAN / $6.05 MDS CAN': at 55 cents per $500, eleven units, a value over $5,000 and up to $5,500. Recital: 'for reversionary title see Deed dated September 18 1945 ... Liber MLP No 6799 folio 549 from Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore surviving trustee etc to grantors FOR leasehold title see Deed dated December 27 1944 ... Liber MLP No 6688 folio 415 etc from Daisy E Masbach to the grantors'. Two years later the company deeded the house to the family's music-school partnership (M.L.P. 7862/252).

Deed dated Aug. 15, 1949, read on the page image ('No stamps required'): Freitag's, Inc., a body corporate, to William F. Freitag, Sr., Belle H. Freitag and Charles C. Freitag, co-partners trading as Freitag's School of Music, 3028 in fee simple, for $5. Recital: the Aug. 1, 1947 deed from William F. Freitag, Sr. and Belle H. Freitag to Freitag's, Inc. (M.L.P. 7217/125). From 1949 the music school's partnership held the house it occupied. The 1969 straw deed says William Sr. withdrew from the partnership by a deed of Oct. 26, 1955 (M.L.P. 9947/118, recited) and Belle H. and Charles C. Freitag carried it on; later deeds spell the firm 'Freitag School of Music'.

Deed dated March 14, 1951, recorded March 15, 1951 (M. Luther Pittman, clerk), read on the page image: Robert F. Podlich, unmarried, of Anne Arundel County, to William F. Freitag, Sr. and Belle H. Freitag, his wife, for $5 and other considerations, in fee simple, the lot 29 ft north of Vineyard Lane (formerly Gilmor Lane), 14 x 82 ft: 'No. 3030 Greenmount Avenue'. It is the lot described in a 99-year lease 'of even date' from Podlich to Marie B. Pipitone at $90 a year, payable March 15 and Sept. 15 (the lease, recorded just before, was not opened), and the Freitags take 'particularly the aforesaid rent payable out of said lot, and the reversion thereto', subject to the lessee's term. Stamps: Maryland $1.10 and 55 cents, $1.65 in all, which at 55 cents per $500 means a price over $1,000 and up to $1,500; federal stamps of $1, 50 cents and 10 cents are visible and a fourth is cut off at the frame. $1,500, the most the stamps allow, is the $90 rent capitalized at 6 per cent. The same day Pipitone assigned the leasehold to the Freitag School of Music partnership (M.L.P. 8386/77). So the $90 rent on 3030, still recited in 1975 and later, was created on this day, and Belle H. Freitag held it in 1975 (R.H.B. 3207/653). No earlier deed is recited for Podlich's title, and how the 1912 rent of $66 on 3030 came to an end before 1951 has not been read. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Podlich's 1951 purchase is read (726:mdlr-mlp8386-70-interrante-podlich-3030-1951): from Nicholas Interrante, whose 1944 reversion came from Charles T. and Ella B. Leight (M.L.P. 6549/554) and 1943 leasehold from Helen M. Bordley. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (late): the Leight deed is M.L.P. 6549/594, not 554, and is read (726:mdlr-mlp6549-594-leight-interrante-3030-rent-1944): the $66 rent the Interrantes bought in 1944 was created by the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County's lease to Helen M. Bordley of Feb. 25, 1935 (S.C.L. 5518/171), not by the 1912 Aull lease. The end of the 1912 rent on 3030 is still unread.

Deed of even date, March 14, 1951, read on the page image (margin 'No State or Federal Stamps Required'): Marie B. Pipitone of Baltimore City to William F. Freitag, Sr. and Belle H. Freitag, his wife, and Charles C. Freitag, co-partners trading as Freitag School of Music, for $5, the leasehold of 3030 Greenmount Avenue (29 ft north of Vineyard Lane, 14 x 82 ft) under the lease of the same day from Robert F. Podlich to her, for the residue of the term 'with the right and benefit of renewal forever'. With M.L.P. 8386/75 this is the Baltimore pattern of a ground-rent sale through an intermediary lessee: the owner leases to the intermediary, sells the rent, and the intermediary assigns the house the same day without stamps. The Freitags bought both halves of 3030 at once, the rent in the spouses' names and the house in the partnership's, next door to the 3028 house the partnership already owned.

Deed dated April 1, 1969, read on the page image: Belle H. Freitag and Charles C. Freitag, co-partners trading as Freitag School of Music, to Deborah C. Zimmerman, for $1, no stamps, 3028 (fee) and 3030 (leasehold under the $90 rent). Recitals: 3028 from Freitag's, Inc. by the Aug. 15, 1949 deed (M.L.P. 7862/252) to William F. Freitag, Sr., Belle H. Freitag and Charles C. Freitag, then partners; 3030 by assignment from Marie B. Pipitone of March 14, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/77); and 'By Deed dated October 26, 1955 ... Liber M.L.P. No. 9947, Folio 118, the said William F. Freitag, Sr., having withdrawn and relinquished his interest in the aforementioned partnership', conveyed his interest to Belle H. and Charles C. Freitag, who continued the partnership. The same day the intermediary deeded both lots to Charles C. Freitag alone (R.H.B. 2497/414): a straw pair that moved the two houses out of the partnership into his name.

Deed dated April 1, 1969, recorded April 2, 1969 (Robert H. Bouse, clerk), read on the page image: Deborah C. Zimmerman, unmarried, to Charles C. Freitag, for $1, 'NO STAMPS OR TRANSFER TAX REQUIRED', 'NO TITLE EXAMINATION', the lots 15 and 29 ft north of Vineyard Lane, each 14 x 82 ft: 3028 in fee and 3030 'subject to the payment of the annual ground rent of Ninety ($90.00) Dollars, payable half-yearly ... on the 15th day of March and September'. Recital: the deed of even date from Belle H. Freitag and Charles C. Freitag, co-partners trading as Freitag School of Music, to the grantor (R.H.B. 2497/410). This is the deed that Charles C. Freitag's 1975 deed to People's Free Medical Clinic recites (R.H.B. 3207/657).

Subordination agreement dated Feb. 14, 1975 and recorded with the closing papers of Feb. 19, 1975 (Title Guarantee Co. application H-85818, the same file as the deeds), read on the page image: 'Belle H. Freitag is the reversionary owner for all that lot of ground known as No. 3030 Greenmount Avenue subject to an annual rent of $90, payable on the 15th days of March and September by Deed dated March 14, 1951 ... Liber MLP No. 8386, folio 75 to herself and William F. Freitag Sr., who having predeceased her thereby vesting the entire reversionary interest in the aforesaid Belle H. Freitag'. For $5 she subordinates the reversion to The Equitable Trust Company's mortgage of the same date. Charles C. Freitag signed for her as attorney-in-fact under a power of attorney dated Feb. 13, 1975 (R.H.B. 3207/652), given 'in connection with the subordination of the ground at 3030 Greenmount Avenue'; the agreement cites the power as 'dated February 13, 1974', a slip for 1975. So the clinic bought the 3030 house in 1975 but not its ground: the $90 rent stayed with Belle H. Freitag.

Mortgage dated Feb. 14, 1975, read on its first page only (folio 659; the instrument is not on the MDLandRec address index): People's Free Medical Clinic Inc. to The Equitable Trust Company, $22,850, due Feb. 14, 1982, 'which principal sum having been used as a portion of the purchase price for the property hereinafter described', on 'all those three lots of ground'. The descriptions are on pages not read; at this closing the three lots are presumably 3028 and 3030, bought from Charles C. Freitag (R.H.B. 3207/657), and 3032, whose reversion the clinic bought from David Siegel the same day (R.H.B. 3207/655). Charles C. Freitag's $3,250 purchase-money second mortgage of the same day is expressly subordinate to it (R.H.B. 3207/664), and Belle H. Freitag subordinated the 3030 ground rent to it (R.H.B. 3207/653).

Handwritten indenture dated Feb. 29, 1848, acknowledged that day in Baltimore City and received for record March 30, 1848 (Baltimore County Court land records; A. W. Bradford, clerk), read on the page image. The volume is a Baltimore County one (MSA CE 66-444): Waverly was county ground until 1888. John D. Nicoll of Baltimore County to Lorentz Leicht of the same county, 'in consideration of the sum of Two hundred Dollars current money', assigns the lot beginning 'at a stone planted in the ground at the corner of the York Turnpike Road and the Lane leading to Mr. Gilmor's', running 36 ft south on the road, 76 ft 4 in west, 38 ft north and 76 ft 6 in east, 'Being a part of a tract of land conveyed by a certain David Mumma to the said John D. Nicoll by his certain deed of Lease' dated Jan. 21, 1846 (A.W.B. 372/234, opened on Oct. 12, 2026: it holds no Mumma lease, see 719:negative-awb-372-234-mumma-nicoll-lease), for the rest of that renewable term, subject to 'the yearly rent of Nine Dollars current money' to Nicoll from Feb. 1, 1848. Witnesses Wm. Stansbury and Edw. J. Peters. The dimensions are exactly those of the 3020 corner lot in the deeds of 1953, 1954 and 1956, which still bound the 3010 lot on 'the sub-lease from John D. Nicholl to Lorenz Leight', so Lorentz Leicht is the cabinetmaker Lawrence Leight (1809-1892) of the lane corner. Old Land Marks dates his house there to 1845, before both this sub-lease and Mumma's 1846 lease to Nicoll; either the family occupied the corner before the leases were written or the tradition's year is early. David Mumma is the first of the toll-gate keepers Old Land Marks names, and the turnpike company's 1912 deed ties the north corner of the lane to a stone marking the beginning of land conveyed to him in 184[4]: Mumma's ground probably lay on both sides of Gilmor Lane. Update Oct. 13, 2026: the $9 rent of this sub-lease is traced: Abraham G. Mott 'bought out' the original (Mumma) rent on the whole lot (Balt. Co. J.B. 96/352, not read), so the $9 became an original rent; Mott sold it with the rest to Dodson and Griffith in 1892 (J.B. 1422/568); they sold it to Mary Clemens on May 7, 1896 (719:mdlr-ro1619-244-dodson-griffith-mary-clemens-9-dollar-rent-1896); and she merged it into the Leights' leasehold on June 9, 1924 (719:mdlr-scl4210-380-mary-clemens-leight-3020-merger-1924). Update Oct. 14, 2026: the parent lease of 1846 was at $32 a year (719:mdlr-jb96-352-mumma-heirs-mott-1876); Abraham G. Mott held Nicoll's leasehold from Samuel Hamilton Caughy by an assignment of Oct. 4, 1860 (Balt. Co. G.H.C. 30/473) and bought the fee in 1876, after which this $9 sub-rent was his to collect. Update Oct. 14, 2026: Nicoll made a second sub-lease out of the same Mumma lot a year before this one: to Franklin Wilson, Feb. 7, 1847, at $7 a year (A.W.B. 378/206, recited in 719:mdlr-ghc30-473-caughy-mott-1860), which Caughy bought back in 1855.
