Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. C, folios 19 to 22 (MSA CE 66-53; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved). Found in the Grantor Index 1770-1786 (MSA CE 33-2, p.338). Dated Sept. 13, 1778. Thomas Cole Speigle, Rachel Cole Speigle and William Carter Junior, planters, for 75 pounds current money, convey John Gorsuch, son of Thomas, part of 'Ensors Inspection lying on the west side of the main Road that leads from Baltimore Town to George Hailes', by the same courses as Joseph Ensor's 1767 deed to them (B P/470): from a bounded black oak of Mrs. Achsah Carnan's S 52 E 22 perches to the main Road, N 14 E 29 1/2 and N 41 E 6 perches bounding on the road, N 81 1/2 W 39 perches, S 50 W 4 perches to Carnan's line and with it to the beginning; 5 1/4 acres. No recital of title and no buildings named. Witnesses Richd. Lemmon and Benja. Griffith [?]; acknowledged Sept. 18, 1778 before Geo. Lindenberger and Jas. Calhoun, Rachel (wife of Thomas Cole Speigle) and Elinor (wife of William Carter Junior) releasing dower; recorded Oct. 22, 1778 (William Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: the Speagle 5 1/4 acres on the west side of the York Road, next to Huntington, passed in 1778 to John Gorsuch, son of Thomas, the same man who in 1787 took James Maidwell's mortgage of the adjoining nine acres (W.G. AA/193). So by 1787 Gorsuch held the lot south of Maidwell's and lent on Maidwell's. Where the Gorsuch 5 1/4 acres went next is not read. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (County grantor index, Dick and Gorsuch): the County grantor index for Gorsuch finds no deed or mortgage by John Gorsuch of Thomas in 1778 to 1786 (CE 33-2 pp. 134-138, the whole Go run: only an estray notice, W.G. B/290; 714:index-ce33-2-p133-gorsuch-john-1778-1786). From 1787 to 1803 (CE 33-3 and 33-4) his only conveyances of Ensor's Inspection are A.A. 205 (1787, to James Edwards, index p. 151, recorded twelve folios after Maidwell's mortgage, A.A. 193; not read), the 1795 release to Maidwell (S.S. 231) and the 1803 deed of trust (76/243, 3 acres, which is Harkin's Rest, bought from Harkin in 1771, and not this lot). There is no Gorsuch deed to Biays, Walker, Maidwell or Dick in the index, and none between W.G. 53/197 (1798) and 73/72 (1802). So the 5 1/4 acres Gorsuch took from the Speagles in 1778 are not shown sold before the 1787 mortgage, and A.A. 205 is the best candidate for where they went (INFERRED: the index gives no acreage or road, and it could instead be another part of Ensor's Inspection, for example Richard Dick's part, which Edwards held by 1804). The lot that 'formerly belonged to John Gorsuch now the property of the said James Biays' in 1801 (rows 46180, 46685) therefore rests on a deed or contract not indexed under Gorsuch, or on A.A. 205 through Edwards. Next: W.G. A.A. 205 itself (MSA CE 66-76 p. 205; the scan on disk stops at p. 197), read against the 1778 courses (row 47038) and the Edwards deeds. (714:index-ce33-3-p151-gorsuch-john-1787-1797 and -ce33-4-p163-gorsuch-john-1798-1803.) Update Oct. 17, 2026 (A.A. 205 read): the lot went to James Edwards on May 16, 1787 for 50 pounds, on word-for-word the same courses and acreage as this deed (W.G. A.A. 205 to 206, row 714:mdlr-waa205-gorsuch-edwards-speagle-5-quarter-acres-1787). Gorsuch held it nine years, 1778 to 1787.

Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. Z, folios 386 to 388 (MSA CE 66-75; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 386 to 390). Found in the Grantor Index 1770-1786 (MSA CE 33-2, p.339: 'Spear William, John Foster, pt of Ensors Inspection 29 a', folio 386 under a ditto of W.G. Z; W.G. Y/386 was pulled first and is not it). Dated Oct. 4, 1786. William Spear of Baltimore County, gentleman, for 400 pounds, conveys John Foster of the same county 'all that part of a Tract of Land Called and known by the Name of Ensors Inspection': 'begining for the same at a Stone standing North forty two degrees East Sixty two and a half perches from a bounded Red Oak standing in an old field being a Bounded tree of Huntington', thence N 42 E 117 perches to a stone in a line of 'Grants Addition'; with that land S 59 E 41 perches to a stone; S 27 W 13 perches until it intersects 'Loveless Addition'; with that land N 58 W 3 perches to the end of its line, S 52 W 38 perches, S 58 E 20 perches, S 7 W 7 perches until it intersects 'Daly [Darley] Hall'; with that land N 66 W 36 perches to a bounded tree of it; S 15 W 53 perches to a stone; S 76 1/2 W 16 perches to a stone; N 8 W 27 1/2 perches to a stone; S 75 1/2 W 18 1/2 perches to a stone; then a straight line to the beginning; twenty-nine acres more or less. Special warranty. Witnesses William Richardson and Christopher Walker; receipt of 400 pounds the same day, witness Lyde Goodwin; acknowledged Oct. 4, 1786 before Lyde Goodwin and Thos. Bailey, justices; recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). No recital of Spear's title. What it settles: (1) the 'about 1786' Spear deed that the 1809 Walker-to-Biays deed recites for Foster's 29 acres, the 3010 corner ground, is read, and its beginning, 62 1/2 perches N 42 E of the Huntington red oak, is the one the later deeds give. (2) It is the north-east part of Spear's 46 acres of 1781 (Bouldin abstract: from the same old-field oak N 42 E 178 perches to Grant's Addition and S 59 E 41 perches, the same second line), and the Huntington oak is the beginning tree of Joseph Ensor's 1762 deed to Job Garretson (B K/84), so the 3010 corner now runs, deed by deed, from Ensor (1762) to Garretson, Spear (1781, abstract), Foster (1786), Walker (1800) and Biays (1809). Spear kept the south-west 62 1/2 perches of the line, the part his heirs sold Biays in 1801 beside 2958 (W.G. 67/447; inference from the courses). (3) Christopher Walker, Foster's buyer of 1800 and the tavern keeper of 'Walker's Tavern', witnessed this deed. The rest of folio 388 to 390 holds James Morgan's 1786 assignment to Patrick and Susannah Kelly of part of lot 206 in the South East Addition of Baltimore Town; the top of 386 is the end of John Hoss to Henry Beckley (recorded Oct. 4, 1786).

Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5005, folios 341 to 343 (MSA CE 168-5013; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 341 to 345). Found in the City Grantor Index 1929, Jan.-June, P-Z (MSA CE 167-232, p.294: 'May 22, Sinclair James M, Ena M, to Waverly Bldg Asso Balto Co, Mtge, E S York Tp Rd, 5005/341'); the '5005/541' cited before was a misreading (folios 541 to 545 were pulled and are other deeds). Dated May 21, 1929, recorded May 22, 1929 (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). James M. Sinclair and Ena M. Sinclair his wife, of Baltimore City, members of the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, mortgage it the lot beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 204 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, also 281 ft 2 in south of the north side of 'a four foot alleyway called Bateman's Alley', 58 ft 4 in on the turnpike to the south-west corner of the whole ground, N 89 E 8 ft 6 in on its second line to the north-west side of the Old York Road, N 31 1/2 E 66 ft along that road, and west 42 ft 4 in to the beginning, 'known as No 3011 Greenmount Ave', being the firstly described lot of J. Holiday Riepe's deed to them in fee simple of March 1, 1927 (S.C.L. 4707/12); for an advance of $2,860 on 22 shares, dues 25 cents and interest 15 cents a share weekly; assent to a decree of sale. Margin: 'For release of mtge. Date 6/24/54 Liber 9513 fol. 53' (the association's 1954 release, read earlier). The release on folio 341 just above it, the same day, frees the Sinclairs from two earlier Waverly mortgages of March 29, 1923 (S.C.L. 3988/541) and June 11, 1926 (S.C.L. 4588/253), on a lot it does not describe: the source of the stray '541'. Lennox B. Clemens is the association's attorney for that release and witnesses the mortgage. What it settles: the 1929 mortgage the 1954 release names is read; 3011 was fee simple in the Sinclairs in 1929, with the two-mile stone and Bateman's Alley as its calls.

Deed of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 2292, folios 510 to 511, with a mortgage at 511 to 513 (MSA CE 168-2300; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 510 to 514). Found in the City Grantee Index 1906, P-Z (MSA CE 166-124, p.222); R.O. 2292/410, pulled earlier, was a misreading of 510. Dated Nov. 30, 1906, acknowledged that day before Howard D. Adams, notary; recorded Dec. 3, 1906 at 2 P.M. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Augustus D. Clemens Junior, of Baltimore County, for $1,000, grants James M. Sinclair, of Baltimore City, the lot beginning on the east side of the York Turnpike road 204 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot, also 281 ft 2 in south of the north side of 'a four foot alleyway called Bateman's alley', 58 ft 4 in south along the turnpike to the south-west corner of the whole ground, N 89 E 8 ft 6 in to the north-west side of the Old York road, N 31 1/2 E 66 ft along it, and west 42 ft 4 in to the beginning (3011 Greenmount); 'Being the second described lot of ground in a deed from Jacob H Aull to Augustus D Clemens Junior dated the fourth day of May one thousand eight hundred and ninety eight ... Liber R O No 1739 folio 295'; for the residue of the term, renewable forever, subject to the annual rent of $75, May 1 and November 1. Special warranty. The same day Sinclair mortgaged the leasehold to the York Road Building Association of Baltimore City for an advance of $910 on seven shares, 'part purchase money', dues 25 cents and interest 15 cents a share weekly, Harry E. Parkhurst attorney to sell. What it settles: how Aull's 1898 leasehold reached Sinclair. Clemens leased the lot to Jacob H. Aull at $75 on April 18, 1898 (R.O. 1730/92) and sold the rent to Lulie H. Wallace the same day (R.O. 1730/91); Aull deeded the leasehold back to Clemens on May 4, 1898 (R.O. 1739/295, not yet read), and Clemens sold it to Sinclair in 1906; Sinclair bought the rent from Wallace in 1921 (S.C.L. 3692/300), merging it. The lease-and-sell-the-rent pattern Clemens used on 3017 and the Gilmor Lane lot (chapter 07) is the same here.

Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber R.O. 1739, folios 295 to 297 (MSA CE 168-1747; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 295 to 299). Cited by the 1906 Clemens-to-Sinclair deed (R.O. 2292/510). Dated and acknowledged May 4, 1898 before Thos. C. Bailey, J.P.; recorded June 22, 1898 at 1:30 P.M. (Robt. Ogle, Clerk). Jacob H. Aull of Baltimore City, for $5, grants Augustus D. Clemens Junior of Baltimore County two lots on the east side of the York Turnpike Road, both measured from the two-mile stone in front of the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot and from the north side of 'a four foot alley way called Batemans alley': (1) beginning 123 ft 5 in south of the stone (200 ft from the alley's north side), 33 ft on the turnpike, east at right angles 58 ft 1 in to the west side of the Old York Road, 34 ft 4 in along it and 67 ft 7 in back, held under Clemens and wife's 99-year lease to Aull of April 14, 1898 (R.O. 1728/284) at $60, April 15 and October 15 (the 3019 lot, north of 3015-3017); (2) beginning 204 ft 7 in south of the stone (281 ft 2 in from the alley), 58 ft 4 in on the turnpike, N 89 E 8 ft 6 in to the Old York Road, N 31 1/2 E 66 ft and back 42 ft 4 in, held under their lease to Aull of April 18, 1898 (R.O. 1730/92) at $75, May 1 and November 1 (3011 Greenmount); for the residue of each term, renewable forever. Special warranty; witness Thos. C. Bailey. The deed just above it (ending on folio 295) is another Aull deed to Clemens, of a Barclay Street lot at $50 from James R. Brewer's 1895 deed to Aull (J.B. 1580/209), acknowledged May 20, 1898. What it settles: Aull was a straw for the 1898 Clemens leases. Clemens leased the 3019 lot (April 14) and the 3011 lot (April 18) to Aull, sold the $60 rent to Henry D. Konig and the $75 rent to Lulie H. Wallace, and took both leaseholds back from Aull on May 4. Clemens held the 3011 leasehold until he sold it to James M. Sinclair in 1906 (R.O. 2292/510), who bought the Wallace rent in 1921 and merged it. The 3011 leasehold side is now read without a gap from the 1898 lease to the 1927 fee.

Land commission and depositions, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber A.L. B, folios 591 to 596 (MSA CE 66-38; read 2026-10-16, folios 591 to 595 by a helper agent and 596 and the last passage of 595 by Claude, from the scans Jeff saved). Found in the Grantor Index 1770-1786 (MSA CE 33-2, p.127: 'Garrison Job &c, Land Commission on Ensors Inspection &c', folio 591; the liber is a ditto of A.L. B, and A.L. A/591 was a miss). Margin: 'Job Garrison, Loyd Ford, Land Commission & Deposition on Ensors Inspection & Grants addition'. At the county court of March 1768 Job Garrison and Loyd Ford, seized of parts of Grants Addition and Ensors Inspection, petitioned that the bounds 'are Decaied and in Danger of Being Lost'; a commission issued March 5, 1768 to William Govane, Thomas Boone, Henry Stevenson junior and Nicholas Merryman son of Samuel, who qualified in May 1768 and took depositions on the land: William Carter (about 52) and Joseph Taylor (about 60, a Quaker) on the stone set up at the beginning of Alexander Grant's land, which they divided between his daughters Ann Grant and Mary, wife of Loyd Ford, about six years before (Gorsuches Folly and Grants Addition); Thomas Gorsuch senior (about 90), John Ensor senior (about 73) and Elizabeth Grant (about 68, Alexander's widow) on a dead bounded white oak, now a large stone, 'on the South Side of a hill and on the East Side of a Small run decending into Joneses falls', bounded in lieu of 'a dead Bounded Read oak of Moses Edwards Land'. The last passage (folios 595 to 596): 'At a large old bounded Red Oak Standing in a leavle old field formerly Situate [settled?] by Moses Edwards before mentioned, Joseph Ensor and Job Garrison owners and possessors in part of a tract of land called Ensors Inspection acknowledged and declared that the said bounded Read oak was and is the beginning Boundree of the said Job Garrison's part of the said tract of Land called Ensors Inspection before all the company there present.' Given under the hands and seals of Thos. Boone, Henry Stevenson son of Edwd. and Nichs. Merryman son of Saml., May 30, 1768 (the clerk wrote '1760'; the March 1768 court and the qualifications fix 1768); filed August Term 1770, enrolled and examined by A. Lawson, Clerk. What it settles: the old-field red oak that begins Joseph Ensor's 1762 deed to Garrison ('a Bounded Tree of ... Huntington'), Garrison's 1781 deed to William Spear and Spear's 1786 deed to John Foster is a sworn, marked corner on the ground in 1768, in a level old field once settled by Moses Edwards. Huntington was first granted to the Edwards family (a John Edwards, 1688), so the 'Edwards' field fits the deeds' calling the oak a Huntington tree (inference). It gives no distance to a road, so it does not by itself fix the oak on a modern map.

Sub-lease, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 4854, folios 321 to 323 (MSA CE 168-4862; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 321 to 325, at 130 and 300 dpi; the companion construction mortgage follows from folio 323 and is filed separately). Dated March 3, 1928. Lula S. Dietrich, widow, of Baltimore City, sub-lessor, sub-leases to Miller Brothers Furniture Company, Incorporated, a Maryland corporation, for all the rest of her term of years save one day (no 99-year term is stated), a lot on the east side of Greenmount Avenue (formerly York Turnpike Road) beginning 204 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield by deed of January 31, 1865 (Balt. Co. J.H.L. 43/548), and 409 ft south of Gorsuch Avenue, at a post at the north-west corner of that whole tract; S 2 W 35 ft along the avenue, S 85 1/2 E 126 ft more or less to the west side of the Old York Road, N 19 1/2 E 35 ft more or less to a post at the north-east corner of the whole lot, N 85 1/2 W 140 ft 6 in to the beginning; the improvements known as No. 3117 Greenmount Avenue. Title recited: the same lot described in a deed of May 6, 1927 from C. Reese Dietrich to John Harmon Dietrich and Lula S. Dietrich (S.C.L. 4735/61); see also a confirmatory deed of March 2, 1928 from Lula S. Dietrich, executrix, to Lula S. Dietrich, survivor; and part of the whole lot conveyed by a deed of assignment from Augustus D. Clemens Jr. to John H. Dietrich dated December 9, 1907 (S.C.L. 2390/331), the whole lot subject to the original ground rent of $150 a year, half-yearly on March 1 and September 1. Rent $1,200 a year in equal quarterly instalments from March 1, 1928, over and above all taxes and assessments; distress for arrears; re-entry until paid after 60 days in arrear, and re-entry as though no sub-lease had been made after six months. Renewable forever: on a $10 renewal fine the sub-lessor gives a new sub-lease at the same rent reserving one day. The sub-lessee may pay the $150 original rent ($75 half-yearly) directly to its holder and deduct it from the $1,200. After five years the sub-lessee may redeem the $1,200 rent for $18,892.58 in gold coin, with rent accrued and a pro rata share. The sub-lease has no building covenant, no valuation and no builder. Signed Lula S. Dietrich and the company by Adolph Miller, President, under the seal 'Miller Bros Furniture Co Inc 1928'; witness and notary R. E. Lee Hall; acknowledged March 3, 1928; recorded March 7, 1928 at 9:50 A.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: the $1,200 sub-rent is carved out of Lula Dietrich's own leasehold of the whole 79 ft lot under the $150 rent, and that leasehold came to John H. Dietrich by assignment from Augustus D. Clemens Jr. in December 1907 (S.C.L. 2390/331), not about 1920 as the undated City plat suggested. John Harmon Dietrich was Lula's husband (S.C.L. 5213/440 calls the 1927 grantees 'John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S. Dietrich his wife'), and he had died by March 2, 1928, when Lula as executrix confirmed the lot to herself as survivor. What it does not settle: how Clemens Jr. came to hold the leasehold (possibly at the 1904 Hershey trustee's sale, an inference), what part C. Reese Dietrich played in 1927 (very probably a straw deed to create a tenancy by the entirety, an inference), and the basis of the $18,892.58 redemption price, which is not the 6 percent figure for $1,200.

Mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 4854, folios 323 to 325 and on (MSA CE 168-4862; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, which stops at folio 325 in the middle of the third lot's description, so the signatures, acknowledgment, recording and any release are not read). Dated March 3, 1928, the day of the Dietrich sub-lease, and entered next after it. Miller Brothers Furniture Company, Incorporated, Adolph Miller and Anna J. Miller his wife, and Jacob Miller, all of Baltimore City, mortgage to Erhard Eyring of Baltimore City, for $1 and to secure a loan of $20,000 'to be used ... in the construction and improvement upon the lot of ground hereinafter firstly described', under plans and specifications signed by Adolph Miller, President, and Eyring. The advances: $5,000 when the roof is on, $7,000 when plastered, $5,000 when all trim is on, and $3,000 within thirty days after completion, each only on a certificate of John F. Eyring, architect, of Baltimore; if the mortgage is assigned to The Eyring Realty Company Incorporated, it may make the advances in Eyring's place. A condition of the loan is that Eyring, the party of the second part, will begin the construction within ten days and fully complete the building within four months of the date. No further encumbrance before the last advance, and the debt advanced falls due at once on a transfer without consent, insolvency, bankruptcy or receivership. The whole $20,000 is due on or before March 1, 1933 at 6 percent, payable half-yearly and charged only from each advance, with a joint and several note for each advance, $1,000 to be repaid at three years and another $1,000 at four. Security: first (Block 4076), the 3117 Greenmount Avenue lot, beginning 114 7/10 ft south of the south curb line of Thirty-second Street, which is 204 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the Coffield land of 1865 (J.H.L. 43/548), with the courses of the sub-lease, being the lot Lula S. Dietrich demised to the company by lease of even date at $1,200 a year (written here as half-yearly; the sub-lease says quarterly); second (Block 1688), Adolph and Jacob Miller's interest in 242 N. Patterson Park Avenue, 14 by 80 ft, 14 ft south of Orleans Street, conveyed by Daniel F. Ludlow to Adolph Miller, Jacob L. Miller and Katherine Miller (now deceased) by deed of June 9, 1921 (S.C.L. 3748 [?] folio 219), subject to $60 rent; third, their interest in the lot at the south-west corner of Orleans Street and Patterson Park Avenue (the description runs on past folio 325). What it settles: this mortgage, not the sub-lease, is the construction instrument for the 1928 store at 3117. Erhard Eyring lent the $20,000 and undertook to build it within four months to John F. Eyring's plans, which fits the newspaper reports that E. Eyring and Sons would build (CR#4925, 4926) and the City permit of July 21, 1928. It very probably explains the equity case Erhard Eyring et al. v. The Miller Brothers Furniture Company et al. (decree of Oct. 21, 1932) and the 1933 trustees' deed of the leasehold to The Eyring Realty Corporation (S.C.L. 5349/127): the Eyrings enforcing this loan after the company's insolvency (an inference). What it does not settle: the recording date, the end of the third description and any release, which are on folios not saved.

Administratrix's deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. Dietrich, late of Baltimore City, deceased, authorized and directed by an order of the Orphans' Court of Baltimore City passed April 27, 1931 to convey under Article 93, Section 144 of the Code of Public General Laws, for $5 grants to Dorothy Dietrich, Wilhelmina Dietrich and Helen Dietrich Butler (nee Dietrich), as tenants in common, their personal representatives and assigns, two lots. First (Block 4076): the 3117 Greenmount Avenue lot, by the description of the 1928 sub-lease (beginning 204 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, assigned to George C. H. Coffield in 1865, J.H.L. 43/548, and 409 ft more or less south of Gorsuch Avenue; 35 ft on the avenue, about 126 ft to the Old York Road, 140 ft 6 in on the north line), 'and especially' the right to collect 'the annual sub rent of twelve hundred dollars' reserved by the sub-lease from Lula S. Dietrich, widow, to Miller Brothers Furniture Company, Incorporated, dated March 3, 1928 (S.C.L. 4854/321), payable quarterly from March 1, 1928; being the lot thirdly described in the deed of May 6, 1927 from C. Reese Dietrich to John Harmon Dietrich and Lulu S. Dietrich his wife (S.C.L. 4735/61), with the confirmatory deed of March 2, 1928 from Lula S. Dietrich, executrix, to Lula S. Dietrich (S.C.L. 4853/235); the whole lot subject to the original $150 ground rent, half-yearly on March 1 and September 1. Second (Block 3856): 409 East Thirty-first Street (formerly Waverly Avenue), 24 ft 6 in on the south side of the street beginning 97 ft 6 in east of Barclay Street, 100 ft deep to a 10 ft alley, the lot secondly described in the same 1927 deed to John H. Dietrich and Lula S. Dietrich his wife, subject to $61.25 ground rent half-yearly on April 15 and October 15. Both pass for the rest of the term with the benefit of renewal forever. Witness and notary R. Irving Hall; acknowledged April 27, 1931; recorded April 27, 1931 at 12:30 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). What it settles: the estate behind the 1936 merger deed (S.C.L. 5686/215) is Lula S. Dietrich's, not Wilhelmina's. Wilhelmina was Lula's administratrix, so Lula died between March 3, 1928 and April 27, 1931, apparently without a will (an administratrix, not an executrix; an inference). The three grantees took the $1,200 sub-rent and the sub-reversion of 3117 as tenants in common by this deed, and that is the title they deeded to The Eyring Realty Corporation in 1936. It also confirms that John Harmon Dietrich, also written John H. Dietrich, was Lula's husband, so the earlier reading of J. Harmon Dietrich as a son is wrong. What it does not settle: the grantees' kinship to Lula is still not stated (a conveyance in kind by order of the Orphans' Court points to her distributees, very probably her daughters; an inference), nor the dates of John Harmon's and Lula's deaths (the Register of Wills index is the route).

Sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber J.W.S. No. 167, folio 405 (MSA CE 62-167; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 260 dpi). The instrument begins on folio 402 (folios 402 to 404 read earlier: David Stewart, assignee of the 1884 Harris lease, sub-leases four lots on the west side of the York Turnpike to Sarah E. Sinclair, the fourth lot beginning 181 ft north of Merryman's Lane, 16 by 100 ft, now 3224) and runs on to folio 406, which was not saved. Folio 405 holds the habendum and the rents. The term is ninety-nine years 'or for all the residue of the term created by the aforesaid lease', beginning on the date of the instrument (Feb. 1, 1888), to Sarah and her executors, administrators and assigns. The clerk writes her 'Sarah C. Sinclair' three times, but his capital E and C are alike and he gives her husband James the same letter, so E is the probable reading. The yearly rents, payable to David Stewart, his heirs, personal representatives or assigns, are $36 on the lot first described, $87 on the second, $81 on the third and $48 on the fourth (3224), $252 in all. They are paid in equal half-yearly instalments accruing from Feb. 1, 1888, clear of all taxes and assessments, 'each of said lots however being liable only for its own rent precisely as if each of said lots had been leased by a separate instrument'. Remedies: distress for any arrears; re-entry after sixty days until the arrears and costs are paid; and after six months, re-entry to hold the lot 'as if this lease had never been made'. Sarah and James E. Sinclair her husband covenant to pay the rent, taxes and assessments. The lessor's covenant for quiet enjoyment begins at the foot of the folio and runs onto folio 406. No signatures, acknowledgment or recording entry are on this folio. What it settles: the sub-rent on the 3224 lot was $48 a year from Feb. 1, 1888, the same sum John N. C. (or H. C.) Legg reserved on the same 16-ft lot in his lease to George T. Drechsler of Apr. 24, 1890 (J.B. 1299/406, $48, payable May 1 and Nov. 1), the rent that ran until the 1926 merger. The 1890 lease appears to restate the 1888 sub-rent on the same lot, though on different rent days [inference]. Each of the four lots was charged separately, so the 3224 rent could be dealt with on its own. What it does not settle: the signatures, acknowledgment and recording date (folio 406, not saved), and how the sub-lease was cleared before Legg's fresh lease of 1890. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (later): folios 406 and 407 read (MSA CE 62-167 p.00406 to p.00407, the scan Jeff saved; read by a helper agent). The instrument ends on folio 407. Folio 406 finishes the lessor's covenants: Stewart warrants the lots against claims by, from or under him; on payment of a $10 renewal fine and costs he will give Sarah C. Sinclair a new lease of all or any of the lots for another 99 years at the same rent, 'so that the demise hereby created may be renewable and renewed from time to time forever'; and any rent may be redeemed after five years at 5 percent and after fifteen years at 6 percent, in gold coin of the United States or its equivalent, with rent accrued and a pro-rata part of the current half-year's rent. A rent not redeemed by Feb. 1, 1904 runs as if the lease were dated that day and is not redeemable at 6 percent for fifteen years more. Folio 407: signed David Stewart (witness Robert A. Thursby [?]), Sarah C. Sinclair and Jas. E. Sinclair (witness Wm. D. Wright [?]). Stewart acknowledged on Feb. 1, 1888 before Thursby, a Baltimore City justice, with the certificate of Jas. Bond, Clerk of the Superior Court of Baltimore City; Sarah C. and James E. Sinclair acknowledged the same day before Wright, a Baltimore County justice. 'Recorded Feby 2nd 1888 at 8:30 AM' (John W. Shanklin, Clerk); a margin note reads 'Delivered ... 5064, Oct 13/88' [?]. Her initial is C in her signature, in the County clerk's hand of 1888 and in the City clerk's hand of 1890 (J.B. 1289/297 and 299); the 1923 deeds write E. The same day the Sinclairs mortgaged to Stewart (J.W.S. 135/275, recorded Feb. 9, 1888), and the foreclosure of that mortgage in April 1890 ended this sub-lease (J.B. 1289/297).

Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber B.B. No. 1, folios 210 to 212 (MSA CE 66-26; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 210 to 214, at 130, 220 and 250 dpi). The book is a fair copy in one uniform later hand (inference from the script), so some spellings may be the copyist's. Headed 'Charles Ridgely to Aeshah Hollyday'. Dated Dec. 27, 1753, between Charles Ridgely of Baltimore County, gentleman, and Achsah Hollyday, 'Daughter of the said Charles Ridgely' (no husband named). The consideration is 'the Naturall Love and affection which he hath & beareth' for her and five shillings sterling, receipted the same day as 'the consideration money': a deed of gift in the words of a bargain and sale. It conveys 'all the following several Tracts of Land lying in the County afsd and on the East side of Jones' Falls': 'Wilkinsons Lott containing Eighty nine acres'; 'Huntington containing fifty acres', named only, with no courses; part of 'Ridgely's Whim', beginning at the third bounded tree of Roberts Park, N 24 deg 15 min W 296 perches to a bound ash, S 28 W 140 perches to a white oak, the beginning tree of Roberts Park, SSE 26, S by W 68, S 53 E 72, S 42, SE by S 50, S 54 and N 56 W 28 perches to a Spanish oak of Durbin's land, N 25 W 83, N 31 W 214, N 24 E 86, N 22 W 44, N 5 W 20 and N 50 E 77 perches, then to a white oak, the fourth bounded tree of Merryman's Beginning, S 73 perches to a poplar, its third bounded tree, and back to the beginning, 'containing by estimation two hundred acres'; and two parts of 'Taylors Purchase lying in the fork of Gunpowder', bounded on Cox's Forrest, Blathynia Cambria, the World's End, 'Clemonara belonging to Charles Carroll Esquire' and Benjamin's Lott, 'in both the afsd parcels of Land six hundred acres'. Habendum to Achsah 'his [sic] heirs and assigns for ever', with a warranty against all claiming under Ridgely. Witnesses Nuxton Gay (so copied; very probably N. Ruxton Gay) and William Lyon, who took the acknowledgment the same day as justices of the peace; 'Received 28th April 1754 & then recorded' (Beale Bordley, Clerk). No alienation-fine receipt follows it, though the next deed in the book has one. The strike on folio 210: the upper three quarters of the folio is blank ruled paper, closed off by a horizontal rule and one diagonal stroke from upper right to lower left that ends at the Ridgely heading, and the same stroke closes the blank at the foot of folio 212 after this deed. It is the copying clerk's line through unused space so that nothing could be written in later. It is not a cancellation: no entry stands under it (the faint lines there are ink showing through from the other side of the leaf), and the deed has no marginal note or release. Folios 213 and 214 hold James Wells Jr. to Ulrich Ecklear (Nov. 21, 1753, 250 acres of Wells Care Enlarged, 75 pounds) and the start of John Robeson to Richard King Stevenson (Mar. 2, 1754); neither bears on Huntington. What it settles: the Onions' 1809 confirmatory deed (W.G. 102/33) cites this deed correctly as Charles Ridgely to Achsah Holliday, Dec. 27, 1753, B.B. 1/210. It is a gift in fee from father to daughter, and it names Huntington among her lands four years before the 1757 resurvey for John Carnan and Achsah his wife (475 acres, patented 1761). So on the 1688 to 1757 hand-off it shows that Charles Ridgely held a Huntington of fifty acres and gave it to Achsah in 1753. Taylors Purchase at 600 acres agrees with the 1768 settlement, which says her father conveyed Taylors Purchase and Ridgely's Whim to her. What it does not settle: Huntington has no courses here, so the deed does not place it on the ground or tie it to 3028. Fifty acres is less than the 135 acres of the 1688 survey, and the deed does not say 'part of', so how Ridgely came to hold it (from John Edwards or Tobias Stansbury) is not shown. The part of Ridgely's Whim here is 200 acres by estimation, against 500 acres in the 1768 deed. Whether Wilkinson's Lott and this part of Ridgely's Whim were taken into the 1757 resurvey is not shown.

Deed of reversion, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber M.L.P. No. 6549, folios 594 to 595 (MSA CE 168-6557; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 594 to 598 and the plat at 598a, at 130 and 300 dpi; folio 594 opens with the end of an instrument acknowledged before Ernest F. Conveyed with 'especially the clear yearly rent of sixty six dollars issuing out of said lot of ground by virtue of the lease aforesaid', 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee and the annual rent issuing thereout shall be forever extinguished'. Aull's 1912 lease to Alice M. Chapman but a new $66 rent created on Feb. 25, 1935, when The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County leased 3030 to Helen M. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1935 read): the 1935 instruments are read (S.C.L. 5518/171 to 175, rows 47394 to 47396). McCoy assigned the 3030 leasehold to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County on July 8, 1932 (recorded July 12) for $5 and other valuable considerations, subject to the 1912 rent of $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1; they held it by Mary A. J. Aull's assignment of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70). No mortgage or default is recited. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. Deed in fee simple on the redemption of ground rents, Baltimore City land records, Liber J.B. No. 1276, folios 42 to 43 (MSA CE 168-1284; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 300 dpi). Captioned 'Alice P. Harris to Deed to David Stewart'. Dated Jan. 25, 1890, by Alice Patterson Harris and W. Hall Harris her husband to David Stewart. Recitals, quoted: 'Whereas by deed dated June 11th AD 1884 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber W M I No 141 folio 407 &c W Hall Harris and Alice P Harris leased to James E Sinclair the two lots hereinafter described And Whereas by mesne assignments and by deed dated January 3rd A.D. 1888 and recorded among said records in Liber J W S No 167 folio 243 &c from Sarah C Sinclair and James E Sinclair to David Stewart said Stewart became possessed of the leasehold interest in said lots created by said lease And Whereas by the terms of said lease the ground rents created thereby on said lots are redeemable and said Stewart now desires to redeem the same' (the day and the last digit of the year are cramped; the assignment itself is dated the third of January 1888). For 'twenty six hundred and eighty dollars and sixty six cents and accrued rent' the Harrises grant and convey to Stewart 'all those two lots of ground lying in Baltimore City (formerly County)'. The first begins on the westernmost side of the York turnpike road 164 ft 8 in northerly from the corner of the northeasternmost side of Merryman's Lane and the westernmost side of the turnpike, at the line drawn through the centre of 'the division wall between the house erected on the lot now being described and the house erected on the adjoining lot on the north thereof', and runs westerly through that wall 100 ft in all to an alley three feet wide communicating with Merryman's lane and laid out parallel with the turnpike, southerly on the east side of the alley 32 ft, easterly 100 ft to the road and northerly to the beginning (132 ft 8 in to 164 ft 8 in north of the lane). The second begins at the same point, at the centre of the division wall between its house and the house on the adjoining lot to the south, and runs westerly 100 ft to the alley, northerly on its east side 32 ft 4 in, easterly 100 ft to the road and southerly 32 ft 4 in to the beginning (164 ft 8 in to 197 ft north of the lane). '(Being the same two lots firstly and secondly particularly described in a Lease from W Hall Harris and Alice P Harris his wife to James E Sinclair mentioned aforesaid)'; a line runs under or through the words 'firstly and secondly particularly described'. With the improvements, rights, ways, alleys and privileges. Habendum 'unto the said David Stewart absolutely in fee simple free and discharged from the operations of said Lease'; special warranty and further assurances. Signed Alice Patterson Harris and W Hall Harris, witness Robert A. Thursby [?], justice of the peace for Baltimore City, before whom both acknowledged on Jan. 25, 1890. 'Recd for record Jan 25 1890 @ 12.55 o'clk P.M. same day recorded & exd per Jas Bond Clk.' Margin: 'Delivd Jan 27/90 to David Stewart'; a pencilled sum, 164 plus 32 making 196, stands beside the second lot. Folios 43 (foot) to 46 hold William L. Dallam's mortgage to the Merchants and Mechanics Permanent Building and Loan Company on Linden Avenue, not this ground. What it settles: the fee of the two lots passed from Alice P. Harris to David Stewart on Jan. 25, 1890 by redemption of the 1884 ground rents, not by an ordinary sale. Stewart already held the leasehold by the Sinclairs' assignment (J.W.S. 167/243), and the price is the two rents of the 1884 lease, $80 and $80.84 a year (recited in J.W.S. 167/404), capitalized at 6 percent ($160.84 divided by 0.06 is $2,680.67; the deed says $2,680.66), the rate at which the lease made them redeemable from June 11, 1889. The 1884 lease ended in Stewart's hands that day ('free and discharged from the operations of said Lease'). The 64 ft 4 in of the two lots is the same frontage as the four lots of Stewart's Feb. 1, 1888 lease to the Sinclairs (J.W.S. 167/402), so after this deed the 1888 rents ($36, $87, $81 and $48) issued out of Stewart's fee, which is why his Apr. 23, 1890 fee deed to John H. C. Legg (J.B. 1289/299) cites this deed and describes four rent-bearing lots [inference]. 3224, 181 to 197 ft north of the lane, is the northern 16 ft of the second lot. Both Harrises sign; the caption and the 1890 recital in J.B. 1289/299 name Alice alone, the holder of the fee under the 1884 deed to her. What it does not settle: it does not recite Harris's own title (the Sinclair deed to her of June 11, 1884, W.M.I. 141/405 is not cited, only the lease at 141/407); the 'mesne assignments' before the 1888 deed are not named (the 1884 lease ran to James E. Sinclair alone, and Sarah C. Sinclair is the first-named assignor in 1888); and the third lot of the 1884 Sinclair-to-Harris deed, beginning 36 ft 1/2 in north of the corner, is not in this deed. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the third lot of the 1884 deed to Harris, not in this redemption, stayed with the Harrises until Jan. 18, 1898, when they sold its fee to Alice Gerry Stewart for $2,500, the $150 rent at 6 percent (R.O. 1715/35, 768:mdlr-ro1715-35-harris-alice-gerry-stewart-third-lot-1898).

The Oct. 1, 1872 lease to Sinclair (E.H.A. 77/361) begins 475 ft south of Wilson Street at the southeast corner of 'lot number Seven as conveyed ... to P. P. Pendleton', so Lot 7 is the southern of the two, 425 to 475 ft south of Wilson Street [inference], and the 3224 ground is the Wilson land immediately south of Pendleton's Lot 7. The 20 ft rear alley, half of it taken from each side, is the 20 ft alley at the back of the 1872 lease. John H. Hartman's parcel lay immediately north of Lot 8; the trustees' deed to John H. Hartman and wife indexed Feb. 12, 1872 at 74/235 is probably its reversion [inference]. Legg of Baltimore City, in fee, the lot 'Beginning for the same at the corner formed by the intersection of the West side of the York Turnpike Road and the Northeast side of Merryman's Lane', north on the turnpike 36 ft 1 1/2 in, west at right angles 42 ft to the lane, and south-east on the lane 55 ft to the beginning. Recital: 'Being the same piece or parcel of ground which by lease dated June 14th 1887 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County was leased by Robert Riddell Brown to James E Sinclair at and under the yearly rent of sixty dollars payable in two equal instalments on June 1st and December 1st in every year and being the same piece or parcel of ground which was conveyed by Robert Riddell Brown to Lucy C George by deed dated 22nd [?] day of June 1887 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber J.W.S. No 162 folio 132 &c'. It passes 'especially and particularly the yearly rent reserved by the lease aforesaid', subject to the lessee's estate; special warranty. Witnesses J. R. Keenan [?] and D. K. What it settles: (1) how the Georges took Brown's reversion: Brown leased the apex to Sinclair on June 14, 1887 at $60 and sold the rent to Lucy C. Mortgage, Baltimore County land records, mortgage series, Liber J.W.S. No. 135, folios 275 to 278 (MSA CE 221-135; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, at 130 and 220 dpi). Captioned 'James E Sinclair et al Mortgage to David Stewart'. Made Feb. 1, 1888 by James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair, husband and wife, of Baltimore County, to David Stewart of Baltimore City. Recital, quoted: 'Whereas the said Mortgagors are justly indebted to the said mortgagee in the sum of one thousand dollars for which sum they have passed to said mortgagee their joint and several promissory note of even date herewith payable six months after date with the agreement that said note shall be extended for a further period of six months without interest which note and indebtedness it was previously agreed should be secured by a mortgage upon the real and lease hold property and chattels of the mortgagors'. For the premises and $1 the Sinclairs 'grant convey assign and set over to the said David Stewart All the property and estate of said mortgagors real personal and mixed situated at or near Waverly in Baltimore County and especially the premises on the South West corner of Merrymans Lane and the York Turnpike Road and the Machinery thereupon and the lots on the York Road North of Merrymans Lane and the lots on the North and South sides of Merrymans Lane West of the York Road now owned by said Mortgagors or one of them subject to certain ground rents and a certain mortgage', with the improvements, rights, ways, alleys and privileges. No metes and bounds, no liber and no lessor is recited. Void on payment of 'said loan of $1000 at maturity'; the Sinclairs keep possession until default and pay all taxes, assessments, public dues and charges on the property and on the mortgage debt. On default the whole debt is due, and 'it shall be lawful for the said David Stewart his heirs personal representatives and assigns or Robert Riddell Brown his attorney or agent at any time after such default to sell the property hereby mortgaged or so much thereof as may be necessary', on twenty days' notice of the time, place, manner and terms of sale in a newspaper printed in Baltimore County; proceeds to the expenses of sale, including a commission of four percent to the party making it, then to the mortgagee's claims, then the surplus to the mortgagors. Signed 'Sarah E [?] Sinclair' (the clerk's initial looks like an E, perhaps over a C; the body and the acknowledgment say Sarah C.) and 'Jas E Sinclair', witness John Willis, justice of the peace for Baltimore County, before whom both acknowledged on Feb. 7, 1888. Stewart made the consideration oath the same day before Robert A. Thursby, justice of the peace for Baltimore City, with the certificate of Jas. Bond, Clerk of the Superior Court of Baltimore City (Feb. 7, 1888). 'Recorded Feby 9th 1888 @ 8.30 A.M. & Exd per John W Shanklin Clerk.' Margin: ticket number 4656 and 'Delivered per Ticket June 8 - 1888', the same delivery date as the Jan. 3, 1888 assignment (J.W.S. 167/243). No release is noted in the margins. The other pages: folio 275 opens with the end of an 1859 Fells Point Building Union instrument, copied from the Baltimore City records (G.E.S. [?] 176/270) and recorded in the County Feb. 8, 1888; folios 278 (lower half) and 279 hold Frank Gustav Tscholski's [?] $800 mortgage of Feb. 8, 1888 to the Confidence Loan and Savings Association of Baltimore City on Eastern Avenue (release noted at J.W.S. 155/281). Neither concerns Waverly. What it settles: this is the mortgage that J.B. 1289/297 recites ('a Mortgage from James E. Sinclair and Sarah C. Sinclair to David Stewart dated February 1st 1888 ... Liber J.W.S. No 135 folio 275') and under whose power of sale Stewart sold six lots to John H. C. Legg on Apr. 8, 1890. The debt was $1,000, interest free, due Aug. 1, 1888 and by the agreed extension Feb. 1, 1889, so it was more than a year overdue at the sale [inference from the terms]. It is a blanket mortgage on all the Sinclairs' Waverly property, real, leasehold and personal, made the day Stewart leased the four lots back to them (J.W.S. 167/402) and four weeks after they assigned him the 1884 Harris leasehold for $1,500 (J.W.S. 167/243): it covers 3224 (in 'the lots on the York Road North of Merrymans Lane', the four sub-lease lots) and the 3200 apex (the same class; lot 1 of the 1890 sale). Because it describes no lot by bounds, Stewart had to file 'a plat and description of the property' with his 1890 suit, as J.B. 1289/297 says he did [inference]. The 'premises on the South West corner of Merrymans Lane and the York Turnpike Road and the Machinery thereupon' is probably lot 2 of the 1890 sale, on the southwest side of the lane beginning 7 ft 8 1/2 in from the turnpike, held under Stewart's lease to Sarah C. Sinclair of May 28, 1887 (J.W.S. 160/403) [inference]; the machinery points to a works or shop of Sinclair's there. Robert Riddell Brown, who bought the apex from Sinclair and leased it back in June 1887 and leased him the lot southwest of the lane in December 1887, is named as Stewart's attorney or agent for the sale, so Brown and Stewart worked together on the Sinclair property. What it does not settle: which 'certain mortgage' the property was subject to on Feb. 1, 1888 (the Waverly Building Association mortgage on the Harris lots was released of record Jan. 23, 1888, County index 136/94; the 1890 deed's 'Mortgage for $3,500 [?] to Alice Gerry Stewart' on lots 1 to 4 is a candidate) [inference]; whether Brown or Stewart conducted the 1890 sale; the court file and plat in Stewart v. Sinclair; and what the machinery was. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (the earlier mortgage released): the Waverly Building Association mortgage of Sept. 17, 1884 (Sinclair and David H. Orr, W.M.I. 111) was released to Sinclair on Jan. 24, 1888 (J.W.S. 136/94-95, 768:mdlr-jws136-94-waverly-bldg-assn-release-sinclair-1888); no other mortgage is recited on the release. Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber H.M.F. 3, folios 165 to 167 (MSA CE 62-3; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, pages 165 to 169, at 110 and 200 dpi; the top of 165 is the receipt and acknowledgment of Mordecai and Catherine Maddock's deed of the same land to David R. Horne for $1,450, and 167 to 169 hold Joseph Roberts's deed to Nathan K. Hall of a lot on the Old Harford Road about seven and a half miles from the city). Dated Oct. 11, 1852. David R. Horne and Pamelia A. Horne his wife, of Baltimore County, for $2,000, convey John Litzinger of the same place, in fee, 'All that piece or parcel of land situate and lying in Baltimore County aforesaid and near the village of Hereford called Solomons Chance': beginning at a stone on the east side of the Old Baltimore and York Road, also on the road to Fosters Meeting House and the road to John Wise's paper mills and Monkton Mills; S 14 1/2 E 28 perches, N 60 E 9, S 42 E 10, S 81 1/2 E 9, S 68 1/2 E 12 to two marked chestnut trees, S 66 1/2 E 8, S 56 1/4 E 39 9/10 to a stone, S 58 3/4 E 25 to a stone, N 42 1/2 W 70 1/2 (as written) to a stone, N 50 1/2 W 14 to a stone, about N 40 W about 100 perches to a stone on the south side of the road, and with the road to the beginning; no acreage is stated. Recital: 'being the same land that by Indenture bearing even date herewith ... was granted and conveyed by Mordecai Maddock and wife to the said David R. Horne'. Witnesses and justices John B. Kidd and Edward B. Freeland; acknowledged Oct. 11, 1852, Pamelia examined apart; $1 received in lieu of stamp Oct. 13; recorded Oct. 13, 1852 (Henry M. Fitzhugh, Clerk); margin 'Deld grantee 2 May 1853'. What it settles: line (1) of the 1851-1874 index (row 47363) is a farm near Hereford in the north of the county, not Waverly ground; it has nothing to do with 3011, 3013 or the fork. Horne bought it from the Maddocks and sold it to Litzinger the same day for $550 more. Edward B. Freeland, J.P., who took this acknowledgment, also took the Litzingers' acknowledgments of the 1864 Treadway deed (G.H.C. 39/499), the 1865 Blum sub-lease (J.H.L. 45/362) and the 1866 White lease (J.H.L. 48/502), so the Hereford buyer and the Waverly John Litzinger are very probably the same man, and he very probably lived up the county after 1852 (an inference from the justice). What it does not settle: the identity outright (the deed names no wife and no earlier residence for him) and what became of Solomons Chance; no Litzinger deed out of it is in the 1851-1874 index.

Deed, Baltimore County land records, Liber H.M.F. 7, folios 347 to 349 (MSA CE 62-7; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, pages 347 to 351, at 110 and 250 dpi; the top of 347 is the end of an acknowledgment by Charles and Catharine Shaffer, and 349 to 351 hold James Eccleston's deed to John M. Tracey of parts of Singerys Trouting Streams and other tracts and Mordecai Benson's deed to Thomas Wilhelm of part of Springfield Enlarged). Dated Dec. 12, 1853. John Litzinger and Elizabeth his wife, of Baltimore County, for $900, convey Abraham H. Bucher of the same, in fee, 'all that part of a tract of land called Ensors Inspection' beginning at the north-west corner of the lot Henry N. Bowerman, Walter T. Allender and others conveyed to the Vestry of St. Johns Church by deed of Sept. 27, 1844, and running on the east side of the old York road N 32 1/2 E 8 2/10 perches, S 81 1/4 E 10 4/10 perches, S 17 W 6 3/10 perches to the north-east corner of the Church lot, and on that lot N 87 1/2 W 12 6/10 perches to the beginning: 77 1/2 square perches (the courses close within 0.3 perch and compute to 79 square perches). Recital: 'being part of the tract of land above mentioned which was conveyed by John W Stump surviving trustee to the aforesaid Henry N Bowerman and others' by deed of Oct. 28, 1845, A.W.B. 359/136; Litzinger's own deed of June 10, 1847 (A.W.B. 381/477) is not recited. Witnesses and justices Nathaniel Parsons and Walter R. Jones; acknowledged Dec. 12, 1853, Elizabeth examined apart; $1 in lieu of stamp and recorded Feb. 15, 1854 (Henry M. Fitzhugh, Clerk). Margin: 'Delivered to Rev W. T. Johnston Rector of St Johns Church Huntingdon May 20 1870' (the initials are uncertain). What it settles: the second parcel of the Bowerman deed to Litzinger (A.W.B. 381/477, row 46151) went, course for course, to Abraham H. Bucher in 1853. It lies east of the Old York Road between St. John's acre on the south (A.W.B. 349/45) and Jacob Aull's 2 acres 29 perches of 1848 on the north (A.W.B. 409/275, row 46158). It is not between the two roads and is not 3011, 3013 or any Greenmount frontage: the old road separates it from the fork. The recorded deed was handed to the rector of St. John's in 1870, so the lot very probably passed to the parish by then (an inference: no deed from Bucher to the Vestry is read). Abraham H. Bucher (1814 to 1893) is buried in St. John's churchyard (row 18255); a George W. Bucher (1843 to 1921) is buried there too (row 18260), and whether he is Abraham's son and the George W. Bucher of 3313 is not shown. What it does not settle: how and when the lot reached the Vestry, and where it lies in today's St. John's ground (the parish held church, cemetery and rectory as separate pieces in 2023).

For $300 they grant, bargain and sell to Litzinger, his heirs and assigns, 'all their right title and interest claim and demand to a piece of land adjoining or belonging to a tract called "Ensors Inspection" (and embraced in a deed of trust from John McFadon to Jno. W. Stump and Philip G. Biays for the use of the first named parties and recorded in Liber W.G. No. 165 folio 492 land records Baltimore County) and lying between the old and New York roads. Beginning at a stone at the south west corner of a lot belonging to Wm. Baden and running parallel with the present York road forty yards, thence seventeen yards in an easterly direction to the old road thence thirty one yards along the old road to Badens Lot and from thence twenty six yards to the place of beginning. Containing about the one sixth of an acre more or less'. Signed Jno. W. Stump, S. Biays, J. Hoke, Ann B. Hoke, Henry Hammond, Fanny Hammond, Henry W. [sic] Bowerman, Elizabeth Bowerman, Walter T. Allender and Hannah J. Allender, before George W. King and Jesse Cloud, who took the acknowledgment the same day in Baltimore City, the four wives (the certificate calls the first 'Nancy B. Hoke') examined apart from their husbands; received to be recorded Dec. 22, 1841 at a quarter past 11 A.M. and recorded the same day (Thos. Kell, clerk); margin 'D. grantee 8th Oct 1842' (delivered, as read). Philip G. Biays, the co-trustee, is not a party, though he joined the 1844 Mumma deed (A.W.B. 354/374, row 46070). What it settles: (1) the deed recited in Litzinger's 1864 deed to John W. Treadway (G.H.C. 39/499, row 47383) is read, and it is the north piece of that lot. Its calls are 40 yards (120 ft) down the turnpike from Baden's south-west corner, 17 yards (51 ft) east to the old road, 31 yards (93 ft) up it (1864: N 20 1/2 E 95 ft) and 26 yards (78 ft) back along Baden's line (1864: N 61 W 82 ft). Laid on the 1864 courses, the line from 120 ft down the turnpike to the post where the old road bends (the end of the N 31 1/2 E 99 ft course) measures 51 ft 2 in and encloses about 6,880 sq ft (0.16 acre, against 'about the one sixth'); the other 94 ft of turnpike to the fork is the 1847 wedge (A.W.B. 381/477, row 46151), whose north line of 3 1/10 perches (51 ft 2 in) is this deed's 17-yard line. So this lot is the 'parcel ... now owned by the said Letzinger' at whose south-west corner the wedge begins, by measure as well as by the 1864 recital. (2) Stump's title is the McFadon deed of trust of April 11, 1822 (W.G. 165/492, row 46094) and nothing else is recited: the grantors are one of its two trustees, its life tenant, Sarah Biays, and the four Biays daughters who held the remainder, with their husbands; the same couples sold the wedge in 1847 after Stump's trustee's deed of 1845 (A.W.B. 359/136, row 46130). (3) The tract is named, but hedged: 'adjoining or belonging to' Ensor's Inspection. (4) By the City frontages (3015, 15 ft; 3017, 19 ft 2 in; 3019 and 3021, the 33-ft Aull lot of 1898; 3023, 28 ft; 3025, 33 ft; 128 ft 2 in in all, against 120) and the 1915 depths (46 ft 3 in at 3015 rising to 75 ft at 3025, against 51 ft at this lot's south line and about 75 ft square to the turnpike at Baden's line), this lot carries 3015 to 3025 and the wedge 3011 and 3013 (72 ft 4 in): an inference from the measures, good to about 8 ft. What it does not settle: whether the strip lies in Ensor's Inspection or in Huntington, whose leasehold of 1809 lay on the same strip north of Baden's lot (row 46153); how it came into McFadon's 1822 ground (no course or Moale lot is given; that it is the front of Moale's Lot 3 of 1819, sold 'subject to a County road' through its front, with buildings on the road let for 22 years (as read there) from May 26, 1819, W.G. 160/582, row 46129, is a lead, not shown); why Philip G. Biays did not join, which may explain the quitclaim form; the lessor and date of William Baden's lot, already there in 1841 (chapters 12 and 13); and what stood on the lot.

For $1 it releases to Zoll the leasehold created by the sub-lease of March 17, 1891, 'it being agreed at the time said sub lease was delivered that this release should be executed', as fully as if the mortgage had never been made. Corporate seal (incorporated 1882), signed by Henry Joesting, President, attested by S. Seevers; acknowledged March 26, 1891 by the association's attorney (Henry W. Fox, reading uncertain) before John J. Dunn, J.P.; recorded April 10, 1891 at 4:45 p.m. (Jas. Bond, Clerk), with the sub-lease and Zoll's mortgage. What it settles: (1) Hamilton had a second mortgage on the 79 ft lot, to the Waverly Building Association, dated October 19, 1889 and recorded in the City (J.B. 1263/413), after the 1888 annexation; (2) both of Hamilton's mortgagees released Zoll's 35 ft on the same day so that Zoll could mortgage it to the Loyola association, and both kept their liens on the rest of the lot and on the $175 sub-rent. What it does not settle: the sum of the 1889 mortgage, whether it was paid before 1895, and whether it is the mortgage that John T. Ensor, styled 'Assignee of Mortgage', foreclosed against Hamilton in 1895 (R.O. 1725/20; that title fits an assigned mortgage better than his own 1886 one, an inference). Update Oct. 16, 2026 (3117 batch 6): J.B. 1263/413 is read (742:mdlr-jb1263-413-hamilton-ensor-waverly-bldg-assn-mortgage-2080-1889): $2,080 on sixteen shares, on the 79 ft lot only, made a first mortgage by John T. Ensor's postponement of his 1886 mortgage, with an assent to a decree under Article 4, sections 692 to 704; it replaced Hamilton's 1885 association mortgage (W.M.I. 116/300), released the same day. It is probably the mortgage Ensor foreclosed as 'Assignee of Mortgage' in 1895 (inference; no assignment is noted on the folios).

Partial release of mortgage, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. Ensor of Baltimore County recites: 'Whereas Charles Hamilton and wife by deed of Mortgage dated April 21st 1886 and recorded among the mortgage records of Baltimore County in liber J.W.S. No. 121 folio 373 &c conveyed to the said John T Ensor together with another lot the lot of ground particularly described in a deed from Martin Kratt to the said Charles Hamilton dated July 2nd 1870 and recorded among the Land records of said County in liber E.H.A. No 67 folio 41 &c to secure the payment of One thousand dollars with interest'; and that Hamilton, by a sub-lease of March 17, 1891 'intended to be recorded simultaneously herewith', sub-leased Zoll the portion beginning 'at a post standing at the northwest corner of the whole lot conveyed by Tagart Trustee to George C H Coffield which point of beginning is on the east side of the York Turnpike Road about 416 feet northerly from the intersection of the York Turnpike and the Old York Road', S 2 W 35 ft, S 85 1/2 E 126 ft more or less to the Old York Road, and so on. Assignment of a leasehold, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 5313, folios 27 to 28 (MSA CE 168-5321; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 27 to 31, at 150 and 300 dpi). Bradenbaugh's deed of four lots (2741 W. Fairmount Avenue and others) to Charles L. Bradenbaugh, all recorded July 12, 1932; none is about 3030. Margin heading 'David McCoy &c Asst to Waverly Bldg Asso of Balto Co' (clerk's number 20), with the stamp note '1-50¢ US S Canld'. Dated July 8, 1932. David McCoy and Mary E. McCoy his wife, of Baltimore City, 'in consideration of the sum of five dollars and other valuable considerations', grant and convey to The Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County, a body corporate, the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue formerly the York Turnpike Road' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'Known as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue'. Title recital: 'BEING the same lot of ground which by Assignment dated the 20th day of December 1929 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber SCL No 5076 folio 70 was conveyed by Mary A J Aull to the said Grantors'. To hold 'for all the residue of the term of years yet to come and unexpired therein with the benefit of renewal forever subject to the payment of the annual rent of Sixty six($66.00)Dollars payable half yearly on the first days of June and December'; special warranty and further assurances. Signed David McCoy and Mary E. McCoy; witness Elisebeth H. Yearley; acknowledged July 8, 1932 before Elisebeth H. Yearley, notary; recorded July 12, 1932 at 2:20 P.M., Stephen C. Little, Clerk. What it settles: (1) the McCoys held the 1912 Aull leasehold, by the assignment of Mary A. J. Aull, Jacob H. Aull's widow (he died Oct. 12, 1921), of Dec. 20, 1929 (S.C.L. 5076/70); the Aulls had kept 3030 since Alice M. Chapman's assignment back to Jacob in 1916. (2) The rent on it was the 1912 rent, $66 due June 1 and Dec. 1, the same days as on 3028 (S.C.L. 3770/255), so the reversion was the one the Hooper trustees held; the Association held the 1912 leasehold from July 1932 and bought that reversion on Feb. 18, 1935, and the two merged in it [inference: no merger clause is read]. (3) The true cite of the assignment is S.C.L. 5313/27 (Grantor Index 1932, row 47520), not 5312/27 (row 47406). What it does not settle: why the McCoys assigned 3030 to a building association. No mortgage, debt or default is recited and no price is stated; the single 50-cent stamp points to a consideration of $500 or less [inference], far under the $1,932 the 1915 City roll put on the lot and house, which fits a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a building-association loan [inference, not read]. How Mary A. J. Aull held the leasehold (by Jacob's will or a deed from him) is not stated. Next: S.C.L. 5076/70 (MSA CE 168-5084) and the folios after it, where a McCoy purchase-money mortgage would be recorded. Update Oct. 16, 2026 (1929 and 1935 read): S.C.L. 5517/92 (MSA CE 168-5525, read; 726:mdlr-scl5517-92-hooper-trustees-waverly-bldg-redemption-3030-1935) is the deed of Feb. 18, 1935 by which Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore and William Jenkins, trustees under Francis X. Hooper's will, on the Waverly Building Association's statutory notice to redeem, conveyed it the 1912 $66 reversion on 3030 for $1,100, 'to the end and intent that the leasehold estate created by the lease aforesaid shall be merged with the fee'. So the trustees of the 1935 recitals are Hooper's, and the 1912 lease and rent on 3030 merged in the Association by that deed, not by inference. S.C.L. 5076/70 and /71 (MSA CE 168-5084, read) show how the leasehold reached the McCoys: Jacob H. Aull's executors deeded it to his widow Mary A. J. Aull on Oct. 11, 1922 (S.C.L. 3918/495, recited), she assigned it to David and Mary E. McCoy on Dec. 20, 1929, and they mortgaged it the same day to the Waverly Building Association for a $3,120 purchase-money advance on 24 shares, released only on Mar. 15, 1951 (M.L.P. 8386/69). Their 1932 assignment to that lender was very probably in lieu of foreclosure [inference].

Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber J.B. 1292, folios 384 to 386 (MSA CE 168-1300; read 2026-10-16 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 384 to 388, at 150 and 300 dpi). The scan also holds the end of H. Kent McCay, trustee, to Narcissa McCay, a lot on the west side of North Charles Street south of Eager Street (acknowledged in Jefferson County, Alabama, Apr. 28, 1890); the Mount Royal Land, Loan and Improvement Company of Baltimore County's release to Noble H. Creager of Erastus B. Tucker's mortgage (J.B. 1252/212), signed by Lennox Birckhead, president (May 13, 1890, 386 to 387); and Valentine and Anna Diller's assignment of a lot on Shuter Street to the Bohemian Permanent Building and Savings Association 'Slovanstvo' (May 14, 1890, 388). Entry 223. Made Apr. 26, 1890 'by John H. C. Legg to David Stewart both of Baltimore City'. For '$1100' (a raised mark follows the figure; $1,100 is the likely reading) Legg 'doth hereby grant assign and convey unto the said David Stewart All those five lots of ground lying in Baltimore City (formerly in Waverly Baltimore County)'. (1) The apex: from the corner of the north-east side of Merryman's Lane and the west side of the York Turnpike, 36 ft 1/2 in north 'to the centre of the division wall between the house on the lot now being described and the house on the adjoining lot on the North', west through the wall 42 ft in all to the lane, and south-east 55 ft on the lane, '(Being the lot the Leasehold in which vested in said Legg by a deed from David Stewart and the fee by a deed from Lucy C. George both deeds having been recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City on April 24th AD 1890)'. (2) On the south-west side of the lane from 7 ft 8 1/2 in north-west of the turnpike, 102 ft 6 in on the lane, 66 ft 7 in south and 78 ft 1 1/2 in east to the beginning: the lot David Stewart leased to Sarah C. Sinclair on May 28, 1887 (J.W.S. 160/403), 'subject to a ground rent of $80 redeemable after five years at six per cent payable March and September', assigned to Legg by Stewart. (3) On the west side of the turnpike from 96 ft 1/2 in north of the lane, 84 ft 11 1/2 in north, then west 'at right angles with said turnpike or nearly so bounding on the lot leased by said Legg to Drechsler' 100 ft to a three-foot alley, back down the alley and 100 ft east: '(For title see two deeds from David Stewart and wife to said Legg dated April 23rd 1890 and recorded prior hereto said deeds vesting this lot in said Legg in fee)'. (4) On the north-east side of the lane from 134 ft 7 in north-west of the turnpike, at the corner of a three-foot alley 100 ft west of the road, 72 ft 4 in on the lane, 63 ft 8 1/4 in north, 55 ft east to the alley and 110 ft 1 in down it, held in fee from Stewart. (5) On the south-west side of the lane west of the alley, 97 ft west 'to the Western outline of all Sinclair's original property', 75 ft 6 in north to the lane and about 125 ft back along it: 'the same lot intended to be leased by Robert Riddell Brown to James E. Sinclair by deed dated December 22nd 1887' (J.W.S. 167/165), 'subject to an annual rent of $50 payable December 22 and June 22 and redeemable after fifteen years at five percent'. 'It being intended to comprise in this deed all the property heretofore granted to said Legg by said David Stewart and wife and by Lucy C. George and husband by deeds recorded April 24th 1890 excepting the lot leased by said Legg to George T. Drechsler.' With the buildings; to Stewart 'absolutely subject however as to the leasehold lots to the aforesaid ground rents'; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Robert A. Thursby, J.P. for Baltimore City, before whom Legg acknowledged on Apr. 26, 1890; received for record May 14, 1890 at 9:55 a.m. and recorded the same day (Jas. Bond, Clerk); margin 'Grantee Nov 11 [?] 90'. What it settles: (a) the apex left Legg two days after he took it. Lot 1 is the apex, and both estates passed, the Sinclair leasehold from the foreclosure deed (J.B. 1289/297) and the fee carrying the $60 rent from the Georges (J.B. 1289/300), so from Apr. 26, 1890 David Stewart held the apex whole (that the lease merged is an inference; the deed does not use the word). (b) The five lots are foreclosure lots 1, 2, 4 and 6 and a third lot running from 96 ft 1/2 in to 181 ft north of the lane: foreclosure lot 3 (96 ft 1/2 in to 132 ft 8 in) joined to the three southern lots of the 1888 sub-lease (132 ft 8 in to 181 ft), which Legg held in fee and lease by the two Stewart deeds. Everything Legg took on Apr. 24 went back to Stewart except 3224, the lot leased to Drechsler, whose reversion Legg sold to Helen Stewart Ridgely (J.B. 1289/565); the round trip, Stewart to Legg on Apr. 23 and Legg back to Stewart on Apr. 26, shows Legg acting as Stewart's conveyancing intermediary, as was inferred on 3224. (c) The rent on lot 2, blotted in the foreclosure deed, is $80; lot 5 is under Brown's December 1887 lease at $50. (d) The deed names no mortgage: the 'Mortgage for $3,500 [?] to Alice Gerry Stewart' that the foreclosure deed laid on lots 1 to 4 is neither excepted nor released here (whether it was already satisfied is unsettled). What it does not settle: how David Stewart, holding the apex in fee from 1890, came to the Auxiliary Realty transfer of 1910 and the $120 lease the Samstags took in 1911; the Alice Gerry Stewart mortgage and its release; and the exact consideration. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (S.C.L. 2610/401 read): the next step is read (752:mdlr-scl2610-401-stewart-pangiris-auxiliary-five-lots-1910): David Stewart's title went to his wife Alice Gerry Stewart by a deed of Feb. 8, 1897 (R.O. 1661/69 [?], recited, not read), and on June 30, 1910 the Stewarts and Elizabeth Pangiris deeded the apex and four houses to the Auxiliary Realty Company, of which David Stewart was Treasurer. The 1910 deed names no mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart and conveys 'free and discharged of any ground rent or of any mortgage'. Update Oct. 17, 2026 (R.O. 1661, R.O. 1715 and S.C.L. 2610/548 read): the next step is read (752:mdlr-ro1661-69-david-stewart-alice-gerry-stewart-waverly-property-1897): on Feb. 8, 1897 David Stewart conveyed 'all his Waverly property' to his wife Alice Gerry Stewart, 'seven lots of ground five of which' are in this deed, the apex in fee, for $2,500 subject to an unrecorded $10,000 mortgage and equitable lien of May 1, 1890 to Annah St. Clair Gerry, dated five days after this deed was made.

Assignment of a sub-lease, Baltimore County land records, Liber E.H.A. No. 59, folios 471 to 473 (MSA CE 62-59; read 2026-10-16 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 471 to 475, at 150 and 300 dpi with the contrast raised). The scan pages hold, in order: the end of John Lee Carroll, Trustee's deed to Charles A. Gambrill and Richard G. and Patrick H. Macgill, acknowledged Nov. 21, 1868 and recorded here Dec. 2, 1868 after Howard County (top of 471); this assignment (471 to 473); Walter and Valaria Virginia Wilson's deed to Richard P. Pindell, Oct. 12, 1868, $1,500, ten acres of 'Gays Inspection' on the Harford Turnpike (473 to 474); and James A. and Mary G. Appold's deed to Andrew Appold, Oct. 14, 1868, $1,000, lots 45 and 46 of 'Friendship' on Matthews and Townsend Avenues (474 to 475); none of the others concerns 3117. The margin index heading reads 'John V. Smith', with a later mark above 'John' (perhaps 'Geo'). Dated October 14, 1868. 'George Vandyke Smith of Baltimore County', 'in consideration of the sum of Three hundred and twenty-five dollars', grants John W. Treadway, John Bruns and William Heise the lot on the east side of the York Turnpike Road 125 ft 6 in north of the beginning of the land 'assigned' (written over a struck word) by Samuel H. Tagart, trustee, to George C. H. Coffield (January 31, 1865, J.H.L. 43/548), by the 1868 courses: N 2 E 79 ft to a post at the north-west corner of the whole tract, S 85 1/2 E 140 ft 6 in to the Old York Road, S 19 1/2 W 78 ft 6 in, N 86 1/4 W 119 ft. Title: 'Being the same lot piece or parcel of ground which was leased or subleased to the said George Vandyke Smith by George C. H. Coffield by lease dated the second day of March in the year one thousand eight hundred and sixty eight and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore County in Liber E. H. A. No 59 folio 86 &c.', part of the parcel Tagart assigned to Coffield, and 'the same lot of ground which was leased for all the rest and residue save one year of the term of years yet to come' to Smith 'at the yearly rent of one hundred and fifty dollars payable in equal half yearly instalments accounting from the first day of March'. To hold for the remainder of the term 'by virtue of the original lease or assignment'. Smith covenants that he has the right to convey, special warranty and further assurances. What it does not settle: who Smith, Bruns and Heise were, what was built, and Cone's assignment (E.H.A. 63/71, not read).
