Baltimore County Circuit Court Land Records Index 1851-1874, vol. 2 (Ce-Fj), MSA CE 35-2, pages 62 to 64: the section for surnames beginning C with given names beginning J, in order of recording from February 19, 1869 to May 4, 1870 (read 2026-10-17 from the scan Jeff saved, at 150 and 300 dpi). Columns are date of record, surname, given name, course ('to' grantor, 'from' grantee), other party, instrument, and liber and folio; the index prints liber numbers only, with deeds, leases and assignments in one series (Nos. 60 to 66 here, E.H.A. by the recording dates) and mortgages and their releases and assignments in a lower-numbered series (Nos. 24, 26 and 32 to 36). There are five lines for Joseph M. Cone and no other Cone: (1) May 7, 1869, 'Cone, Joseph M &c, from John W Treadway &c, Deed, 62, 262'; (2) May 27, 1869, 'Cone, Joseph M, to Lanvale Bldg asso, Mort, 33, 77' (the association's name is a probable reading); (3) August 3, 1869, 'Cone, Joseph M, to Martin Kratt, Assgt, 63, 271'; (4) March 24, 1870, 'Cone, Joseph M, from Lanvale Bldg asso, Rel mtg, 36, 51' (with a tick mark after the folio); (5) March 24, 1870, 'Cone, Joseph M, to Harrison Bldg asso no 6, Mort, 36, 56'. Other Cones would sit under other given-name letters, which these pages do not cover. Also on the pages: June 22, 1869, 'Cross, John C, to Waverly Mutual Bldg asso, Mort, 33, 232' (very probably the John C. Cross whose wife Elenor took the 1874 Wilson lease beside Margaret Hamilton's, J.B. 86/483; inference); and February 18, 1870, 'Carlisle, James H, from Augustus D Clemens &wf, Deed, 65, 235' (an Augustus D. Clemens, not necessarily the Jr. who bought the 79 ft lot in 1898). What it settles: (1) line 1 confirms E.H.A. 62/262, read, recorded May 7, 1869; (2) line 3 gives the true place of Cone's assignment to Kratt: E.H.A. 63, folio 271, recorded August 3, 1869, a few days after the 'on or about July 30, 1869' of Kratt's 1870 recital, which gives folio 71 (a dropped '2'; the scan of 63/71 to 78, read, holds June 1869 deeds); it is indexed as an assignment, in the deed series; (3) Cone mortgaged something to the Lanvale building association twenty days after taking the 79 ft lot jointly with Kratt, had the mortgage released on March 24, 1870, and the same day mortgaged to the Harrison Building Association No. 6. What it does not settle: what Cone's two mortgages covered (the index gives no descriptions; that the May 1869 one was on his half of the 79 ft lot is possible, since its release in March 1870 came three months before Kratt sold the whole lot to Hamilton, but the same-day remortgage suggests other ground, inference either way), the price and terms of the assignment, and whether a wife joined (the index line shows no '&wf'). Update Oct. 17, 2026 (3117 E.H.A. 63/271 read): line 3 is read (E.H.A. 63/271 to 273; 742:mdlr-eha63-271-cone-kratt-half-79ft-leasehold-1869). Cone signs alone, for $50 and Kratt's payment of three notes given to Treadway and others, and covenants that he has not encumbered the lot, which suggests the Lanvale mortgage of line 2 was on other ground (inference).

Executors' deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. 3918, folios 495 to 496 (MSA CE 168-3926; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scan Jeff saved, folios 495 to 499, at 150 and 300 dpi). Folio 495 opens with the end of a deed by Marie L. Patterson (acknowledged Oct. 10, 1922 before Dorothea Jacob; recorded Oct. 13, 1922 at 9:30 A.M.); folios 497 to 499 hold Clinton J. and Helen Douty Ogle's assignment of 1644 N. Fulton Avenue to James Bernard and Catharine L. Griffin and the Griffins' $3,380 mortgage to the Rekab Building Association (recorded Oct. 13, 1922 at 9:10 A.M. and 2:51 P.M.), and the start of Charles Gensler's deed as trustee in bankruptcy of Amelia Puepke to Frances A. Milosh; none is about 3030. Margin heading 'Mary A J Aull &c Executors Deed to Mary A J Aull' (clerk's number 350), the typed note 'Block No 3656' beside the 3030 lot (the City block is 3856; very probably a typing slip [inference]) and 'New Annex' beside the second lot; grantee stamp 'Grantee T NOV 3 1922'. Dated Oct. 11, 1922. Mary A. J. Aull and W. Harry Holmes, 'Executors of the Estate of Jacob H Aull late of Baltimore City deceased', to Mary A. J. Aull. Recital: 'WHEREAS by an order of the Orphans Court of Baltimore City passed on the sixth day of October in the year one thousand nine hundred and twenty two in the matter of the estate of Jacob H Aull deceased the said Mary A J Aull and W Harry Holmes Executors were authorized and directed to convey unto the said Mary A J Aull the hereinafter described lots of ground in accordance with Article 93 Section 139 Code of Public General Laws of Maryland'. For $5 and under that order they convey 'all those two lots of ground'. First: the lot on the west side of 'Greenmount Avenue formerly the York Turnpike Road' 29 ft north of the north side of 'Vineyard Lane formerly Gilmor Lane', 14 by 82 ft to a 4-ft alley, between partition walls, 'Knonw as No 3030 Greenmount Avenue BEING the same lot of ground which by deed dated August 27th 1916 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber S C L No 3109 folio 328 &c was conveyed by Alice M Chapman to Jacob H Aull'. Second: on the north side of Rossiter Avenue 317 ft 5 in east of the east side of the York Turnpike Road, 63 ft 3 in along Rossiter Avenue to the westernmost outline of the first lot of a lease from Jacob H. Aull and wife to Alice M. Chapman of Nov. 2, 1910 (Balt. Co. W.P.C. 368/502), north 115 ft 9 in more or less to the northernmost outline of 'the whole tract of land belonging to said Jacob H Aull', N 87 50 W 59 ft more or less to lot No. 8 of a plat not otherwise named, and south 104 ft 10 in to the beginning, 'Known as No 510 Rossiter Avenue For reference See deed dated June 6th 1913 Balto Co W P C No 413 folio 446 &c'. For the residue of the terms with renewal forever, 'subject to the payment of the annual rent of $66.00 on the firstly described lot of ground payable in equal half yearly installments on the 1st days of June and December and ninety dollars on the secondly described lot of ground payable in equal half yearly installments on the first days of April and October'. Signed Mary A. J. Aull and W. Harry Holmes, Executors; witness Cora A. Du Laney; acknowledged Oct. 11, 1922 before Cora A. Du Laney, 'a Notary Public of the State of Maryland in and for Anne Arundel County', under a 'Baltimore City' venue heading; recording line typed 'October 11th 1922 at 2.51 o'clk PM', though the instruments on either side were recorded Oct. 13 and the Griffin mortgage at the same minute that day, so the date is very probably a slip for Oct. 13 [inference]. What it settles: (1) how the widow held 3030: Jacob H. Aull (d. Oct. 12, 1921) held the 1912 leasehold by Alice M. Chapman's assignment back of Aug. 27, 1916 (S.C.L. 3109/328, row 46607) until his death; his executors, his widow and W. Harry Holmes, conveyed it to her on Oct. 11, 1922 for $5 under an Orphans' Court of Baltimore City order of Oct. 6, 1922. With the 1912 lease, the 1916 assignment, the 1929 sale to the McCoys, their 1932 assignment and the 1935 merger, the 1912 leasehold on 3030 is now read link by link from 1912 to 1935. (2) The order covers only two lots: 3030, the one Aull house of the 1912 row still in his hands (3026 went to the Spellmans in 1917, 3028 and 3032 in 1918), and 510 Rossiter Avenue in the New Annex, the Aull home where he died, also a leasehold, at $90, out of his own tract and next to a 1910 lease to Chapman. No other corridor lot is named. What it does not settle: the will (the deed calls them executors but cites no will liber or folio) and the terms of the Oct. 6, 1922 order; whether Aull held other leaseholds or fees that passed by other instruments.

Grantee index lines, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Grantee Indexes 1908, 1909 and 1910, A to G volumes, the 'Au' pages (MSA CE 166-128 p.49 to 51, MSA CE 166-131 p.53 to 57 and MSA CE 166-134 p.53 to 56; read 2026-10-17 by a helper agent from the scans Jeff saved, at 150 and 300 dpi). Each year's pages run in recording order; 1908 p.51, 1909 p.56 and 1910 p.56 are blank, and 1909 p.57 begins 'Av'. On these pages the grantor and the right-hand columns run about half a line below the grantee, so lines were matched in order. There are 60 lines for 'Auxiliary Realty Co.' (9 in 1908, 27 in 1909, 24 in 1910), and the first is the first line of 1908 (Jan. 3, Edwin C. Conklin and wife, deed, N.E.S. Cathedral St, S.C.L. 2395/113), so the company was already buying when the 1908 volume opens (formed in 1907 or earlier, inference). Only one pair is on the York road, both recorded Sept. 30, 1910 (1910 p.54): 'Cityco Realty Co', 'Mtge', '5 Lots W S York Road', S.C.L. 2610 folio 403; and 'Alice G Stewart &c', 'Deed &c', '5 Lots W S York Road', S.C.L. 2610 (by ditto) folio 401. Other lines with Stewart, Gerry-family or corridor-chain names: Apr. 16, 1908, 'David Stewart Trustee', Deed, location 'S.C.L. 2409.138', S.C.L. 2416/60, the property of the Mar. 17, 1908 deed from 'Indiana Rehan &c' ('Real & Personal', S.C.L. 2409/138); Mar. 4, 1909, grantee 'Auxiliary Realty Co &c' from 'Mary A. Legg &c', Deed, 'E S Hargrove alley', S.C.L. 2484/52; Jan. 25, 1910, 'David Stewart', Deed, 'N S Preston St', S.C.L. 2556/16; Feb. 1, 1910, 'Elizabeth Pangoris' [Pangiris], Deed, 'S.W.S. Ostend St', S.C.L. 2557/431; Apr. 29, 1910, 'Real Estate Pooling Co', Asst, 'E S Charles St', S.C.L. 2576/326. No Gerry or Griswold line. The rest are deeds of single lots and rows across the city (Cathedral, Madison, Woodyear, Mount Royal, Calhoun, Lexington, Preston, Ostend, Division and other streets), mortgages and assignments of mortgages (several on 'Interest in Estate' from the Baugher family and the Hoods), and one partial release; none is on the York road, Greenmount or Merryman's Lane. No line in November or December 1910 is from Cityco Realty Co.: the Nov. 10, 1910 sale of 1100 and 1102 York road from Cityco back to Auxiliary that the Sun reported is not in the 1910 grantee pages (recorded in 1911, or under another name, inference). Deed, Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 2559, folios 393 to 395 (MSA CE 168-2567; read 2026-10-17 from the scan Jeff saved, folios 393 to 397, a faded high-contrast copy of a clerk's hand, at 110 to 450 dpi; the top of 393 is the end of the sisters' deed back to Frederick Fink, this deed opens at the foot of 393 under the index heading 'Frederick Fink &c Deed to Mary Catherine Fink &c' and ends on 395, and the rest of 395 to 397 is Mary K. Fink's mortgage to the Central Savings Bank, both filed as their own rows). Dated Feb. 9, 1910 (the numeral before 'th' prints like a 4 in this hand; the 1917 and 1919 recitals both read 'February 9th 1910', so the 9th is taken) and acknowledged the same day before William D. Gould, J.P.; recorded Feb. 10, 1910, about 1 P.M. (Stephen C. Little, Clerk). Frederick Fink and Pansy V. Fink his wife, of Baltimore City, for 'five dollars ($5.00) in hand paid', grant Mary Catherine Fink, Bertha Kiel wife of Samuel F. A. Kiel and Estella Fink, 'their heirs and assigns in fee simple all their right title and interest in and to all those four parcels of ground' in Baltimore City 'which are fully described in the deeds following'. First: the lot of the deed from Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens his wife to William L. Fink of April 18, 1898, Liber R.O. No. 1729 folio 241 (the 3013 lot, row 46109). Second: the lot of the deed from Eugenia D. Gabler and Louis H. Gabler her husband, Sarah Pennington, Edward W. Mumma and wife, David T. Mumma and wife and Margaret M. Matthews, Nov. 10, 1894, J.B. 1530/115. Third: the lot of the deed to William L. Fink from Matilda W. Sanger and Charles W. Sanger her husband of April 1897 (the liber and folio read like 'No. 1347, folio 44' and are not safe to cite). Fourth: the lot of the County deed from the Gablers, Sarah and Ross J. Pennington, the Mummas, Julia and Nathan A. Clowes and Margaret M. Matthews to William Louis (as read) Fink of Dec. 30, 1887, Baltimore County 'now City', Liber J.W.S. No. 167 folio 484. No courses are given for any of them; each is described by its deed. Recital: the four lots are 'part of the rest residue and remainder of the estate of which William L. Fink late of Baltimore City aforesaid deceased died seized and possessed', which he 'by his last will and testament dated the 2nd day of February in the year 1893 duly admitted to probate by the Orphans Court of Baltimore City ... and recorded in the office of the Register of Wills of the said City in Wills Liber S.R.M. No. 82 folio 278 &c gave bequeathed and devised unto his wife Louisa Fink for life or for such time as she continued to remain a widow and from and after her death or marriage whichever should first happen to his four children the said Mary Catherine Fink, Bertha Fink who since intermarried with the said Samuel F. A. Kiel, Frederick Fink and Estella Fink as tenants in common share and share alike per stirpes and not per capita', her tenancy ending 'by her death on the 26th day of July 1907' (the numerals as read; the year cannot be right, see below). To hold to the three sisters 'as tenants in common in fee simple'; special warranty and further assurances. Witness Wm. D. Gould; signed Frederick Fink and Pansy V. Fink (seals). What it settles: (1) The step from William L. Fink to the Kiels and Himmelmanns is a family succession, not a sale. Fink, grantee of the 14-ft lot in 1898, left the residue of his estate by will to his wife Louisa for life or widowhood and then to his four children, Mary Catherine, Bertha, Frederick and Estella, as tenants in common; the deed says he 'died seized and possessed' of the 1898 lot, so he died after April 18, 1898, and the deed reads the lot as part of the residue of a will made five years before he bought it. (2) On Feb. 9, 1910 Frederick and his wife conveyed all their interest in the four lots to his three sisters; the same day, in the deed that ends at the top of folio 393, the sisters released Frederick a lot their mother Louisa had bought in 1907 (row 720:mdlr-scl2559-392-mary-bertha-estella-to-frederick-fink-louisa-fink-lot-1910-negative): a division of the two estates between the brother and the sisters (an inference from the pair). Each sister held an undivided share of 3013 from then, probably a third (an inference: no shares are stated). (3) Louisa Fink was the mother of Frederick, Bertha and Estella only ('her three children'), so Mary Catherine was very probably William L. Fink's daughter by an earlier marriage (an inference). Mary K. Fink of the 1915 roll and of the 1919 recital is Mary Catherine Fink: the 1919 deed cites as 'Mary K Fink to Estella F Himmelmann' the 1917 deed that is signed Mary Catherine Fink. (4) The 1917 deed (row 720:mdlr-scl3126-290-mary-catherine-fink-himmelmann-3013-and-five-limond-place-lots-1917) names the first lot of this deed '3013 York Road (formerly 1005)' and puts the County deed of 1887 behind five Limond Place lots, not behind 3013. What it does not settle: William L. Fink's date of death and the will itself (Wills S.R.M. 82/278, not read); the year of Louisa Fink's death: the recital reads 1907, yet the other deed on folio 393 recites her buying a lot from Frank D. Watkins on Sept. 26, 1907, so she lived past July 1907 and a numeral is misread (probably 1908 or 1909, an inference); the second and third parcels (Matilda W. Sanger was the ground-rent owner of the 3201 Greenmount block and leased William L. Fink ground there in 1889, J.B. 1244/245, row 17768, so the third parcel may lie there, an inference); the 1914 deeds that divided the sisters' shares (S.C.L. 2883/370 and 371, recited in 1917, not read); and whether the will, made in 1893, reached a lot bought in 1898 as the deed assumes.

Deed (the tail only), Baltimore City Superior Court land records, Liber S.C.L. No. 2559, ending on folio 393 (MSA CE 168-2567; read 2026-10-17; only the last page, 393, is on the scan, and it opens in the middle of the description, so the heading, the price and the lot's courses are on folio 392 or earlier and are not seen). Mary Catherine Fink, Bertha Kiel and Samuel F. A. Kiel her husband, and Estella Fink grant Frederick Fink, in fee simple, 'all the right title and interest of the said grantors' in a lot that Louisa Fink took 'by virtue of two deeds', one from Charles J. Murphy of Jan. 26, 1907 (Liber R.O. 2305, folio 824, as read; the writer's 2 prints like a 4) and one from Frank D. Watkins, widower, of Sept. 26, 1907 (R.O. 2371, folio 290, as read), 'and title to which said lot of ground descended in fee simple on the death of the said Louisa Fink their mother intestate to her three children the said Frederick Fink, Bertha Kiel born Fink and Estella Fink as her only heirs at law and being also the same lot of ground in and to which the said Mary Catherine Fink acquired a one fourth right title and interest by virtue of a deed bearing even date herewith ... from the said Frederick Fink and Pansy V. C. Legg to David Stewart dated April 26th A D 1890 and recorded among the Land Records of Baltimore City in Liber J B No 1292 folio 384 &c one of which is particularly described in a Deed from Lucy C George and husband to David Stewart dated July 18th A D 1890 and recorded as aforesaid in Liber J B No 1303 folio 206 &c and the last of which is particularly described in a Deed from Milton Heathcote to David Stewart dated October 13th A D 1891 and recorded as aforesaid in Liber J B No 1363 folio 585 &c the lot described in the second mentioned Deed being the reversion in the lot fifthly described in the first mentioned Deed the lot at the southwest corner of Merrymans Lane and York Road being subject to an eighty dollar ground rent payable March and September and the Heathcote lot to a $150 ground rent payable December 11th and June 11th and the other lots being in fee', 'subject however as to said two lots to said ground rents subject also to the operation and effect of an unrecorded Mortgage and equitable lien made by David Stewart to Annah St. Clair Gerry to secure the payment of a note drawn by him in her favor for $10,000 dated May 1st 1890'. Ogle, Clerk). The Charles Street recitals also show Robert R. Brown as Stewart's conduit (Alice Gerry Patterson's leasehold to Brown and Brown's deed back to Stewart, both May 19, 1886, J.B. 1096/257; Brown to Stewart, Feb. 11, 1891, J.B. 1330/127). What it settles: (1) the apex went from David Stewart to his wife on Feb. 8, 1897: it is lot 1 of the five lots of Legg's deed (J.B. 1292/384), conveyed by that reference, so the 1910 recital 'R.O. 1661 fol 69' is confirmed. The deed does not single the apex out and gives no bounds. (2) The estate is fee simple: only two Waverly lots carry rents, the $80 lot at the south-west corner of the lane (reversion bought from the Georges on July 18, 1890) and the $150 'Heathcote lot', and 'the other lots' are 'in fee', so the apex stands free of the $60 Brown rent (which merged in Legg, inference). No mortgage to Alice Gerry Stewart herself is named. (5) Robert R. Brown, the apex's lessor of 1887, appears as Stewart's go-between in 1886 and 1891 too, so the 1887 sale and lease back was a Stewart pattern (inference). Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. A.A., folios 205 to 206 (MSA CE 66-76; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 205 to 208 of the volume; the deed opens at the foot of 205, below the end of an Etienne Zacharie, Anne, Philip and Jas. Waters indenture, runs onto 206, and Nathan Bowen to Solomon Bowen begins below it). Indenture of May 16, 1787 between John Gorsuch son of Thomas, of Baltimore County, and James Edwards of the same: for 50 pounds, Gorsuch sells Edwards in fee 'all that part of a tract or parcel of land called Ensors Inspection lying on the west of the main road that leads from Baltimore Town to George Hailes', beginning at a bounded black oak of Mrs. Achsah Carnan's and running with her land S 52 E 22 perches 'to the main road', up the road N 14 E 29 1/2 perches to a black oak marked with six notches, bounding on the road N 41 E 6 perches to a bounded red oak marked with six notches, N 81 1/2 W 39 perches to a forked white oak marked with six notches, S 50 W 4 perches till it intersects Carnan's line, and with it to the first black oak, 'five acres and one quarter of an acre more or less', with the improvements and appurtenances; covenant of warranty against Gorsuch and his heirs. Witnesses Hez. Waters and Jon. Rutter, who also witnessed Gorsuch's receipt for the 50 pounds on the same sheet; acknowledged May 16, 1787 before John Moale and Lyde Goodwin, justices of the peace, Elizabeth Gorsuch his wife privately examined and releasing her dower; received for record May 18, 1787 and recorded the same day (W. Gibson, Clerk). The five courses, walked from the black oak, enclose 5.21 acres with the closing line implicit (about 26 perches toward S 30 E) against the deed's 5 1/4 [arithmetic]. What it settles: (1) The index's 'Gorsuch John to Edwards James, Pt Ensors Inspection, A.A. 205' (1787) is the Speagle lot. The beginning oak, the S 52 E 22, N 14 E 29 1/2, N 41 E 6, N 81 1/2 W 39 and S 50 W 4 perch courses and the 5 1/4 acres are word for word those of Speigle, Speigle and Carter's 1778 deed to Gorsuch (W.G. C/19, row 47038), and of Joseph Ensor's 1767 deed to the Speigles before it (B P/470). The inference of the earlier row that A.A. 205 was the best candidate is now read. (2) Gorsuch held the lot nine years, 1778 to 1787, and sold it three months after Maidwell mortgaged him the adjoining nine acres (Feb. 26, 1787, row 46640): by May 1787 the ground south of Maidwell's was James Edwards's, not Gorsuch's. (3) Edwards then bought the neighbouring ground from Maidwell himself in 1801 and 1804 (rows below). (4) The road is 'the main road that leads from Baltimore Town to George Hailes', the line the York Turnpike followed from 1808. What it does not settle: (1) Where the lot went after Edwards. The 1801 Spear deeds and Biays's plat call a lot that 'formerly belonged to John Gorsuch' 'now the property of the said James Biays' (rows 46180, 46685, 46678), but Gorsuch still owned 3 acres of Ensor's Inspection in 1803 (the Harkin's Rest trust, row 46253), so that lot is probably a different one, and no Edwards to Biays deed before Nov. 3, 1804 is known (INFERRED). (2) Whether Edwards held the 5 1/4 acres together with Richard Dick's part of the road line (the 1804 Maidwell deed below calls another Edwards parcel). Next: the County grantor index under Edwards, James, 1787 to 1804 and 1805 on, for the sale of the 5 1/4 acres onward.

Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 66, folios 123 to 125 (MSA CE 66-116; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 123 to 126; the deed opens on 123 under the index heading 'James Maydwell Deed To James Edwards', below the end of a Walsh and Williamson lease, and ends on 125, where David Robinson's letter of attorney to Charles Halsey follows). Indenture of Mar. 25, 1801 between James Maydwell of Baltimore County, wheelwright, and James Edwards of the same place, merchant: for $875 Maydwell sells Edwards in fee 'all that part of a tract of land situate in Baltimore County called Ensors Inspection that is contained within the following metes and bounds': beginning at a white oak marked with three notches, 'the beginning of that part of said tract conveyed by Joseph Ensor to the said James Madwell by deed dated the seventh of July one thousand seven hundred and sixty eight', N 34 E 13 perches to a stake standing one foot north of a stone, S 80 E 24 1/2 perches to a stake, S 12 1/2 E 4 perches, S 82 1/2 E 12 perches to a stake 'in the south thirty five degrees west line of the said part conveyed by Joseph Ensor to said Madwell', then bounding on that line S 35 W 9 perches to the end of it, and on 'the given line of said part' to the beginning tree; 'two and a half acres of land', with the benefits and appurtenances. Warranty; Maydwell signed 'James Maydwell', witnesses John Moale and Josias Penington; receipt for $875 the same day; acknowledged Mar. 25, 1801 before Moale and Penington, Temperance his wife privately examined and releasing her dower; received for record Apr. 2, 1801 and recorded the same day (William Gibson, Clerk). The courses, walked from the oak, enclose 2.57 acres and close by a line of about 39 1/2 perches toward N 81 W, the direction of the N 80 1/2 W closing line of Maidwell's own nine acres [arithmetic]. What it settles: (1) Maidwell sold the south end of his nine acres, along the first line (13 of its 35 perches), the closing line and the S 35 W road line (9 of its 14), to James Edwards in March 1801 for $875, six months after he sold the north 2 1/4 acres to James Biays (W.G. 67/62, row 46277, dated Sept. 26, 1800 as recorded). (2) The deed names Ensor's 1768 deed to Maidwell by its date, so this is the same Maidwell as the 1768 grantee and the 1787 mortgagor; he is a wheelwright, Edwards a merchant. (3) The piece's S 80 E 24 1/2, S 12 1/2 E 4 and S 82 1/2 E 12 courses are the north line of the 1804 piece (next row). What it does not settle: how Edwards came by the 'other parcel' that the 1804 deed names, or whether this 2 1/2 acres touches the modern 2958 lot. Next: W.G. 82/206 (next row) and the Edwards to Biays deed of Nov. 3, 1804 (W.G. 83/371, row 46194) laid on this one.

Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 82, folios 206 to 208 (MSA CE 66-132; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 206 to 209; the deed opens at the foot of 206 under the index heading 'James Maydwell Deed To James Edwards', after an Anthony Kimmel to August Schwatke lease assignment, and ends on 208, where Henry S. Keatinge to Robert Walsh follows). Indenture of Sept. 11, 1804 between James Maidwell of Baltimore County and James Edwards of the same: for $2,000, Maidwell sells Edwards in fee 'all that part of a tract of land called Ensors inspection situate in Baltimore County which is contained within the following metes and bounds': beginning at a stone marked J B 'standing on the west side and near to the York Turnpike road at the south east corner of a part of said tract conveyed by said James Maidwell to James Biays', S 84 W 34 perches along that part to another stone marked J B, S 34 W 8 1/2 perches 'to the north west corner of a part of said tract heretofore sold by said James Maidwell to said James Edwards' (the 2 1/2 acres of Mar. 25, 1801), then bounding on it S 80 E 24 1/2 perches, S 12 1/2 E 4 perches (the words 'and a half perch still bounding on said Edwards part south twelve and a half east four perches' interlined between the 22nd and 23rd lines of the first page) and S 82 1/2 E 12 perches 'until it intersects the out line of another parcel of land belonging to said James Edwards', and thence on that line to the beginning; 'three acres of land more or less together with all and singular the buildings and improvements thereon'. Warranty; the name of Charles A. Pindell stands under the note of the interlineation; acknowledged Sept. 11, 1804 before two justices, Temperance his wife privately examined and releasing her dower (the justices' names at the foot are Rob. Gorsuch and Geo. Gouldsmith Presbury); received for record Sept. 15, 1804 and recorded the same day (William Gibson, Clerk). The courses, walked from the J B stone, enclose 2.98 acres with the east side implicit [arithmetic]. What it settles: (1) Maidwell's nine acres were divided among Biays (the north 2 1/4 acres, 1800), Edwards (the south 2 1/2 acres, 1801) and Edwards again (the middle 3 acres, 1804), so by Sept. 15, 1804 Edwards held about 5 1/2 of the nine acres (2.57 and 2.98 computed) and Maidwell at most the remainder, about an acre on the deed's nine or half an acre on the computed 8.17 (INFERRED). (2) The 3 acres carry 'buildings and improvements' and sold for $2,000, against $875 for the 2 1/2 acres of 1801, whose deed names none: the buildings stood on this middle piece (INFERRED from the price and the words). (3) On Sept. 11, 1804 Edwards already owned 'another parcel of land' on the east of this piece, along the road: Richard Dick's part, 'now owned by the said James Edwards' in Edwards's deed to Biays of Nov. 3, 1804 (W.G. 83/371, row 46194), is the likely parcel (INFERRED; neither deed names the vendor). (4) The J B stones, James Biays's, at the south-east corner of his 2 1/4 acres and on its south line fix where Biays's ground ends. What it does not settle: when and from whom Edwards bought Dick's part, which of the three pieces is the ground of 2958 or its neighbours, and how the 5 1/4 acres of A.A. 205 (row above) lie against these. Next: the County grantor index under Edwards, 1804 to 1805; the Dick grantee entries in 1770 to 1786 (CE 32-2, Di) for the deed to Edwards.

Lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber E.H.A. 74, folios 235 to 237 (MSA CE 62-74; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 233 to 237; pp. 233 and 234 are the end of the previous instrument and were not read). Index heading 'David S. Wilson &c Trustees, Lease to John H. Hartman & wf' (margin: 'delivered March 31/77 per Rec't'). Lease made Feb. 27, 1872 between David S. Wilson, Thomas J. Wilson and Henry R. Wilson, trustees under the last will and testament of James Wilson late of Baltimore City, deceased, 'which will bears date the twenty second day of January A.D. 1848, has been duly proven and is now of record in the office of the Register of Wills for Baltimore City', and John H. Hartman and Catharine his wife, of Baltimore County. The trustees, 'acting under the powers conferred on them by said Will', for $700 and the rent reserved lease 'all that lot of ground situate in Baltimore County aforesaid (near to and north of the first toll gate at Waverly on which the Stone House stands which is now occupied by said Hartman' and which is thus described: beginning at a point on the York Turnpike Road where a line drawn along the north wall of the Stone House intersects the west side of the road, west reversing that line 200 ft, south parallel with the road 50 ft, east parallel with the first line 200 ft, and north along the westernmost side of the road 50 ft to the beginning; the trustees may, if they wish, use the westernmost ten feet of the lot to open an alley. With the improvements. Term 99 years from the day before the date, at $100 a year from May 1 (the year reads 18 and a word that looks like 'twenty'; 1872 is the only fit, INFERRED) in half-yearly instalments on Nov. 1 and May 1; distress for arrears; re-entry after 60 days (a second clause says six months' arrears allow the trustees to renew and annul the lease, so the two clauses disagree on the period, as they appear on the page); renewable forever on the lessees' request and proper cost; and the trustees will at any time 'on or before the first day of May A.D. 1875' on payment of $1,666.66 over and above the rent in arrear and the accruing rent, convey the lot in fee simple free of rent. H. Ady, Clk.). What it settles: (1) The lot just north of Pendleton's Lot 8 is a 50 ft by 200 ft lot with a stone house, leased to Hartman in February 1872 at $100 a year, redeemable for the capitalisation at 6 percent ($1,666.66) until May 1, 1875; it fits the plate of 1889 (J. H. Hartman 50 ft, 2 S. and attic stone dwelling, 375 ft south of Wilson Street, p. 147) in width, in the stone house and in position; the plate gives 190 ft deep against the lease's 200. (2) The trustees recite that the will was 'of record in the office of the Register of Wills for Baltimore City' and that they act under its powers, with no liber; the paper's two citations of the same will (D.M.P. 24/154 and N.H. 26/354) are therefore not settled by this deed. (3) The lease does not cite the Wilson plat, a lot number or Wilson Street: the lot is described from the stone house's north wall, so it does not restate the measurements from Wilson Street that the Pendleton deed gives (E.H.A. 72/153). What it does not settle: where Wilson Street and the lanes fall against 3224; whether Hartman bought the fee before 1875; why 'the first toll gate' is the reference (the Gate House lot of 1871 is at Gilmor Lane, far south, so the phrase may mean a gate near Wilson Street or loosely the toll-gate district, INFERRED either way). Next: the Wilson sales plat (the Circuit Court equity papers); a deed of the fee to Hartman, 1872 to 1875.

Index pages, Baltimore County Court Grantor Index A-Z, 1829 to 1832 (MSA CE 33-10): pp. 437 to 441, the 'Pa' surnames (1829 to 1832), and p. 644, 'Yo' (1829 to 1832); read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scans Jeff saved. The question is Frederick Parks's administrators' assignment of the fork lot to John Litzinger on Apr. 7, 1831, which Litzinger's 1834 deed (T.K. 237/457, rows 46247 and 46248) cites with no liber. The 'Pa' pages hold no Frederick Parks and no administrators: the Parks lines are Ruth Parks, guardian of Mary Ann Jarman, to Charles Grover (1830, W.G. 203/66), Abraham Parks, a surrender of a lot on Gough Street (205/69) and Peter Parks, a mortgage to Wm. Bosley of part of John's Forest and Merriman's Adventure (1829, W.G. 201/455, the number is carried by ditto marks), none of them Huntington. The deed is on p. 644 under the first-named administrator, in the 1831 group: 'Young, McClintock &c., admrs of Fredk. Parks' to 'John Litzinger', 'Asst' (assignment), 'Pt of Huntington', W.G. 210, folio 583. Confidence: grantor, grantee, instrument and 'Pt of Huntington' high; the liber and folio 210/583 medium-high (the folio's last digit could be 5 or 8; the index's own neighbours, 209/305 above and 210/636 below, support 583). The same line group has 'Young, McClintock &c, trustee of Peter Diven &c' to Patrick J. Diven, a Jones Street lot (210/636), which is a different matter. What it settles: (1) The assignment is indexed as W.G. 210/583, so MSA CE 66-260 (liber plus 50), page 583, is the deed Litzinger's 1834 deed leaves without a liber; it is a conveyance of part of Huntington by Frederick Parks's administrators, McClintock Young and James Buchanan (the index prints 'Young, McClintock &c'). (2) Parks's administrators are filed under Young, so an index search under Parks never finds it, the reason the 'Pa' run was blank. (3) The 'Pt of Huntington' puts the fork lot on Huntington and not on Ensor's Inspection, as the paper reads it (the lot between the roads, W.G. 54/156, the Gough 1798 Brown lease). What it does not settle: the deed's courses and parties' wording; Parks's own title (the 1798 Brown lease, Brown's assignment of 1801 or a later one); whether the figures are 210/583 or 210/588. Next: W.G. 210/583 itself (MSA CE 66-260, pp. 583 to 587) for the lot and the recitals of Parks's title.

Deed, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 69, folios 163 to 164 (MSA CE 66-119; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 163 to 166; the deed opens at the FOOT of 163, under the index heading 'James Barry Deed To James Edwards and Andrew Van Bibber', below the end of Edward Hall Spicer's deed to Amos Scott, and ends on 164, where William Asquith's lease to Samuel French follows). Indenture of April 13, 1801 between James Barry 'of the Territory of Columbia' and James Edwards and Abraham Van Bibber of Baltimore County (the index heading writes Andrew): for 'one Cent' Barry sells them, 'as Tenants in common but not as Joint Tenants', all that piece or parcel of ground in Baltimore County: 'Beginning at a Stone set up in the first line of Merryman's lot for a Corner between Merryman and Hall and running thence with said line South forty Degrees West two poles fifteen Links, then North forty nine and three quarters degrees West Eleven poles fifteen Links, thence North forty degrees East two poles fifteen Links, thence with a straight line to the Beginning containing thirty Square perches of Ground more or less', with all of Barry's right, title, interest, property, claim and demand. Signed James Barry; witness Owen Dorsey; acknowledged April 13, 1801 before Owen Dorsey and Geo. Gould Presbury, justices of the peace; received for record Oct. 12, 1801 and recorded and examined the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk); a pencil '30' stands in the margin. Arithmetic (a link is 1/25 of a pole): 2 poles 15 links is 2.6 perches (42.9 ft) and 11 poles 15 links is 11.6 perches (191.4 ft); a figure with sides of those two lengths (the first and third calls are parallel, 2.6 by 11.6 perches) holds 30.2 square perches (about 8,200 square feet, 0.19 acre), which is the deed's thirty [arithmetic]. Assignment of a lease, Baltimore County Court land records, Liber W.G. 148, folios 693 to 695 (MSA CE 66-198; read Oct. 17, 2026 by the main session from the scan Jeff saved, pp. 693 to 696; the deed opens at the foot of 693, under the index heading 'Joseph Eaverson admr of Thomas Eaverson Assignment To George Tharp', below the end of Isaac Gardner's deed to Moses Wells, and ends at the top of 695, where Philip Gore's deed to William Gore follows). Indenture of Jan. 15, 1819 between Joseph Eaverson, administrator of the goods, chattels, rights and credits of Thomas Eaverson of Baltimore County, deceased, and George Tharp of the City of Baltimore. It recites that Thomas Eaverson in his life and at his death was possessed of 'a lot or piece of ground part of a tract of land called Huntington situate in Baltimore County near Christopher Walkers. Beginning for the same at the intersection of the York turnpike road (agreeable to Bakers survey) and the road leading to Mr. Vanbibbers Mill and running up the said York road ten perches thence running square with the said York road down to a road leading to said Vanbibbers Mill', for the residue of the term of years 'originally leased'; that letters of administration were granted to Joseph Eaverson; and that at an orphan court held at the City of Baltimore 'some time the year 1815' it was ordered that he set up and expose to public sale the leasehold estate; he did so, 'subject to the payment of the yearly rent therein contained to such person or persons legally authorized to receive the same on the days and times mentioned in the original lease', and George Tharp was the highest bidder at 'one thousand and one dollars'. For that sum Eaverson assigns Tharp, his executors, administrators and assigns, the lot, the buildings and all the term of years yet to come in the original lease, subject to the yearly rent in the original lease. Signed Joseph Eaverson; witness Geo. Gould Presbury; acknowledged Jan. 15, 1819 before Presbury and Rob. Gorsuch, justices of the peace; received for record Feb. 16, 1819 and recorded the same day (Wm. Gibson, Clerk). What it settles: (1) The leasehold of the fork lot began, in this chain, with Thomas Eaverson, who died before about 1815; his administrator sold it by court order (Baltimore County Orphans' Court, about 1815) and George Tharp bought it, taking the assignment on Jan. 15, 1819 (the sale and the assignment are four years apart; the deed does not say why). (2) So the chain of the lot is now: Thomas Eaverson (lessee) to Joseph Eaverson, administrator, to Tharp (W.G. 148/693, 1819, $1,001) to Edward Jenkins (W.G. 175/449, Jan. 25, 1825, $700; mortgage W.G. 167/456, 1823) to Frederick Parks (W.G. 176/711, Mar. 28, 1825, $500) to his administrators and John Litzinger (W.G. 210/583, Apr. 7, 1831, $426). The price fell from $1,001 to $426 over twelve years; the assignments say nothing about improvements. What it does not settle: (1) The ORIGINAL LEASE: its lessor, date and rent are not named here (nor in the 1823, 1825 and 1831 papers), so the lessor of the fork lot's lease is still unknown; the Orphans' Court sale proceedings of about 1815 (Archives, not on MDLandRec) may name it. (2) Which side of the turnpike the lot lies on (the call is 'up the said York road'; not shown). (3) Which road is meant: 'the road leading to Mr. Vanbibbers Mill' is the road the 1802 deeds call the road to Van Bibber's Mill (the later Merryman's Lane, INFERRED).
